facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In August 1940, the first pedestrians could use the bridge, provided they still had to walk on planks for the last part (between the bridge deck and the headland, so above sand). At the same time, Hildo Kropp was still busy carving images out of Norwegian granite.

features.opening: Joep Langebrug (bridge 417) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid.

features.name: Theo Fransmanbrug

facts.text: A hydraulically powered bascule section allows the middle of this eighty-meter span to lift.
facts.sourceQuote: Hij kwam met een uit drie delen bestaande overspanning, waarvan de middelste beweegbaar is uitgevoerd. Dat middenstuk is een hydraulisch aangedreven basculebrug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It came with a three-part span, the middle of which is moveable. That central section is a hydraulically powered bascule bridge.

facts.text: Green timber framing gives the structure the appearance of a Bailey bridge despite its concrete pillars.
facts.sourceQuote: De overspanning wordt gedragen door betonnen krammen (pijlers met jukken). Het geheel kreeg door het groene vakwerk, dat tevens tot leuning dient, het uiterlijk van een Baileybrug, maar dan met versieringen, met name het midden en westelijk deel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The span is supported by concrete frames (pillars with braces). The whole structure took on the appearance of a Bailey bridge due to the green timber framing, which also serves as a railing, but with decorations, especially the center and western part.

facts.text: Theo Fransmanbrug honors Theo Fransman, the first district chairman who enabled NDSM site development.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug is vernoemd naar Theo Fransman, de eerste stadsdeelvoorzitter van Amsterdam-Noord (tussen 1981 en 1990) die veel gedaan heeft om de ontwikkeling rondom het NDSM-terrein mogelijk te maken na het sluiten van de werf.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge is named after Theo Fransman, the first district chairman of Amsterdam-North (between 1981 and 1990) who did a lot to make the development around the NDSM site possible after the shipyard closed.

facts.text: The spans were hoisted into place by crane in May or June 2013 before opening on August 30.
facts.sourceQuote: De overspanningen werden in mei/juni 2013 door een hijskraan op hun plaats gehesen. De brug werd op 30 augustus 2013, inclusief naamplaat, in gebruik genomen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The spans were hoisted back into place by a crane in May/June 2013. The bridge was put into use on August 30, 2013, including nameplate.

features.opening: The Theo Fransmanbrug (bridge number 1788) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-North.

features.name: Oude Lijn

facts.text: The oldest section opened in 1839, running directly from Amsterdam to Haarlem.
facts.sourceQuote: The oldest section, opened in 1839, ran from Amsterdam to Haarlem.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The oldest section, opened in 1839, ran from Amsterdam to Haarlem.

facts.text: Track doubling was finally completed on August 2, 2024, ending a long delay.
facts.sourceQuote: On 2 August 2024 the doubling of the tracks was completed after a long delay.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On 2 August 2024 the doubling of the tracks was completed after a long delay.

facts.text: A new tunnel and station in Delft opened in March 2015 to underpass the old viaduct.
facts.sourceQuote: In March 2015 a new tunnel and station were opened in Delft, underpassing the former railway station and viaduct.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In March 2015 a new tunnel and station were opened in Delft, underpassing the former railway station and viaduct.

facts.text: The railway is called Oude Lijn, which translates to "old line" in Dutch.
facts.sourceQuote: The railway from Amsterdam through Haarlem to Rotterdam (also: Oude Lijn, Dutch for "old line") runs from Amsterdam Centraal to Rotterdam Centraal through Haarlem and The Hague.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The railway from Amsterdam through Haarlem to Rotterdam (also: Oude Lijn, Dutch for "old line") runs from Amsterdam Centraal to Rotterdam Centraal through Haarlem and The Hague.

facts.text: Since December 2011, direct trains have served the route from Amsterdam to The Hague.
facts.sourceQuote: From December 2011 it is used by all direct trains from Amsterdam to The Hague, and all direct supplement-free trains from Amsterdam to Rotterdam except those through Woerden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From December 2011 it is used by all direct trains from Amsterdam to The Hague, and all direct supplement-free trains from Amsterdam to Rotterdam except those through Woerden.

features.opening: The railway from Amsterdam through Haarlem to Rotterdam (also: Oude Lijn, Dutch for "old line") runs from Amsterdam Centraal to Rotterdam Centraal through…

features.name: Gooilijn

facts.text: The railway opened in 1874 with the Amersfoort–Zutphen section following two years later.
facts.sourceQuote: The railway between Amsterdam and Amersfoort was opened by the Hollandsche IJzeren Spoorweg-Maatschappij in 1874 with the Amersfoort–Zutphen section opening in 1876.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The railway between Amsterdam and Amersfoort was opened by the Hollandsche IJzeren Spoorweg-Maatschappij in 1874 with the Amersfoort–Zutphen section opening in 1876.

facts.text: The section between Amsterdam and Amersfoort is called Gooilijn because it runs through the Gooi region.
facts.sourceQuote: It is also informally called the Oosterspoorweg (English: Eastern railway), with the part between Amsterdam and Amersfoort sometimes being called the Gooilijn (Gooi line) because of the region it runs through.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is also informally called the Oosterspoorweg (English: Eastern railway), with the part between Amsterdam and Amersfoort sometimes being called the Gooilijn (Gooi line) because of the region it runs through.

features.opening: The Amsterdam–Zutphen railway is a railway line in the Netherlands running from Amsterdam, North Holland to Zutphen, Gelderland via the province of Utrecht.

features.name: M. Justbrug

facts.text: Green-gray granite rubble clads the wide landheads of this structure designed by Peter Pennink.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug is ontworpen door Peter Pennink, destijds in dienst dan wel werkend voor de Dienst der Publieke Werken. Hij paste als bekleding van de brede landhoofden groengrijze gneis breuksteen toe.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was designed by Peter Pennink, then employed or working for the Department of Public Works. He used green-gray granite rubble as cladding for the wide landheads.

features.opening: The M. Justbrug (bridge 803) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid.

features.name: Singelgrachtbrug

facts.text: A new lift bridge opened on July 2, 1923 next to the existing swing bridge.
facts.sourceQuote: Om voldoende capaciteit op het spoor te krijgen werd er eerst op 2 juli 1923 naast de bestaande draaibrug een nieuwe grotere, hogere ophaalbrug in gebruikgenomen (inclusief een nieuw spoorwegviaduct tussen deze brug en Amsterdam Centraal) (de onderdelen van deze brug waren in Duitsland gefabriceerd).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In order to obtain sufficient capacity on the tracks, a new larger, higher hoist bridge was first put into use on July 2, 1923 next to the existing swing bridge (including a new railway viaduct between this bridge and Amsterdam Central) (the parts of this bridge were manufactured in Germany).

facts.text: Engineers David Adriaan van Heijst and Pieter Joosting designed these large bridges.
facts.sourceQuote: Het ontwerp van die relatief grote bruggen kwam van Rijkswaterstaat uit de pen van ingenieurs David Adriaan van Heijst (1879-1966, zoon van schrijver David François van Heijst) en Pieter Joosting (bekend van De Hef).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design of those relatively large bridges came from Rijkswaterstaat from the pen of engineers David Adriaan van Heijst (1879-1966, son of writer David François van Heijst) and Pieter Joosting (known from De Hef).

facts.text: Three distinct lines connect Central Station to Haarlem, Zaandam, and Schiphol here.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug ligt in de drie spoorlijnen tussen de stations Amsterdam Centraal Station en Station Amsterdam Sloterdijk, de lijnen: Amsterdam - Haarlem; Amsterdam - Zaandam; Amsterdam Centraal - Schiphol.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge is located in the three railway lines between the stations Amsterdam Central Station and Amsterdam Sloterdijk, the lines: Amsterdam - Haarlem; Amsterdam - Zaandam; Amsterdam Central - Schiphol.

features.opening: The Houtmanspoorbrug, colloquially known as the Singelgrachtbrug, is a system of lift bridges in Amsterdam-Centrum, near the Spaarndammerbuurt district.

features.name: Zeilbrug

facts.text: Official records sometimes list the structure as Zeilstraatbrug rather than Zeilbrug.
facts.sourceQuote: Evenwel is in de Basisadministratie Adressen en Gebouwen de brug vermeld als Zeilstraatbrug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, in the Basic Addresses and Buildings Administration, the bridge is listed as Zeilstraatbrug.

facts.text: Municipal documents historically referred to this span only by its number, bridge 348.
facts.sourceQuote: Diverse documenten van de gemeente Amsterdam vermeldden alleen brug 348; Zeilbrug was kennelijk geen officiële benaming.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Various documents from the municipality of Amsterdam only mentioned bridge 348; Zeilbrug was apparently not an official name.

facts.text: Piet Kramer designed the Zeilbrug in Amsterdam School style using brick, stone, and wrought iron.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug werd ontworpen in de Amsterdamse Schoolstijl door de architect Piet Kramer en de ingenieur Wichert Arend de Graaf van de Dienst der Publieke Werken van de gemeente Amsterdam. Een mengeling van baksteen en natuursteen en siersmeedijzeren balustrades kwam uit Kramers per.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was designed in the Amsterdam School style by the architect Piet Kramer and the engineer Wichert Arend de Graaf of the Department of Public Works of the municipality of Amsterdam. A mixture of brick and natural stone and wrought iron balustrades came from Kramers per.

facts.text: Granite sculptures of fishermen, ships, and seal heads by Hildo Krop adorn the Zeilbrug.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook granieten beeldhouwwerken aan de brug, met vissers, schepen en koppen van zeerobben, in ontwerpen van Hildo Krop ontbreken hier niet.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Granite sculptures on the bridge, with fishermen, ships and heads of seals, in designs by Hildo Krop are also not missing here.

facts.text: Tram line 1 crossed the Zeilbrug starting in 1929 before line 2 took over in 1948.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 1929 reed tramlijn 1 over de brug. In 1948 kwam lijn 2 daarvoor in de plaats.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1929, tram line 1 has been running over the bridge. In 1948, line 2 took its place for this purpose.

features.opening: The Zeilbrug or Zeilstraatbrug (bridge no. 348) is a bridge over the Schinkel in Amsterdam.

features.name: Armand Sunierbrug

facts.text: The municipality took over management in 1952 after the bridge had been administered as P-83.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug was in de administratie bekend als P-83 hetgeen inhield dat de brug weliswaar in Amsterdam lag, maar niet in beheer was bij de gemeente. Dat werd anders in 1952; de brug moest vernieuwd worden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was known in the administration as P-83, which meant that while the bridge was located in Amsterdam, it was not under the management of the municipality. That changed in 1952; the bridge had to be renovated.

features.opening: Armand Sunierbrug (bridge 327) is the name of a swing bridge in Amsterdam.

features.name: Entrepotdok

facts.text: Until 1895, goods stored here avoided import duties until released to the market.
facts.sourceQuote: Until 1895, goods could be stored temporarily in this warehouse without having to pay import duties (a type of bonded warehouse). They only had to pay duty when the goods were put on the market.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 1895, goods could be stored temporarily in this warehouse without having to pay import duties (a type of bonded warehouse). They only had to pay duty when the goods were put on the market.

facts.text: The complex features 84 monumental warehouses built between 1708 and 1829.
facts.sourceQuote: The Entrepotdok has 84 monumental warehouses. They were built between 1708 and 1829.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Entrepotdok has 84 monumental warehouses. They were built between 1708 and 1829.

facts.text: Around 1890, the dock lost its warehouse function after a new facility opened nearby.
facts.sourceQuote: The dock lost its function as a warehouse for undeclared goods around 1890 due to construction of the Nieuwe Entrepotdok on the Cruquiusweg, and the buildings were empty for a long time.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The dock lost its function as a warehouse for undeclared goods around 1890 due to construction of the Nieuwe Entrepotdok on the Cruquiusweg, and the buildings were empty for a long time.

facts.text: The name Entrepotdok translates to Warehouse Dock.
facts.sourceQuote: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name along the northeast side of the canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name along the northeast side of the canal.

facts.text: Construction of these warehouses spanned from 1708 until 1829 across two centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.

facts.text: Squatters occupied the complex during the 1990s before it became residential apartments.
facts.sourceQuote: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.

features.opening: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name…

features.name: Grimnessesluis

facts.text: The original vaulted bridge vanished around 1868, forcing the current structure to shift ten meters forward.
facts.sourceQuote: Toen dat water een paar jaar later werd gedempt, was het Rokin versmald en werd de oude brug overbodig. Rond 1868 verdween de oude brug, zodat in praktijk de brug 10 meter opgeschoven was.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When that water was dammed a few years later, the Rokin narrowed and the old bridge became unnecessary. Around 1868, the old bridge disappeared, so in practice the bridge was moved 10 meters forward.

facts.text: Grimnessesluis is the sole survivor of a historic trio of bridges that once stood at this intersection.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug maakte toen onderdeel uit van een drietal bruggen op de kruising Grimburgwal, Rokin en Spui. De Grimnessesluis is de enige die daarvan nog over is.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was then part of a trio of bridges at the intersection of Grimburgwal, Rokin and Spui. The Grimnessesluis is the only one left of those.

features.opening: The Grimnessesluis (bridge 202) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Kees Fensbrug

facts.text: Kees Fensbrug received its name in 2009 after literary critic Kees Fens watched from his nearby house.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2009 werd de brug vernoemd naar literatuurcriticus Kees Fens, die vanuit zijn huis uitkeek op de brug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2009, the bridge was named after literary critic Kees Fens, who looked out over the bridge from his house.

features.opening: The Kees Fensbrug (bridge number 49) is a permanent viaduct bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Planciusspoorbrug

facts.text: Tram overhead wires were frequently damaged by trucks that were too tall to pass underneath safely.
facts.sourceQuote: Regelmatig werd de bovenleiding van de tram door te hoge vrachtwagens vernield.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The overhead wires of the tram were regularly damaged by too high trucks.

facts.text: Planciusspoorbrug spans Planciusstraat, both named after Petrus Plancius.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug overspant de noordzuid lopende Planciusstraat, haar directe naamgever, beide zijn vernoemd naar Petrus Plancius.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge spans the north-south running Planciusstraat, its direct namesake, both are named after Petrus Plancius.

facts.text: Until November 2017, the structure was known as S6 and S7 railway bridges.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot november 2017 stond de brug bekend als S6 en S7 (spoorbrug 6 en 7). In die maand ver/hernoemde de gemeente Amsterdam alle spoorbruggen in de stad voor opname in het Basisregistraties Adressen en Gebouwen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until November 2017, the bridge was known as S6 and S7 (rail bridge 6 and 7). In that month, the municipality of Amsterdam renamed all railway bridges in the city for inclusion in the Basic Addresses and Buildings Register.

facts.text: The viaduct carries three distinct lines connecting Amsterdam Central to Sloterdijk.
facts.sourceQuote: Het viaduct ligt in de drie spoorlijnen tussen de stations Amsterdam Centraal Station en Station Amsterdam Sloterdijk, de lijnen: Amsterdam - Haarlem; Amsterdam - Zaandam; Amsterdam Centraal - Schiphol.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The viaduct is located on the three railway lines between Amsterdam Central Station and Amsterdam Sloterdijk Station, the lines: Amsterdam - Haarlem; Amsterdam - Zaandam; Amsterdam Central - Schiphol.

features.opening: The Planciusspoorbrug is a railway viaduct in Amsterdam-Centrum in the Netherlands.

features.name: Pia Beckbrug

facts.text: The Pia Beckbrug honors jazz pianist Pia Beck, chosen from public proposals in January 2017.
facts.sourceQuote: In een actie van de gemeente Amsterdam om naamloze bruggen alsnog van een naam te voorzien kon de bevolking voorstellen indienen, waarbij als voorwaarden werd gesteld dat de naamstelling iets met de brug of buurt te maken had. De nieuwe naam van dit bouwwerk, vernoemd naar jazzpianiste Pia Beck, werd in januari 2017 bekendgemaakt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In an initiative by the municipality of Amsterdam to finally give nameless bridges a name, the population could submit proposals, with the conditions that the naming should have something to do with the bridge or neighborhood. The new name of this building, named after jazz pianist Pia Beck, was announced in January 2017.

facts.text: The surrounding neighborhood features streets named after jazz legends like Louis Armstrong and Duke Ellington.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug werd aangelegd ter ontsluiting van een wijk, waarvan de namen vernoemd zijn naar jazzmusici als Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington en Count Basie.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was built to open up a neighborhood, whose names are named after jazz musicians such as Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington and Count Basie.

features.opening: The Pia Beckbrug (bridge number 1868) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Slotervaart in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

features.name: Rozenoordspoorbrug

facts.text: Over 100 resistance fighters were executed at this location by the end of World War II.
facts.sourceQuote: Tegen het einde van de Tweede Wereldoorlog werden op deze plaats meer dan 100 verzetsstrijders gefusilleerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: By the end of World War II, more than 100 resistance fighters were executed at this location.

features.opening: The Rozenoord Bridge (bridge no. 174P (A10)) consists of two traffic bridges over the Amstel River in Amsterdam.

features.name: Jan Evertsenbrug

facts.text: The Jan Evertsenbrug takes its name from Admiral Jan Evertsen via the adjacent street.
facts.sourceQuote: Het bouwwerk werd daarbij vernoemd naar de Jan Evertsenstraat, die op haar beurt is vernoemd naar de admiraal Jan Evertsen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building was named after Jan Evertsenstraat, which in turn is named after Admiral Jan Evertsen.

facts.text: Amsterdam officially assigned this name to the structure on December 8, 2017.
facts.sourceQuote: Amsterdam vernoemde op 8 december 2017 (bijna) alle viaducten in de ringweg, om een betere plaatsaanduiding te krijgen. Op die datum werd de nieuwe naam Jan Evertsenbrug opgenomen in de Basisadministratie Adressen en Gebouwen (BAG).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Amsterdam renamed almost all the overpasses in the ring road on December 8, 2017, to get a better place name. On that date, the new name Jan Evertsenbrug was included in the Basic Addresses and Buildings Administration (BAG).

features.opening: The Jan Evertsenbrug (145p) is a work of art in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

features.name: Henriëtte van Heukelom-van den Brandelerbrug

facts.text: Dark brown armrests made of tropical hardwood sit atop wooden platforms with planks on the walkway.
facts.sourceQuote: Daarover liggen houten liggers met daarop gemonteerd planken en donkerbruine leuningen uitgevoerd in tropisch hardhout.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are wooden platforms with planks mounted on them and dark brown armrests made of tropical hardwood.

facts.text: A footpath was relocated after completion specifically to connect directly to this bridge.
facts.sourceQuote: Het voetpad werd na oplevering van de brug verlegd zodat het op de brug aansloot.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The footpath was relocated after the bridge was completed so that it connected to the bridge.

features.opening: Henriëtte van Heukelom-van den Brandelerbrug is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid.

features.name: Abdellah Zakibrug

facts.text: Commissioners initially rejected the name because they deemed the bridge not important enough.
facts.sourceQuote: De Commissie Naamgeving Openbare Ruimten (CNOR) adviseerde in beginsel positief op een vernoeming, maar vond de brug daarvoor niet belangrijk genoeg; men wilde de vernoeming later gebruiken bij de inrichting van een nieuwe woonwijk, waarvan de straten vernoemd worden naar schrijvers.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Commission on Naming Public Spaces (CNOR) initially advised positively on a naming, but found the bridge for this not important enough; they wanted to use the naming later when designing a new residential area, whose streets will be named after writers.

facts.text: The Abdellah Zakibrug honors Moroccan artist Abdellah Zaki, whose daughter campaigned for the tribute.
facts.sourceQuote: In maart 2023 werd de brug officieel vernoemd naar de Marokkaanse kunstenaar Abdellah Zaki. Zijn dochter had zich hiervoor ingespannen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In March 2023, the bridge was officially named after the Moroccan artist Abdellah Zaki. His daughter had made an effort for this.

facts.text: Mayors Femke Halsema and Nabila Rmili unveiled the official nameplate in April 2024.
facts.sourceQuote: De tenaamstelling werd in april 2024 aan de brug bevestigd; tevens werd er een infobord geplaatst. Deze werden door burgemeesters Femke Halsema van Amsterdam en Nabila Rmili van Casablanca onthuld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name was confirmed on the bridge in April 2024; an information board was also placed there. These were unveiled by mayors Femke Halsema of Amsterdam and Nabila Rmili of Casablanca.

features.opening: The Abdellah Zakibrug (bridge 180) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Oud-West.

features.name: Anton Jolingbrug

facts.text: Emergency bridges were installed in July 1886 while workers demolished the upper structure.
facts.sourceQuote: De verlaging en verbreding werd in gang gezet en in juli 1886 lagen er noodbruggen en is men bezig de bovenbouw te slopen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The lowering and widening was started and in July 1886 there were emergency bridges and work was underway to demolish the upper structure.

facts.text: A 1625 map depicts this location as a vaulted bridge with five passages over the canals.
facts.sourceQuote: Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode tekende op zijn kaart uit 1625 de brug als welfbrug met vijf doorvaarten in de Lely Graft over de Heere Graft.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode drew the bridge as a vaulted bridge with five passages in the Lely Graft over the Heere Graft on his map from 1625.

features.opening: The Anton Jolingbrug (bridge 20) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Berlagebrug

facts.text: Before this crossing, a ferry operated by the Zuidergasfabriek served the area since 1911.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1911, the Zuidergasfabriek operated their own ferry farther south of the Amstellaan, which became a municipal service in 1927.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1911, the Zuidergasfabriek operated their own ferry farther south of the Amstellaan, which became a municipal service in 1927.

facts.text: A nearby thoroughfare was renamed Stalinlaan before becoming Vrijheidslaan in 1956.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1925, the main thoroughfare of the new Rivierenbuurt district, the Amstellaan (later renamed Stalinlaan, then renamed again to Vrijheidslaan, in 1956), was completed.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1925, the main thoroughfare of the new Rivierenbuurt district, the Amstellaan (later renamed Stalinlaan, then renamed again to Vrijheidslaan, in 1956), was completed.

facts.text: Architect Piet Kramer was initially considered but rejected due to public criticism of his fantastical designs.
facts.sourceQuote: Initially architect Piet Kramer, one of the most prominent members of the Amsterdam School, was under consideration; he had a wealth of experience designing bridges and other buildings for the city. However, there was very public criticism of Kramer and his methods, with one architect, Hans Mieras, publishing an article that argued that two parties (an architect and an engineer) could never achieve the "purity" of a design by a single person. Mieras denounced Kramer and his "fantastical" designs which, he said, "could never contribute to enduring beauty in an environment".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Initially architect Piet Kramer, one of the most prominent members of the Amsterdam School, was under consideration; he had a wealth of experience designing bridges and other buildings for the city. However, there was very public criticism of Kramer and his methods, with one architect, Hans Mieras, publishing an article that argued that two parties (an architect and an engineer) could never achieve the "purity" of a design by a single person. Mieras denounced Kramer and his "fantastical" designs which, he said, "could never contribute to enduring beauty in an environment".

facts.text: Original plans called for round control towers and keeper houses before they were changed to rectangular shapes.
facts.sourceQuote: The control tower (placed eccentrically) and the bridgekeeper's house had been designed as round buildings, but this was changed to rectangular.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The control tower (placed eccentrically) and the bridgekeeper's house had been designed as round buildings, but this was changed to rectangular.

facts.text: Boathouses on the eastern bank and a marina on the western bank were integrated directly into the bridge design.
facts.sourceQuote: The banks on either side were integrated into the design, with boathouses on the Weesperzijde (east) and a marina on the Amsteldijk (west).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The banks on either side were integrated into the design, with boathouses on the Weesperzijde (east) and a marina on the Amsteldijk (west).

features.opening: The Berlagebrug (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈbɛrlaːɣəˌbrʏx]; English: Berlage Bridge) is a bascule bridge over the river Amstel in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

features.name: Leidsebrug

facts.text: A stone arch bridge known as the Leidse Barrier stood here until replaced between 1923 and 1925.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug werd in 1917 ontworpen door Piet Kramer in de stijl van de Amsterdamse school, maar werd pas tussen 1923 en 1925 gebouwd, ter vervanging van een oude stenen boogbrug die daar tot dan toe lag en ook wel de "Leidse Barrière" werd genoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was designed in 1917 by Piet Kramer in the style of the Amsterdam School, but was not built until between 1923 and 1925, to replace an old stone arch bridge that had been there until then and was also known as the "Leidse Barrier".

facts.text: Piet Kramer designed this structure in the Amsterdam School style back in 1917.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug werd in 1917 ontworpen door Piet Kramer in de stijl van de Amsterdamse school, maar werd pas tussen 1923 en 1925 gebouwd, ter vervanging van een oude stenen boogbrug die daar tot dan toe lag en ook wel de "Leidse Barrière" werd genoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was designed in 1917 by Piet Kramer in the style of the Amsterdam School, but was not built until between 1923 and 1925, to replace an old stone arch bridge that had been there until then and was also known as the "Leidse Barrier".

facts.text: The new span measures ten meters wider than its predecessor to accommodate shipping traffic.
facts.sourceQuote: De nieuwe brug werd 10 meter breder dan de oude brug en kreeg een tweetal doorvaarten voor het scheepvaartverkeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The new bridge was 10 meters wider than the old bridge and received two through passages for shipping traffic.

facts.text: Since 2015, the bridge has been closed to all traffic except trams during a complete renovation.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 2015 werd de brug, een rijksmonument, volledig gerenoveerd en behalve voor de trams voor al het verkeer tijdelijk gesloten en het verkeer werd omgeleid.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 2015, the bridge, a national monument, has been completely renovated and, except for the trams, temporarily closed to all traffic and traffic was diverted.

facts.text: Before renovation, large numbers of stopping buses regularly caused delays for tram traffic on the bridge.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot dan hadden de Connexxion buslijnen waaronder 170, 172 en 197 op de brug staduitwaarts een halte gelegen naast de trambaan en stadinwaarts voorbij de brug tegenover het Hirschgebouw op de trambaan wat regelmatig vertraging voor het tramverkeer veroorzaakte door het grote aantal halterende bussen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until then, the Connexxion bus lines including 170, 172 and 197 on the bridge cityward had a stop located next to the tramway and cityward past the bridge opposite the Hirschgebouw on the tramway, which regularly caused delays for tram traffic due to the large number of stopping buses.

facts.text: After renovation, bus lines did not return to the bridge despite previously serving it with many stops.
facts.sourceQuote: Daarnaast halteerde een groot aantal nachtbussen zowel van het GVB als van Connexxion op de brug. Na de renovatie keerde de buslijnen niet terug op de brug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In addition, a large number of night buses from both GVB and Connexxion stopped on the bridge. After the renovation, the bus lines did not return to the bridge.

features.opening: The Leidsebrug or Leidsepleinbrug, bridge no. 174, is a fixed plate bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum and crosses the Singelgracht.

features.name: Hendrick Jacobsz Staetsbrug

facts.text: Boatmen once raised a different bridge because they could pass under this one but hit the low bridge 34.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug speelde nog een rol in de verhoging van brug 34 in de Utrechtsestraat, want schippers vonden het vreemd dat ze wel onder deze brug doorkonden, maar vervolgens gestuit werden door de lage brug 34.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge still played a role in the raising of bridge 34 in the Utrechtsestraat, because boatmen found it strange that they could pass under this bridge, but then bumped into the low bridge 34.

features.opening: The Hendrick Jacobsz.

features.name: Entrepotdoksluis

facts.text: The current lock opened in 1840 with a double wooden drawbridge spanning its waters.
facts.sourceQuote: The current Entrepotdoksluis (lock) was opened in 1840. A double wooden drawbridge was then built over it.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The current Entrepotdoksluis (lock) was opened in 1840. A double wooden drawbridge was then built over it.

facts.text: Busy shipping prevented replacing the original bridge with a fixed structure during repairs.
facts.sourceQuote: As the shipping was still busy, the bridge could not be replaced by a fixed bridge when it was repaired.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As the shipping was still busy, the bridge could not be replaced by a fixed bridge when it was repaired.

facts.text: An iron and steel drawbridge replaced the wood around 1902 after a municipal decision.
facts.sourceQuote: Around 1902, the municipality opted for an iron/steel drawbridge.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Around 1902, the municipality opted for an iron/steel drawbridge.

facts.text: Designer Arend de Graaf created this bridge as part of his first generation of drawbridges.
facts.sourceQuote: According to Smit van Wichert, the designer was Arend de Graaf and belongs to his first generation of drawbridges.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: According to Smit van Wichert, the designer was Arend de Graaf and belongs to his first generation of drawbridges.

facts.text: Electric power controls arrived in 1911 via the NB Haarlemsche Machinefabriek.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1911, the controls were given electric power with a drive from the NB Haarlemsche Machinefabriek v / h / Gebr.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1911, the controls were given electric power with a drive from the NB Haarlemsche Machinefabriek v / h / Gebr.

facts.text: Modern control methods now reduce lubrication needs from ten times monthly to once per quarter.
facts.sourceQuote: However, today the bridge is controlled in the same way as the adjacent bridge 327, which resulted in a saving on the lubrication frequency from 10 times a month to once every quarter.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, today the bridge is controlled in the same way as the adjacent bridge 327, which resulted in a saving on the lubrication frequency from 10 times a month to once every quarter.

features.opening: The Entrepotdoksluis (bridge no. 80) is a bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum that crosses a lock by the same name.

features.name: Wim Sonneveldbrug

facts.text: André van Duin unveiled the new nameplate on June 28, 2017, during Wim Sonneveld's centenary.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2017 is de 100e geboortedag van Sonneveld herdacht. Op 28 juni 2017 onthulde onder meer André van Duin de nieuwe naamplaat van de brug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2017, Sonneveld's 100th birthday was commemorated. On June 28, 2017, among other things, André van Duin unveiled the new nameplate of the bridge.

facts.text: Piet Kramer designed this bridge with a simple style and no decorations or sculptures.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug is in 1935/1936 geplaatst naar een eenvoudig ontwerp van Piet Kramer, er zijn geen versieringen of beeldhouwwerken toegepast.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was built in 1935/1936 according to a simple design by Piet Kramer, no decorations or sculptures were applied.

facts.text: Construction of the structure took place during the years 1935 and 1936.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug is in 1935/1936 geplaatst naar een eenvoudig ontwerp van Piet Kramer, er zijn geen versieringen of beeldhouwwerken toegepast.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge was built in 1935/1936 according to a simple design by Piet Kramer, no decorations or sculptures were applied.

features.opening: The Wim Sonneveldbrug (bridge 175) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Bullebaksluis

facts.text: The Bullebaksluis honors the Bullebak, a water ghost from folklore that dragged children into the canals.
facts.sourceQuote: Beide bruggen zijn vernoemd naar een wezen uit een oud volksverhaal, het waterspook de Bullebak, dat in gewelven bij de sluisjes woonde en kinderen die te dicht bij de waterkant kwamen het water in sleurde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Both bridges are named after a creature from an old folk tale, the water ghost the Bullebak, who lived in vaults near the sluices and dragged children who came too close to the water into the water.

facts.text: Piet Kramer designed the original structure around 1930 as Amsterdam's public works architect.
facts.sourceQuote: De brug die stamt uit ongeveer 1930 is ontworpen door Piet Kramer, de bruggenarchitect van de Dienst der Publieke Werken van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge dating back to around 1930 was designed by Piet Kramer, the bridge architect of the Amsterdam Public Works Department.

facts.text: Tram line 10 crossed this busy bridge until July 2018 when line 5 took over its route.
facts.sourceQuote: Ze werd nog licht aangepast in 1968 en 1978 (delen werden vernieuwd en ze kreeg een ander profiel rijdek) De brug, waarvan het wegdek in de 21e eeuw direct in de Marnixstraat is opgenomen, was een zeer drukke verkeersbrug waar ook tramlijn 10 overheen reed (sinds juli 2018 tramlijn 5).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was slightly modified again in 1968 and 1978 (parts were renewed and it got a different driving profile) The bridge, whose road surface was incorporated directly into Marnixstraat in the 21st century, was a very busy traffic bridge where tram line 10 also ran over it (since July 2018 tram line 5).

facts.text: Alderman Sharon Dijksma banned freight and buses from the bridge in March 2019 due to poor condition.
facts.sourceQuote: Vanwege de slechte conditie van de brug besloot wethouder Sharon Dijksma in maart 2019 dat de brug per direct verboden terrein voor vracht- en busverkeer zou zijn.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Due to the poor condition of the bridge, alderman Sharon Dijksma decided in March 2019 that the bridge would immediately be prohibited territory for freight and bus traffic.

features.opening: The Bullebakssluis (bridge number 160) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Vier Heemskinderenbrug

facts.text: The Vier Heemskinderenbrug takes its name from a facade stone depicting the Vier Heemskinderen on horseback.
facts.sourceQuote: Een van die monumenten Herengracht 394 heeft een gevelsteen onder het middelste raam op de eerste verdieping met daarop de Vier Heemskinderen te paard, de naamgevers van deze brug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: One of those monuments Herengracht 394 has a facade stone under the middle window on the first floor with on it the Vier Heemskinderen on horseback, the namesakes of this bridge.

facts.text: Masonry, natural stone, and reinforced concrete form the structure topped with wrought iron balustrades.
facts.sourceQuote: Ze bestaat uit metselwerk, natuursteen (boog- en dekwerk) en gewapend beton met smeedijzeren balustrades.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It consists of masonry, natural stone (arch and roofwork) and reinforced concrete with wrought iron balustrades.

features.opening: The Vier Heemskinderenbrug, also known as Vier Heemskinderensluis, is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Jan Wilsbrug

facts.text: A steel tube carries the bike path while the footpath hangs on the side.
facts.sourceQuote: The span is carried by a steel tube on which the bike path is located. The footpath hangs there on the side, as it were.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The span is carried by a steel tube on which the bike path is located. The footpath hangs there on the side, as it were.

facts.text: Rotary castles equipped the pontoons to help maneuver the structure through Amsterdam canals.
facts.sourceQuote: The pontoons were equipped with rotary castles to maneuver better through the Amsterdam canals.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The pontoons were equipped with rotary castles to maneuver better through the Amsterdam canals.

facts.text: Jan Wilsbrug honors architect Jan Wils who designed the nearby Olympic Stadium.
facts.sourceQuote: The bridge is named after architect Jan Wils who provided the design of the nearby Olympic Stadium and the two buildings in Amsterdam famous for Citroën on Stadionplein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge is named after architect Jan Wils who provided the design of the nearby Olympic Stadium and the two buildings in Amsterdam famous for Citroën on Stadionplein.

features.opening: The Jan Wils Bridge is a permanent bridge for pedestrians and cyclists in Amsterdam-Zuid.

features.name: Pathé Arena

facts.text: The largest room features a 200 square meter screen for IMAX presentations.
facts.sourceQuote: De grootste zaal (14) heeft 480 stoelen en wordt gebruikt voor IMAX-voorstellingen; het scherm in deze zaal heeft een grootte van 200 m².
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The largest room (14) has 480 seats and is used for IMAX presentations; the screen in this room has a size of 200 m².

facts.text: Illuminated stairs flank the escalators as a distinctive architectural feature.
facts.sourceQuote: Kenmerkend aan de bioscoop zijn de lichtgevende trappen aan weerszijden van de roltrap.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Characteristic of the cinema are the illuminated stairs on either side of the escalator.

facts.text: The cinema drew 1.4 million visitors in 2019 despite having fewer rooms now.
facts.sourceQuote: Deze vestiging was ooit qua aantal zalen en stoelen de grootste bioscoop in Nederland, maar is na een renovatie van de zalen in 2018 teruggegaan in capaciteit. In 2019 trok de bioscoop 1,4 miljoen bezoekers.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This branch was once the largest cinema in the Netherlands in terms of number of rooms and seats, but after a renovation of the rooms in 2018, its capacity has decreased. In 2019, the cinema attracted 1.4 million visitors.

features.opening: Cinema in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

features.name: Montelbaanstoren

facts.text: The Duke of Alba proposed a castle named Monte Albano, which evolved into the current name Montelbaanstoren.
facts.sourceQuote: Because the 3rd Duke of Alba proposed incorporating the tower into a castle (the Monte Albano) the tower became known in Dutch as the Monte Albano Toren. Over the years this became garbled to "Montelbaanstoren." The castle was never built.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because the 3rd Duke of Alba proposed incorporating the tower into a castle (the Monte Albano) the tower became known in Dutch as the Monte Albano Toren. Over the years this became garbled to "Montelbaanstoren." The castle was never built.

facts.text: In 1516, this tower was constructed to defend Amsterdam and its harbor as part of the city walls.
facts.sourceQuote: The original tower was built in 1516 as part of the Walls of Amsterdam for the purpose of defending the city and the harbour.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The original tower was built in 1516 as part of the Walls of Amsterdam for the purpose of defending the city and the harbour.

facts.text: Hendrick de Keyser designed the decorative upper section added in 1606, bringing the total height to 48 meters.
facts.sourceQuote: The top half, designed by Hendrick de Keyser, was extended to its current, decorative form in 1606. Since then the tower has been 48m tall.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The top half, designed by Hendrick de Keyser, was extended to its current, decorative form in 1606. Since then the tower has been 48m tall.

facts.text: Although the Duke of Alba planned to incorporate the tower into his castle Monte Albano, that castle was never built.
facts.sourceQuote: Because the 3rd Duke of Alba proposed incorporating the tower into a castle (the Monte Albano) the tower became known in Dutch as the Monte Albano Toren. Over the years this became garbled to "Montelbaanstoren." The castle was never built.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because the 3rd Duke of Alba proposed incorporating the tower into a castle (the Monte Albano) the tower became known in Dutch as the Monte Albano Toren. Over the years this became garbled to "Montelbaanstoren." The castle was never built.

features.opening: The Montelbaanstoren is a tower on the bank of the Oudeschans – a canal in Amsterdam.

features.name: ASC SDW

facts.text: ASC SDW operated an athletics department from 1920 to 1955 featuring athletes like Giel Koolemans.
facts.sourceQuote: Tussen 1920 en 1955 was er een kleine atletiek-afdeling met bekende atleten als Giel Koolemans en Guus Dräger.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1920 and 1955 there was a small athletics department with well-known athletes such as Giel Koolemans and Guus Dräger.

facts.text: The club grounds include two cork-injected artificial turf fields alongside grass pitches.
facts.sourceQuote: Hier beschikt de club over twee kurk-ingestrooide kunstgrasvelden, een grasvoetbalveld en een half grasvoetbalveld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Here the club has two cork-injected artificial turf fields, a grass football field and a half grass football field.

facts.text: A canteen sits centrally between the fields with twelve dressing rooms located directly underneath.
facts.sourceQuote: Daarnaast centraal tussen de velden een kantine met er onder twaalf kleedruimtes.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In addition, centrally between the fields is a canteen with twelve dressing rooms underneath.

features.opening: ASC SDW (Amsterdam Sports Club Strong Through Willpower) is an amateur football club from Amsterdam, North Holland, Netherlands.

features.name: De Duif

facts.text: The name De Duif derives from the century-old hidden church Het Vrededuifje that previously stood on Kerkstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: Willibrorduskerk was itself a replacement for the century-old hidden church called "Het Vrededuifje" which had stood on the "Kerkstraat".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Willibrorduskerk was itself a replacement for the century-old hidden church called "Het Vrededuifje" which had stood on the "Kerkstraat".

facts.text: De Duif hosts the yearly Tangomagia and Tribal Art Fair festivals.
facts.sourceQuote: It hosts yearly events like the Tangomagia and the Tribal Art Fair.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It hosts yearly events like the Tangomagia and the Tribal Art Fair.

facts.text: The venue served as a location during the summer 2006 Holland Festival.
facts.sourceQuote: In the summer of 2006 it was one of the locations of the Holland Festival.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the summer of 2006 it was one of the locations of the Holland Festival.

facts.text: Television productions and product presentations occur within its walls.
facts.sourceQuote: In fact it is used for things like dance performances, product presentations, television production, theater, shows and business meeting events.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In fact it is used for things like dance performances, product presentations, television production, theater, shows and business meeting events.

features.opening: De Duif is a church on the Prinsengracht in Amsterdam.

features.name: Muiderkerk

facts.text: The original church partially burned down in 1989, leaving its distinctive tower unscathed.
facts.sourceQuote: De oude Muiderkerk, gebouwd in 1892, brandde deels af in 1989 maar de markante toren bleef gespaard.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The old Muiderkerk, built in 1892, partially burned down in 1989 but the distinctive tower remained unscathed.

facts.text: A modern structure built against the old tower lacks the exterior appearance of a traditional church.
facts.sourceQuote: De huidige Muiderkerk is tegen de oude toren aan gebouwd en is onderdeel van een bouwcomplex uit 1997 dat ontworpen werd door architect Van Hoogevest. Het nieuwe gedeelte heeft niet het karakteristiek exterieur dat men van een kerk verwacht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The current Muiderkerk is built against the old tower and is part of a 1997 construction complex designed by architect Van Hoogevest. The new part does not have the characteristic exterior that one expects of a church.

facts.text: The complex houses part of the Royal Institute for the Tropics.
facts.sourceQuote: Het complex huisvest ook een deel van het Koninklijk Instituut voor de Tropen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The complex also houses part of the Royal Institute for the Tropics.

features.opening: The Muiderkerk is a Protestant church on Linnaeusstraat in Amsterdam-Oost, on the edge of Oosterpark.

features.name: Andrieskerk

facts.text: The architect rejected straight lines to mimic crystals and restore human scale.
facts.sourceQuote: Hupkes lichtte het ontwerp al in 1969 toe; hij wilde af van rechte lijnen en rechthoekige vensters; hij liet zich meer inspireren door kristallen en wilde de menselijke maat terug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Hupkes already explained the design in 1969; he wanted to get rid of straight lines and rectangular windows; he was more inspired by crystals and wanted to return to the human scale.

facts.text: Copper plates on the roof were chosen so they would turn green over time.
facts.sourceQuote: Het dak werd afgewerkt met koperen platen, zodat het na verloop van tijd groen zou uitslaan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The roof was finished with copper plates, so that it would turn green over time.

facts.text: A large mural behind the altar depicts both death and resurrection.
facts.sourceQuote: Binnen is er achter het altaar een grote wandschildering waarin dood en opstanding verbeeld worden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Inside, behind the altar is a large mural depicting death and resurrection.

features.opening: The Andrieskerk is the church building of the Christian Community at Arent Janszoon Ernststraat 869 in the Buitenveldert district of Amsterdam.

features.name: De Dokwerker

facts.text: The monument was moved in 1970 to face a synagogue after originally gazing toward Waterlooplein.
facts.sourceQuote: De Dokwerker stond niet altijd op de plek waar hij nu staat. In het begin stond het beeld met de blik gericht op het Waterlooplein. In 1970 is het ten behoeve van werkzaamheden aan de metro en de Stopera verplaatst in de richting van de synagoge.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: De Dokwerker was not always in the place he is now. At first, the statue stood with its gaze directed at the Waterlooplein. In 1970, it was moved in the direction of the synagogue for work on the metro and the Stopera.

features.opening: De Dokwerker is a statue and monument on Jonas Daniël Meijerplein in Amsterdam in memory of the February Strike of 1941.

features.name: Nassaukerk

facts.text: Mayor Willem de Vlugt attended the opening on June 18, 1926, while the Bloemgrachtkerk closed its doors.
facts.sourceQuote: De opening, waarbij burgemeester Willem de Vlugt (de gemeente Amsterdam had een bijdrage verzorgd in de vorm van een tijdklok in het torentje) aanwezig was, vond plaats op 18 juni 1926, tegelijkertijd sloot de Bloemgrachtkerk haar deuren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The opening, at which Mayor Willem de Vlugt (the municipality of Amsterdam had provided a contribution in the form of a time clock in the tower) was present, took place on June 18, 1926, at the same time the Bloemgrachtkerk closed its doors.

facts.text: The final construction cost reached 153,300 guilders for a capacity of 924 people.
facts.sourceQuote: Men schatte in 1924 in dat de bouw 115.000 gulden zou kosten, voor een kerk die ruimte bood aan 700 personen; het werd uiteindelijk 153.300 gulden (aanbesteding februari 1925) voor een kerk geschikt voor 924 personen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1924, it was estimated that the construction would cost 115,000 guilders, for a church that could accommodate 700 people; it eventually cost 153,300 guilders (bid February 1925) for a church suitable for 924 people.

facts.text: The organ front forms a cross shape using hollow pipes as compartments on either side of the main pipes.
facts.sourceQuote: Het orgelfront heeft een kruisvorm, dit is bereikt doordat aan weerszijden van de orgelpijpen vakken zijn gemaakt met loze pijpen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The organ front has a cross shape, this has been achieved by making compartments on either side of the organ pipes with hollow pipes.

facts.text: Valckx & Van Kouteren constructed this pneumatic instrument with twenty-one registers in 1931.
facts.sourceQuote: Het orgel is gebouwd door Valckx & Van Kouteren in 1931. Het is een pneumatisch orgel met 21 registers.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The organ was built by Valckx & Van Kouteren in 1931. It is a pneumatic organ with 21 registers.

facts.text: A planned sale was cancelled in 1940, sparing the Nassaukerk while the Haarlemmerpoortkerk changed owners instead.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1940 leek het doek te vallen voor de kerk; een besluit tot verkoop werd echter ingetrokken, in plaats van de Nassaukerk werd de Haarlemmerpoortkerk van Tjeerd Kuipers verkocht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1940, it seemed that the curtain was falling for the church; however, a decision to sell was withdrawn, instead of the Nassaukerk, the Haarlemmerpoortkerk by Tjeerd Kuipers was sold.

features.opening: The Nassaukerk is a Protestant church of 1926 on the De Wittenkade in the Staatsliedenbuurt in Amsterdam-West.

features.name: Berlage's Stock Market

facts.text: Berlage's Stock Market uses massive brick walls to symbolize a democratic society where individuals are insignificant but the mass is powerful.
facts.sourceQuote: The enormous brick walls found in the Exchange embodied, in Berlage’s view, democratic society: “as individuals insignificant, as a mass a power.” The clock tower containing the “Beursbengel” may have been inspired by the thirteenth-century Torre del Popolo in the northern Italian city of Brescia.[1] More broadly, Romanesque and Renaissance architecture in northern Italy formed an important source of inspiration for Berlage’s Exchange, as can be seen, for example, in the Basilica of Saint Ambrose in Milan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The enormous brick walls found in the Exchange embodied, in Berlage’s view, democratic society: “as individuals insignificant, as a mass a power.” The clock tower containing the “Beursbengel” may have been inspired by the thirteenth-century Torre del Popolo in the northern Italian city of Brescia.[1] More broadly, Romanesque and Renaissance architecture in northern Italy formed an important source of inspiration for Berlage’s Exchange, as can be seen, for example, in the Basilica of Saint Ambrose in Milan.

facts.text: The clock tower housing the Beursbengel may have been inspired by the thirteenth-century Torre del Popolo in Brescia, Italy.
facts.sourceQuote: The enormous brick walls found in the Exchange embodied, in Berlage’s view, democratic society: “as individuals insignificant, as a mass a power.” The clock tower containing the “Beursbengel” may have been inspired by the thirteenth-century Torre del Popolo in the northern Italian city of Brescia.[1] More broadly, Romanesque and Renaissance architecture in northern Italy formed an important source of inspiration for Berlage’s Exchange, as can be seen, for example, in the Basilica of Saint Ambrose in Milan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The enormous brick walls found in the Exchange embodied, in Berlage’s view, democratic society: “as individuals insignificant, as a mass a power.” The clock tower containing the “Beursbengel” may have been inspired by the thirteenth-century Torre del Popolo in the northern Italian city of Brescia.[1] More broadly, Romanesque and Renaissance architecture in northern Italy formed an important source of inspiration for Berlage’s Exchange, as can be seen, for example, in the Basilica of Saint Ambrose in Milan.

facts.text: Berlage designed the Exchange so that its form and ornament closely correspond to its underlying structure.
facts.sourceQuote: In designing the Exchange, Berlage adhered to the principle that form and ornament should closely correspond to the structure—unity in diversity.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In designing the Exchange, Berlage adhered to the principle that form and ornament should closely correspond to the structure—unity in diversity.

facts.text: Engineers installed screw piles reaching twenty meters deep to stabilize the structure on a new concrete slab.
facts.sourceQuote: The solution involved installing screw injection piles throughout the entire basement. These piles were driven down to the so-called second sand layer, approximately 20 meters below Amsterdam Ordnance Datum (NAP). Across the full surface of the basement, a concrete foundation slab was constructed, which—through recesses in the masonry—was designed to support the superstructure.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The solution involved installing screw injection piles throughout the entire basement. These piles were driven down to the so-called second sand layer, approximately 20 meters below Amsterdam Ordnance Datum (NAP). Across the full surface of the basement, a concrete foundation slab was constructed, which—through recesses in the masonry—was designed to support the superstructure.

facts.text: The exterior color scheme was restored based on original hues identified through meticulous research.
facts.sourceQuote: Special points of attention during the restoration included the complete reconstruction of the former Safe Deposit (vaults) in the basement beneath the Café, and the striking “new” exterior color scheme, which was based on original colors identified through meticulous research.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Special points of attention during the restoration included the complete reconstruction of the former Safe Deposit (vaults) in the basement beneath the Café, and the striking “new” exterior color scheme, which was based on original colors identified through meticulous research.

features.opening: The Beurs van Berlage (literally Berlage's stock market) is a building on the Damrak, in the centre of Amsterdam.

features.name: Canal Ring Area of Amsterdam

facts.text: Canal Ring Area of Amsterdam expanded in four stages between 1585 and 1665.
facts.sourceQuote: This led to Amsterdam's expansion in four stages between 1585 and 1665.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This led to Amsterdam's expansion in four stages between 1585 and 1665.

facts.text: Reclamation of Herengracht, Keizersgracht, and Prinsengracht began in 1613.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1613, during the Twelve Years' Truce, reclamation of Herengracht, Keizersgracht, and Prinsengracht began.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1613, during the Twelve Years' Truce, reclamation of Herengracht, Keizersgracht, and Prinsengracht began.

facts.text: The Dutch name Grachtengordel literally translates to canal belt or girdle.
facts.sourceQuote: The Grachtengordel (Dutch pronunciation: [ˌɣrɑxtə(ŋ)ˈɣɔrdəl] , lit. 'canal belt/girdle'), known in English as the Canal District, is a neighborhood in Amsterdam, Netherlands located in the Centrum district.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Grachtengordel (Dutch pronunciation: [ˌɣrɑxtə(ŋ)ˈɣɔrdəl] , lit. 'canal belt/girdle'), known in English as the Canal District, is a neighborhood in Amsterdam, Netherlands located in the Centrum district.

facts.text: Canals run generally parallel from Brouwersgracht, leading gradually southeast into the Amstel river.
facts.sourceQuote: From the Brouwersgracht, the canals are generally parallel with one another, leading gradually southeast into the Amstel river.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From the Brouwersgracht, the canals are generally parallel with one another, leading gradually southeast into the Amstel river.

facts.text: Many buildings display different architectural styles due to restorations across various centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: Many of these buildings, however, underwent restoration or reconstruction in various centuries, meaning that the buildings display many different architectural styles and facades.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Many of these buildings, however, underwent restoration or reconstruction in various centuries, meaning that the buildings display many different architectural styles and facades.

features.name: Westergasfabriek

facts.text: Westergasfabriek means Western Gas Factory, one of four plants built by the Imperial Continental Gas Association.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 19th century the Imperial Continental Gas Association (ICGA) built four coal gas plants in Amsterdam: the Eastern Gas Factory, the Western Gas Factory, the Northern and the Southern.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 19th century the Imperial Continental Gas Association (ICGA) built four coal gas plants in Amsterdam: the Eastern Gas Factory, the Western Gas Factory, the Northern and the Southern.

facts.text: Television studios here host shows like Pauw & Witteman and De Wereld Draait Door.
facts.sourceQuote: Its television studios host programmes like Pauw & Witteman (a former late night talkshow), De Wereld Draait Door (an early evening talk show with Matthijs van Nieuwkerk) and Eva Jinek's Sunday morning talk show.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Its television studios host programmes like Pauw & Witteman (a former late night talkshow), De Wereld Draait Door (an early evening talk show with Matthijs van Nieuwkerk) and Eva Jinek's Sunday morning talk show.

facts.text: The main grass field accommodates six annual festivals.
facts.sourceQuote: The main grass field of the park allows for six festivals to be organized annually.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The main grass field of the park allows for six festivals to be organized annually.

facts.text: Thousands of visitors attend daily activities at the park.
facts.sourceQuote: Thousands of people visit the park and its activities every day.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Thousands of people visit the park and its activities every day.

features.opening: The Westergasfabriek is a former gasworks in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, now used as a cultural venue.

features.name: Oudemanhuispoort

facts.text: City sculptor Anthonie Ziesenis created the sculptural group adorning the gate designed by Abraham van der Hart.
facts.sourceQuote: De stad gaf de opdracht toen aan stadsbouwmeester Abraham van der Hart die een nieuwe buitenpoort ontwierp met kenmerken van de klassieke Dorische bouworde. Stadsbeeldhouwer Anthonie Ziesenis vervaardigde de beeldengroep op de poort.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The city then commissioned the city architect Abraham van der Hart to design a new outer gate with characteristics of classical Doric architecture. City sculptor Anthonie Ziesenis made the sculptural group on the gate.

facts.text: From 1836 to 1870, the Royal Academy of Fine Arts maintained a branch within this complex building.
facts.sourceQuote: Van 1836 tot 1870 had de Koninklijke Akademie voor Beeldende Kunsten een vestiging in het complex; daarna van 1870 tot 1875 de Rijksacademie.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1836 to 1870, the Royal Academy of Fine Arts had a branch in the complex; then from 1870 to 1875 the Royal Academy.

facts.text: The gate on the east side of a connecting passage gives Oudemanhuispoort its name.
facts.sourceQuote: In een van de vier vleugels is een doorgang die de Oudezijds Achterburgwal aan de westzijde verbindt met de Kloveniersburgwal aan de oostzijde, de poort aan de Oostzijde van deze doorgang is naamgever van het gebouwencomplex.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In one of the four wings is a passage that connects the Oudezijds Achterburgwal on the west side with the Kloveniersburgwal on the east side, the gate on the East Side of this passage is the namesake of the building complex.

features.opening: Oudemanhuispoort (often abbreviated as: OMHP) is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam, between the Spui and the Waterlooplein.

features.name: Artis Bibliotheek

facts.text: All issues of the journal Contributions to Zoology, published from 1848 to 1995, are now held here.
facts.sourceQuote: From 1848 to 1995, the Zoological Society Natura Artis Magistra published the journal Contributions to Zoology. All issues of this journal are now in the collection of the Artis Bibliotheek.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1848 to 1995, the Zoological Society Natura Artis Magistra published the journal Contributions to Zoology. All issues of this journal are now in the collection of the Artis Bibliotheek.

facts.text: Since 2005, the collection has belonged to the University of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: Since 2005, the Artis Bibliotheek has been part of the Special Collections at the University of Amsterdam, which in turn has been part of the Allard Pierson Museum since 2019.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 2005, the Artis Bibliotheek has been part of the Special Collections at the University of Amsterdam, which in turn has been part of the Allard Pierson Museum since 2019.

facts.text: In 2019, it joined the Allard Pierson Museum as part of Special Collections.
facts.sourceQuote: Since 2005, the Artis Bibliotheek has been part of the Special Collections at the University of Amsterdam, which in turn has been part of the Allard Pierson Museum since 2019.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 2005, the Artis Bibliotheek has been part of the Special Collections at the University of Amsterdam, which in turn has been part of the Allard Pierson Museum since 2019.

features.opening: The Artis Library (Dutch: Artis Bibliotheek) is a nineteenth-century library located at Plantage Middenlaan 45 in Amsterdam.

features.name: Royal Theater Carré

facts.text: Royal Theater Carré takes its name from the Carré family, who first performed in the Netherlands in 1863.
facts.sourceQuote: Carré is closely connected to the family Carré. This family group gave their first performances by the end of the 18th century and in 1863 they came to the Netherlands for the first time.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Carré is closely connected to the family Carré. This family group gave their first performances by the end of the 18th century and in 1863 they came to the Netherlands for the first time.

facts.text: In 1893, renting the venue for summer vaudeville allowed performances to run year-round instead of just in winter.
facts.sourceQuote: At first Carré was only used during the winter, the winter circus of Oscar Carré then performed but during the rest of the year this group travelled and the theatre was empty. However, in 1893 the theatre was rented by Dutch theatre producer Frits van Haarlem for his vaudeville shows in the summer, which meant that there were performances during the entire year.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At first Carré was only used during the winter, the winter circus of Oscar Carré then performed but during the rest of the year this group travelled and the theatre was empty. However, in 1893 the theatre was rented by Dutch theatre producer Frits van Haarlem for his vaudeville shows in the summer, which meant that there were performances during the entire year.

facts.text: International stars like Josephine Baker and Dutch icons such as Lou Bandy once graced this stage.
facts.sourceQuote: Dutch stars like Lou Bandy and Louis Davids and international celebrities like Josephine Baker and the clown Grock performed here.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Dutch stars like Lou Bandy and Louis Davids and international celebrities like Josephine Baker and the clown Grock performed here.

facts.text: Founded in 1887, the venue was originally built as a permanent circus building.
facts.sourceQuote: When the theatre was founded in 1887, it was originally meant as a permanent circus building.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When the theatre was founded in 1887, it was originally meant as a permanent circus building.

facts.text: The interior accommodates approximately 1,700 seats for its performances.
facts.sourceQuote: Its address is Amstel 115 and has approximately 1,700 seats.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Its address is Amstel 115 and has approximately 1,700 seats.

features.opening: The Royal Theater Carré (Dutch: Koninklijk Theater Carré) is a Neo-Renaissance theatre in Amsterdam, located near the river Amstel.

features.name: Max Euwe Centrum

facts.text: The center moved to a former prison on Max Euweplein in December 1991 after outgrowing its initial location.
facts.sourceQuote: Door de snelle groei van de bibliotheek en het aantal bezoekers, werd de eerste locatie al snel te klein. Vooral dankzij de inzet van toenmalig MEC-voorzitter Kees Snoep en de Amsterdamse zakenman Leo van der Kar volgde op 13 december 1991 de verhuizing naar het voormalige Huis van Bewaring aan het Max Euweplein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Due to the rapid growth of the library and the number of visitors, the first location soon became too small. Thanks in particular to the efforts of then MEC chairman Kees Snoep and the Amsterdam businessman Leo van der Kar, the move to the former Detention Center on Max Euweplein took place on December 13, 1991.

facts.text: Amsterdam mayor Ed van Thijn, a chess enthusiast, helped secure the venue for the new center.
facts.sourceQuote: Met steun van de Koninklijke Nederlandse Schaakbond (KNSB), sponsoren, donateurs en de Amsterdamse burgemeester Ed van Thijn, zelf een schaakliefhebber, kreeg het Max Euwe Centrum een eigen ruimte aan de Paleisstraat – nabij de Dam – waar ook het Bondsbureau van de KNSB was gevestigd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: With support from the Royal Dutch Chess Federation (KNSB), sponsors, donors and the Amsterdam mayor Ed van Thijn, himself a chess enthusiast, the Max Euwe Centrum was given its own space on Paleisstraat - near the Dam - where the KNSB Federal Bureau was also located.

facts.text: The current building previously served as a detention center before housing the chess organization.
facts.sourceQuote: In dit gebouw hebben zich sinds de sluiting van de penitentiaire inrichting in 1979 diverse startende bedrijven en non-profitorganisaties gevestigd, waaronder het Max Euwe Centrum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since the closure of the penitentiary facility in 1979, various start-up companies and non-profit organizations have settled in this building, including Max Euwe Centrum.

facts.text: The center honors Max Euwe, a Dutch world chess champion who lived from 1901 to 1981.
facts.sourceQuote: Het bestaat uit een klein museum over de schaakcarrière en het leven van de Nederlandse wereldkampioen Max Euwe (1901-1981) en een ontmoetingscentrum annex bibliotheek met circa elfduizend boeken en tijdschriften.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It consists of a small museum about the chess career and the life of the Dutch world champion Max Euwe (1901-1981) and a meeting center annex library with about eleven thousand books and magazines.

facts.text: Visitors can explore an annex library holding approximately eleven thousand books and magazines.
facts.sourceQuote: Het bestaat uit een klein museum over de schaakcarrière en het leven van de Nederlandse wereldkampioen Max Euwe (1901-1981) en een ontmoetingscentrum annex bibliotheek met circa elfduizend boeken en tijdschriften.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It consists of a small museum about the chess career and the life of the Dutch world champion Max Euwe (1901-1981) and a meeting center annex library with about eleven thousand books and magazines.

features.opening: The Max Euwe Centrum is a chess centre on the Max Euweplein in Amsterdam.

features.name: Nederlandse Film en Televisie Academie

facts.text: Founded in 1958, the Nederlandse Film en Televisie Academie began training crews decades ago.
facts.sourceQuote: The Netherlands Film Academy (Dutch: Nederlandse Filmacademie) (NFA) was founded in 1958.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Netherlands Film Academy (Dutch: Nederlandse Filmacademie) (NFA) was founded in 1958.

facts.text: Students specialize in fields ranging from sound design to interactive visual effects.
facts.sourceQuote: Specialisation is possible in fiction directing, documentary directing, screenwriting, editing, producing, sounddesign, cinematography, production design, and interactive multimedia/visual effects.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Specialisation is possible in fiction directing, documentary directing, screenwriting, editing, producing, sounddesign, cinematography, production design, and interactive multimedia/visual effects.

facts.text: Alumni include director Paul Verhoeven, known for Total Recall and Basic Instinct.
facts.sourceQuote: Mike van Diem, director of Character Gied Jaspars, television and radio director Frank Ketelaar, screenwriter, film and television director Martin Koolhoven, director Nanouk Leopold, director Dick Maas, director Pim de la Parra, director Diederik van Rooijen, director Theo van de Sande, cinematographer of Blade and Grown Ups Carel Struycken, actor in The Addams Family and Twin Peaks Paul Verhoeven, director of Total Recall and Basic Instinct Leon de Winter, writer and film producer

features.opening: The Netherlands Film Academy (Dutch: Nederlandse Filmacademie) (NFA) was founded in 1958.

features.name: Vondelmonument

facts.text: The municipality held only the few square meters under the statue from 1868 until gaining the whole park in 1953.
facts.sourceQuote: Hoewel het park pas in 1953 in handen van de gemeente Amsterdam overging, had die al sinds 1868 een heel klein stukje van het park in handen, namelijk 'de paar vierkante meter waarop het beeld van Vondel staat.'
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Although the park only came into the hands of the municipality of Amsterdam in 1953, it had already had a very small part of the park in its hands since 1868, namely 'the few square meters on which the statue of Vondel stands.'

facts.text: For nearly a century, Amsterdam owned just the tiny patch of ground beneath the statue before acquiring the rest of the park.
facts.sourceQuote: Hoewel het park pas in 1953 in handen van de gemeente Amsterdam overging, had die al sinds 1868 een heel klein stukje van het park in handen, namelijk 'de paar vierkante meter waarop het beeld van Vondel staat.'
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Although the park only came into the hands of the municipality of Amsterdam in 1953, it had already had a very small part of the park in its hands since 1868, namely 'the few square meters on which the statue of Vondel stands.'

facts.text: Napoleon III is specifically mentioned as one of the crowned heads who contributed to funding the Vondelmonument.
facts.sourceQuote: De ondertitel luidde 'Geestdriftige poëzie achter prikkeldraad' en er wordt aan herinnerd dat destijds 'meer dan één gekroond hoofd in Europa' aan het standbeeld heeft bijgedragen, waarvan Napoleon III met name wordt genoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The subtitle was 'Spirituous poetry behind barbed wire' and it is recalled that at the time 'more than one crowned head in Europe' contributed to the statue, of which Napoleon III is particularly mentioned.

features.opening: The Vondel monument, also known as the Vondelbeeld, is a large statue of the 17th-century Dutch poet and playwright Joost van den Vondel in the Vondelpark in…

features.name: Cat Cabinet

facts.text: Founder Bob Meijer named the museum after his red tomcat, John Pierpont Morgan.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1985, the building was restored, and in 1990 the museum was founded by Bob Meijer in memory of his red tomcat John Pierpont Morgan (named after the American banker J. P. Morgan).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1985, the building was restored, and in 1990 the museum was founded by Bob Meijer in memory of his red tomcat John Pierpont Morgan (named after the American banker J. P. Morgan).

facts.text: The location served as a filming site for the 2004 movie Ocean's Twelve.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum served as filming location for Ocean's Twelve in 2004.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum served as filming location for Ocean's Twelve in 2004.

facts.text: Live cats actually inhabit the museum alongside the displayed artworks.
facts.sourceQuote: There are some cats in the museum as well.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are some cats in the museum as well.

features.opening: The KattenKabinet ("Cat Cabinet") is an art museum in Amsterdam devoted to works depicting cats.

features.name: LJG

facts.text: The congregation flourished again under Rabbi Jacob Soetendorp from 1954 to 1972.
facts.sourceQuote: Onder Jacob Soetendorp, die van 1954 tot 1972 rabbijn was van de Liberaal Joodse Gemeente Amsterdam, kwam de gemeente weer tot bloei.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Under Jacob Soetendorp, who was rabbi of the Liberaal Joodse Gemeente Amsterdam from 1954 to 1972, the congregation flourished again.

facts.text: Menno ten Brink has served as a rabbi for the community since 1995.
facts.sourceQuote: Rabbijn voor de LJG zijn (anno 2025): Menno ten Brink (sinds 1995) en Joram Rookmaker.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Rabbins for the LJG are (as of 2025): Menno ten Brink (since 1995) and Joram Rookmaker.

facts.text: The Gan Hasjalom cemetery in Hoofddorp and Amstelveen falls under its care.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook de begraafplaats Gan Hasjalom, in Hoofddorp en Amstelveen, valt onder de Amsterdamse LJG.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Gan Hasjalom cemetery, in Hoofddorp and Amstelveen, is also under the Amsterdam LJG.

features.name: HvA

facts.text: The HES merged into the Hogeschool of Amsterdam after over 125 years as a separate economics school.
facts.sourceQuote: De Hogeschool voor Economische Studies (HES) in Amsterdam was een HBO-onderwijsinstelling met opleidingen op economisch gebied en was een school met een traditie van meer dan 125 jaar. Tegenwoordig is het onderdeel geworden van economische onderwijsinstituut van de Hogeschool van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Hogeschool for Economische Studies (HES) in Amsterdam was a HBO educational institution with courses in the field of economics and was a school with a tradition of more than 125 years. Today it has become part of the economic education institute of the Hogeschool of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The HES merged with the Hogeschool of Amsterdam, making all former HES courses part of the new institution.
facts.section: Fusie en de huidige stand van zaken
facts.sourceQuote: Later in hetzelfde jaar zijn de HES en de Hogeschool van Amsterdam gefuseerd. Alle opleidingen die voorheen zelf door de HES werden gegeven werden vallen nu onder de Hogeschool van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Later in the same year, the HES and the Hogeschool of Amsterdam merged. All courses that were previously taught by the HES themselves are now under the Hogeschool of Amsterdam.

features.name: AFC

facts.text: The name Amsterdamsche Football Club was chosen after a long discussion at the founding meeting.
facts.sourceQuote: On 18 January 1895 the founding meeting took place in the basement of a house on the Koninginneweg where after a long discussion the name "Amsterdamsche Football Club (AFC)" was chosen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On 18 January 1895 the founding meeting took place in the basement of a house on the Koninginneweg where after a long discussion the name "Amsterdamsche Football Club (AFC)" was chosen.

facts.text: Six boys aged fifteen and sixteen founded the club, including Gerard Scheepens and Hein Brass.
facts.sourceQuote: The meeting was held by six boys aged fifteen and sixteen. Four of them being Gerard Scheepens, Hein Brass, Frits Bernard and G.J.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The meeting was held by six boys aged fifteen and sixteen. Four of them being Gerard Scheepens, Hein Brass, Frits Bernard and G.J.

facts.text: AFC was established in 1895 during a meeting held in a basement on Koninginneweg.
