facts.sourceQuote: In 1639 werd Jacoba Victoria, dochter van Guillelmo (1602-1658), in het huis geboren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1639, Jacoba Victoria, daughter of Guillelmo (1602-1658), was born in the house.

facts.text: The full family name sometimes appears as Van den Heuvel tot Beichlingen Bartolotti.
facts.sourceQuote: De naam is soms ook "Van den Heuvel tot Beichlingen gezegd Bartolotti".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name is sometimes also said "Van den Heuvel tot Beichlingen Bartolotti".

features.opening: Het Huis Bartolotti (also Het Bonte Huis) is a canal house at Herengracht 170-172 in Amsterdam.

features.name: Compagnietheater

facts.text: Amsterdam carpenter Jan Smit executed the construction of this structure designed by Abraham van der Hart.
facts.sourceQuote: Het gebouw is ontworpen door de Amsterdamse stadsarchitect Abraham van der Hart en is gebouwd in 1792-1793; op de plaats van het voormalige dolhuis. De uitvoering berustte bij de Amsterdamse timmerbaas Jan Smit.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building was designed by the Amsterdam city architect Abraham van der Hart and was built in 1792-1793; on the site of the former lunatic asylum. The execution was entrusted to the Amsterdam carpenter Jan Smit.

facts.text: Anthonie Ziesenis created the sculptural group on the facade representing the steadfastness of faith.
facts.sourceQuote: De beeldengroep aan de voorgevel is van de hand van Anthonie Ziesenis en representeert de standvastigheid van het geloof.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The sculptural group on the front facade is by Anthonie Ziesenis and represents the steadfastness of faith.

facts.text: Francine Houben of Mecanoo converted the building into a theater between 1995 and 1996.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1995-1996 is het pand door Francine Houben van architectenbureau Mecanoo verbouwd tot theater.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1995-1996, the building was converted into a theater by Francine Houben of architectural firm Mecanoo.

facts.text: A 2014 renovation restored the facade, sculptural group, and roof while adding a kitchen.
facts.sourceQuote: In de zomer van 2014 is het Compagnietheater gerenoveerd. De buitengevel is opnieuw gevoegd, de beeldengroep is gerestaureerd en het dak is gerenoveerd. Bovendien is de entree vernieuwd en er zijn extra faciliteiten gekomen (van daglichtsysteem in de Grote Zaal tot een keuken op de begane grond).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the summer of 2014, the Compagnietheater was renovated. The facade has been re-joined, the sculptural group has been restored and the roof has been renovated. In addition, the entrance has been renovated and additional facilities have been added (from daylight system in the Great Hall to a kitchen on the ground floor).

features.opening: The Compagnietheater is housed in the former church of the Reformed Lutheran church on the Kloveniersburgwal in Amsterdam.

features.name: Oude Lutherse Kerk

facts.text: Doric columns support the roof while Ionic and Tuscan columns hold up the surrounding galleries.
facts.sourceQuote: Het inwendige is rechthoekig van vorm, omgeven door galerijen die rusten op Ionische en Toscaanse zuilen. Dorische zuilen dragen de dakconstructie.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The interior is rectangular in shape, surrounded by galleries resting on Ionic and Tuscan columns. Doric columns support the roof structure.

facts.text: Construction occurred rapidly between 1632 and 1633.
facts.sourceQuote: De kerk is in de periode 1632-1633 onder leiding van Wessel Becker en Willem van Daelen gebouwd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church was built between 1632 and 1633 under the direction of Wessel Becker and Willem van Daelen.

facts.text: Wessel Becker and Willem van Daelen directed the building project.
facts.sourceQuote: De kerk is in de periode 1632-1633 onder leiding van Wessel Becker en Willem van Daelen gebouwd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church was built between 1632 and 1633 under the direction of Wessel Becker and Willem van Daelen.

features.opening: The Oude Lutherse Kerk at Singel 411, corner Spui, in Amsterdam is a Lutheran church, built on the site where the Lutheran congregation hall used to stand.

features.name: Vondelpark Open Air Theater

facts.text: Attendees pay no entry fee, though a voluntary donation is requested for the shows.
facts.sourceQuote: De voorstellingen zijn gratis toegankelijk, wel wordt een vrije gift gevraagd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The performances are free to attend, but a voluntary donation is requested.

facts.text: Every Saturday features professional artists preceded by young talent in a pre-program.
facts.sourceQuote: De zondag is de dag van de muziek, variërend van onder andere pop, rock, tot Nederlandstalige-, wereld- en klassieke muziek Elke Openluchttheaterdag bestaat uit een hoofdprogramma van professionele artiesten en gezelschappen voorafgegaan door een voorprogramma van jong en nieuw talent.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Sunday is the day of music, ranging from pop, rock, among others, to Dutch, world and classical music. Every Open Air Saturday consists of a main program of professional artists and companies preceded by a pre-program of young and new talent.

facts.text: Young performers use 'In de Voorhoede' to introduce themselves to the audience.
facts.sourceQuote: Jonge dansers, (klassieke) musici, cabaretiers en muzikanten krijgen 'In de Voorhoede' de ruimte om zich te introduceren aan het publiek.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Young dancers, (classical) musicians, cabaret artists and musicians get 'In de Voorhoede' the space to introduce themselves to the audience.

features.opening: The Vondelpark Open-Air Theater in Amsterdam has been organizing concerts and performances by amateurs and professional performers in the field of cabaret,…

features.name: De Vriendschap

facts.text: A lightning strike destroyed the original mill on September 23, 1899.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 23 september 1899 brandt de oude molen af als gevolg van blikseminslag.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On September 23, 1899, the old mill burns down as a result of lightning strike.

facts.text: The name De Vriendschap was adopted in 1817 following a mill exchange.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1813 veranderde de naam in Het Anker en in 1817, als gevolg van een molenruil in Weesp, in De Vriendschap.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1813 the name was changed to Het Anker and in 1817, as a result of a mill exchange in Weesp, to De Vriendschap.

facts.text: Miller Wouterus van den Akker purchased the mill in 1860.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1860 koopt molenaar Wouterus van den Akker, destijds molenaar op molen ‘t Haantje, de molen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1860, miller Wouterus van den Akker, then miller at mill 't Haantje, buys the mill.

facts.text: The outer wheel measures 24.80 meters and bears the number 193.
facts.sourceQuote: De buitenroede heeft het nummer 193 en is 24,80 m lang.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The outer wheel has the number 193 and is 24.80 m long.

features.opening: De Vriendschap is a windmill built in 1900 on the site of a mill that burned down in 1899.

features.name: Begijnhof

facts.text: Before 1979, about 110 of the 140 houses consisted of only a single room.
facts.sourceQuote: Until its renovation in 1979, the court had 140 dwellings — some 110 of them consisting of a single room, and about 25 comprising two.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until its renovation in 1979, the court had 140 dwellings — some 110 of them consisting of a single room, and about 25 comprising two.

facts.text: The name Begijnhof indicates the site was originally a béguinage.
facts.sourceQuote: As the name suggests, it was originally a béguinage.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As the name suggests, it was originally a béguinage.

facts.text: Two distinct churches, the Catholic Miracle Church and English Reformed Church, stand on the grounds today.
facts.sourceQuote: Today it is also the site of two churches, the Catholic Miracle Church and the English Reformed Church.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Today it is also the site of two churches, the Catholic Miracle Church and the English Reformed Church.

features.opening: The Begijnhof is one of the oldest hofjes in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

features.name: Sint-Franciscus Xaveriuskerk

facts.text: A Jesuit church has stood at this location since 1654.
facts.sourceQuote: Since 1654 there has been a Jesuit church at this location.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1654 there has been a Jesuit church at this location.

facts.text: Architect Alfred Tepe designed an unusually tall structure due to space limitations.
facts.sourceQuote: Space limitations urged architect Alfred Tepe to design an unusually tall church with a monumental front.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Space limitations urged architect Alfred Tepe to design an unusually tall church with a monumental front.

facts.text: Services are conducted in a variety of styles within this single building.
facts.sourceQuote: Services there are in a variety of styles.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Services there are in a variety of styles.

facts.text: Alfred Tepe designed the church, which opened in 1883.
facts.sourceQuote: The church was designed by Alfred Tepe and was opened in 1883.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church was designed by Alfred Tepe and was opened in 1883.

facts.text: Friedrich Wilhelm Mengelberg created the exuberant interior.
facts.sourceQuote: The exuberant interior was made by Friedrich Wilhelm Mengelberg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The exuberant interior was made by Friedrich Wilhelm Mengelberg.

features.opening: De Krijtberg Kerk is a Roman Catholic church in Amsterdam, located at the Singel.

features.name: Van Buurenmonument

facts.text: Van Buuren received a silver medal and this monument upon his 1936 retirement.
facts.sourceQuote: Bij zijn afscheid in december 1936 als voorzitter van de Bouwmaatschappij kreeg Van Buuren de zilveren medaille van Amsterdam aangeboden en een gedenkteken dat werd geplaatst in het centrale plantsoen van de Coöperatiehof.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At his farewell in December 1936 as chairman of the Bouwmaatschappij, Van Buuren was offered the silver medal of Amsterdam and a monument that was placed in the central square of the Coöperatiehof.

facts.text: A bronze plaque honoring him was installed on Rivierenlaan in November 1933.
facts.sourceQuote: Van Buuren werd in 1933 benoemd tot ridder in de Orde van Oranje-Nassau en in november van dat jaar gehuldigd met een bronzen plaquette aan de Rivierenlaan, gemaakt door Jan Schultsz.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Van Buuren was appointed a knight of the Order of Orange-Nassau in 1933 and in November of that year was honored with a bronze plaque on Rivierenlaan, made by Jan Schultsz.

facts.text: The sphere rests on a short base featuring a compass rose, a motif recurring in architect Piet Kramer's work.
facts.sourceQuote: Het bolvormig monument heeft een korte voet die rust op een kompasroos. Die kompasroos is een terugkerend onderdeel bij Piet Kramer, zie bijvoorbeeld zijn brug 543 in het Amsterdamse Bos.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The spherical monument has a short base that rests on a compass rose. That compass rose is a recurring element at Piet Kramer's work, see for example his bridge 543 in the Amsterdamse Bos.

features.opening: The Van Buurenmonument is a memorial in Amsterdam commemorating Lucas van Buuren.

features.name: Old Church

facts.text: Founded around 1213, it was consecrated as a Roman Catholic church in 1306.
facts.sourceQuote: The oldest structure in Amsterdam, the building was founded around 1213 and consecrated in 1306 as a Roman Catholic church by the bishop of Utrecht with Saint Nicolas as its patron saint.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The oldest structure in Amsterdam, the building was founded around 1213 and consecrated in 1306 as a Roman Catholic church by the bishop of Utrecht with Saint Nicolas as its patron saint.

facts.text: Saint Nicolas serves as the patron saint of this historic building.
facts.sourceQuote: The oldest structure in Amsterdam, the building was founded around 1213 and consecrated in 1306 as a Roman Catholic church by the bishop of Utrecht with Saint Nicolas as its patron saint.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The oldest structure in Amsterdam, the building was founded around 1213 and consecrated in 1306 as a Roman Catholic church by the bishop of Utrecht with Saint Nicolas as its patron saint.

features.opening: The Oude Kerk (English: Old Church) is a Reformed church in Amsterdam, Netherlands, being the oldest parish church in the city.

features.name: Moco Museum

facts.text: Kim Logchies-Prins and Lionel Logchies founded the institution to reach wider audiences.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum was founded in 2016 by Kim Logchies-Prins and Lionel Logchies as an independent initiative aiming “to make modern and contemporary art more accessible to a wider audience beyond traditional collectors and institutions”.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum was founded in 2016 by Kim Logchies-Prins and Lionel Logchies as an independent initiative aiming “to make modern and contemporary art more accessible to a wider audience beyond traditional collectors and institutions”.

facts.text: Early exhibitions featured street art and works by Banksy and Andy Warhol.
facts.sourceQuote: Early collections and programming focused on popular modern and contemporary figures and street art, aiming to reach broader audiences through accessible exhibitions, and included works by artists such as Banksy and Andy Warhol.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Early collections and programming focused on popular modern and contemporary figures and street art, aiming to reach broader audiences through accessible exhibitions, and included works by artists such as Banksy and Andy Warhol.

facts.text: Critics view it as part of a shift blending high-profile pop culture with contemporary collections.
facts.sourceQuote: Commentators have described the museum as part of a broader shift towards privately funded art spaces that combine high-profile popular culture with contemporary art collections, including digital and immersive works.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Commentators have described the museum as part of a broader shift towards privately funded art spaces that combine high-profile popular culture with contemporary art collections, including digital and immersive works.

facts.text: The Amsterdam location opened in 2016 inside the historic Villa Alsberg.
facts.sourceQuote: Moco Museum in Amsterdam opened in 2016 on Museumplein, in the historic Villa Alsberg, a townhouse designed in 1904 by Eduard Cuypers the nephew of Pierre Cuypers, designer of Amsterdam Central Station and the Rijksmuseum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Moco Museum in Amsterdam opened in 2016 on Museumplein, in the historic Villa Alsberg, a townhouse designed in 1904 by Eduard Cuypers the nephew of Pierre Cuypers, designer of Amsterdam Central Station and the Rijksmuseum.

facts.text: Eduard Cuypers, nephew of the Rijksmuseum designer, designed this townhouse in 1904.
facts.sourceQuote: Moco Museum in Amsterdam opened in 2016 on Museumplein, in the historic Villa Alsberg, a townhouse designed in 1904 by Eduard Cuypers the nephew of Pierre Cuypers, designer of Amsterdam Central Station and the Rijksmuseum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Moco Museum in Amsterdam opened in 2016 on Museumplein, in the historic Villa Alsberg, a townhouse designed in 1904 by Eduard Cuypers the nephew of Pierre Cuypers, designer of Amsterdam Central Station and the Rijksmuseum.

features.opening: The Moco Museum (Modern Contemporary Museum) is an independent art museum with locations in Amsterdam, Barcelona, and London, dedicated to exhibiting modern…

features.name: Willet-Holthuysen

facts.text: The house was built around 1685 for Jacob Hop, who served as mayor of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: The house was built for Jacob Hop, mayor of Amsterdam, around 1685.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The house was built for Jacob Hop, mayor of Amsterdam, around 1685.

facts.text: Louisa Holthuysen bequeathed the estate to Amsterdam in 1895, naming it after her and husband Abraham Willet.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1895, its owner, Louisa Holthuysen, bequeathed the building and its contents, including the art collected by her and her husband, Abraham Willet, to the city of Amsterdam on condition that it became a museum bearing their names.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1895, its owner, Louisa Holthuysen, bequeathed the building and its contents, including the art collected by her and her husband, Abraham Willet, to the city of Amsterdam on condition that it became a museum bearing their names.

facts.text: Jacob de Wit's decorative paintings were once owned by the house but taken away by previous owners.
facts.sourceQuote: Decorative pieces by Jacob de Wit were at some stage in the house, but previous owners took them with them.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Decorative pieces by Jacob de Wit were at some stage in the house, but previous owners took them with them.

facts.text: The blue room features wall paintings of former owners alongside works by Jacob de Wit from other buildings.
facts.sourceQuote: In the blue room, several paintings on the walls show previous owners (by unspecified artists). In this room there are also several decorative paintings by Jacob de Wit, though these have been sourced from other buildings in Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the blue room, several paintings on the walls show previous owners (by unspecified artists). In this room there are also several decorative paintings by Jacob de Wit, though these have been sourced from other buildings in Amsterdam.

facts.text: The garden and kitchen were restored in 1972 after being part of the souterrain level.
facts.sourceQuote: Three floors are open to the public, the souterrain, with the kitchen and garden (restored in 1972), the first floor (bel-etage with long hallway), and the top floor, with one bedroom on display and rooms for exhibitions.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Three floors are open to the public, the souterrain, with the kitchen and garden (restored in 1972), the first floor (bel-etage with long hallway), and the top floor, with one bedroom on display and rooms for exhibitions.

features.opening: Museum Willet-Holthuysen is a located on the Herengracht in Amsterdam.

features.name: P.W. Janssen

facts.text: Janssen's statue was temporarily removed between 1954 and 1955 when the lawn fountain changed to a pier bath.
facts.sourceQuote: Het beeld werd enige tijd weggehaald toen in 1954/1955 de grote fontein in het middel van het plantsoen vervangen werd door een pierenbad. Op 13 mei 1955 werd het weer op zijn plaats getakeld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The statue was removed for a while when in 1954/1955 the large fountain in the middle of the lawn was replaced by a pier bath. On May 13, 1955, it was again brought back into place.

facts.text: Mayor Wilhelmus Frederik van Leeuwen, born in the Dutch East Indies, attended the monument's unveiling.
facts.sourceQuote: Burgemeester Wilhelmus Frederik van Leeuwen (geboren in Nederlands-Indië) was bij de onthulling aanwezig.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Mayor Wilhelmus Frederik van Leeuwen (born in Dutch East Indies) was present at the unveiling.

features.opening: The Monument Peter Wilhelm Janssen is a monument on Bellamyplein in Amsterdam-West.

features.name: Meerpadkerk

facts.text: Carpenter Pieter Kater Gzn constructed the church in 1843.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Meerpadkerkje is een kleine doopsgezinde witgeschilderde houten kerk ("vermaning") in Nieuwendam, tegenwoordig een deel van Amsterdam-Noord, gebouwd in 1843 door de Nieuwendamse timmerman Pieter Kater Gzn.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Meerpadkerkje is a small Baptist whitewashed wooden church ("remonstration") in Nieuwendam, now part of Amsterdam-North, built in 1843 by the Nieuwendamse carpenter Pieter Kater Gzn.

features.opening: The Meerpadkerkje is a small white-painted wooden Mennonite meeting house in Nieuwendam, now part of Amsterdam-Noord, built in 1843 by the Nieuwendam carpenter…

features.name: Dominicuskerk

facts.text: A hidden church received a new facade in 1829 before being renovated again in 1844.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1829 werd de schuilkerk - met een boven de pastorie gelegen kerkzaal - van een nieuwe voorgevel voorzien, die in 1844 bij een tweede grondige verbouwing door de Amsterdamse architect Robertus van Zoelen alweer door een volgende werd vervangen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1829, the hidden church - with a church hall located above the parsonage - was provided with a new facade, which was again replaced by a subsequent one in 1844 during a second thorough renovation by the Amsterdam architect Robertus van Zoelen.

facts.text: The current Dominicuskerk was completed and inaugurated by Bishop Bottemanne of Haarlem in 1893.
facts.sourceQuote: De kerk werd in 1893 voltooid en ingewijd door bisschop Bottemanne van Haarlem.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church was completed in 1893 and inaugurated by Bishop Bottemanne of Haarlem.

facts.text: Pierre Cuypers designed this church for the Dominican order.
facts.sourceQuote: Zij werd als rooms-katholieke Parochiekerk van Sint-Dominicus gebouwd door Pierre Cuypers en bediend door de Dominicanen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was built as a Roman Catholic Parish Church of St. Dominic by Pierre Cuypers and served by the Dominicans.

features.opening: The Dominicuskerk is a neo-Gothic church building on Spuistraat in Amsterdam.

features.name: Oost-Indisch Huis

facts.text: Hendrick de Keyser likely designed the building featuring Amsterdam Renaissance style and Tuscan-style pilasters.
facts.sourceQuote: A gate with Tuscan-style pilasters and a small tunnel lead to an inner courtyard with elegant facades in Amsterdam Renaissance style, a style closely identified with the architect Hendrick de Keyser, who was most likely responsible for designing the building.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A gate with Tuscan-style pilasters and a small tunnel lead to an inner courtyard with elegant facades in Amsterdam Renaissance style, a style closely identified with the architect Hendrick de Keyser, who was most likely responsible for designing the building.

facts.text: After the East India Company dissolved in 1798, the site served as the colonial government seat until 1808.
facts.sourceQuote: After the East India Company was dissolved in 1798, the building served until 1808 as the seat of the colonial government of the Batavian Republic.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the East India Company was dissolved in 1798, the building served until 1808 as the seat of the colonial government of the Batavian Republic.

facts.text: Shipcrews were recruited here alongside meetings of the Heeren XVII Lords Seventeen regents.
facts.sourceQuote: The 20 regents of the Amsterdam chamber met here. In addition, the majority of meetings of the Heeren XVII (the Lords Seventeen), the regents of the East India Company, were also held at the Oost-Indisch Huis. Shipcrews were recruited here, and the archives and map collection of the East India Company were also kept here.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The 20 regents of the Amsterdam chamber met here. In addition, the majority of meetings of the Heeren XVII (the Lords Seventeen), the regents of the East India Company, were also held at the Oost-Indisch Huis. Shipcrews were recruited here, and the archives and map collection of the East India Company were also kept here.

facts.text: The Oost-Indisch Huis translates to East India House.
facts.sourceQuote: The Oost-Indisch Huis (Dutch for "East India House") is an early 17th-century building in the centre of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Oost-Indisch Huis (Dutch for "East India House") is an early 17th-century building in the centre of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Despite its age, the building holds official status as a listed Dutch national heritage site.
facts.sourceQuote: It is a listed Dutch national heritage site (rijksmonument).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is a listed Dutch national heritage site (rijksmonument).

features.opening: The Oost-Indisch Huis (Dutch for "East India House") is an early 17th-century building in the centre of Amsterdam.

features.name: Melkweg

facts.text: Melkweg first opened its doors as a cultural center on July 17, 1970.
facts.sourceQuote: The building was closed for a year, but reopened by Cor Schlösser and others as a cultural center, with its first event on July 17, 1970.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The building was closed for a year, but reopened by Cor Schlösser and others as a cultural center, with its first event on July 17, 1970.

facts.text: The Max hall expanded to hold 1,500 people in 2007.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1995, The Max opened, first with a capacity of 1,000 people, expanded to 1,500 in 2007.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1995, The Max opened, first with a capacity of 1,000 people, expanded to 1,500 in 2007.

facts.text: U2 played their first concert outside Ireland and the UK at Melkweg in October 1980.

features.name: Hollandsche Schouwburg

facts.text: Nazi occupiers designated the venue a Jewish theatre in 1941 before using it as a deportation center.
facts.sourceQuote: Originally, the Hollandsche Schouwburg was a Dutch theatre, but it was deemed a Jewish theatre in 1941 by Nazi occupiers, and it was later used as a deportation center during the Holocaust in the Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Originally, the Hollandsche Schouwburg was a Dutch theatre, but it was deemed a Jewish theatre in 1941 by Nazi occupiers, and it was later used as a deportation center during the Holocaust in the Netherlands.

facts.text: Teenager Lydia Riezouw secretly photographed prisoners from her window, including her friend Greetje Velleman.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1942, teenaged Lydia Riezouw took five photographs from her home window of the Jewish prisoners being held at Hollandsche Schouwburg, which included her Jewish friend Greetje Velleman.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1942, teenaged Lydia Riezouw took five photographs from her home window of the Jewish prisoners being held at Hollandsche Schouwburg, which included her Jewish friend Greetje Velleman.

facts.text: Staff at the nursery opposite saved many Jewish children, an act recorded by resistance member Betty Goudsmit-Oudkerk.
facts.sourceQuote: The illustrious personnel of the nursery opposite the Hollandsche Schouwburg located at the Plantage Middenlaan in Amsterdam saved many Jewish children. This is described in the book of resistance member Betty Goudsmit-Oudkerk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The illustrious personnel of the nursery opposite the Hollandsche Schouwburg located at the Plantage Middenlaan in Amsterdam saved many Jewish children. This is described in the book of resistance member Betty Goudsmit-Oudkerk.

features.opening: The Hollandsche Schouwburg (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈɦɔlɑntsə ˈsxʌubʏr(ə)x]; English: Hollandic Theatre) is a museum in Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

features.name: De Papegaai

facts.text: De Papegaai (The Parrot) was hidden behind a bird-trader's house when Catholicism was banned.
facts.sourceQuote: It is nicknamed "De Papegaai" (The Parrot) because it was originally hidden in a garden behind a regular housefront that belonged to a bird-trader in the days when Catholicism could not be practised publicly.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is nicknamed "De Papegaai" (The Parrot) because it was originally hidden in a garden behind a regular housefront that belonged to a bird-trader in the days when Catholicism could not be practised publicly.

facts.text: A perched parrot statue flanks the narrow Neo-Gothic facade alongside Saint Joseph.
facts.sourceQuote: Today there is a narrow, Neo-Gothic facade flanked by statues of Saint Joseph and a perched parrot.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Today there is a narrow, Neo-Gothic facade flanked by statues of Saint Joseph and a perched parrot.

features.opening: De Papegaai is the lesser of the two parochial churches in the St Nicholas Roman Catholic parish in Amsterdam.

features.name: De Dolphijn

facts.text: Hendrick de Keyser's classicist facade design was simplified by removing pilasters and cornices.
facts.sourceQuote: Er bestaat een ontwerptekening van de voorgevel door Hendrick de Keyser, maar dit ontwerp is niet geheel uitgevoerd: de gevel is versoberd door het schrappen van classicistische elementen als pilasters en kroonlijsten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There is a design drawing of the facade by Hendrick de Keyser, but this design has not been fully executed: the facade has been simplified by removing classicist elements such as pilasters and cornices.

facts.text: Construction occurred between 1599 and 1602, though the exact year remains unknown.
facts.sourceQuote: Het huis De Dolphijn is gebouwd rond 1600. Het precieze jaar is niet bekend; alleen dat het tussen 1599 en 1602 moet zijn geweest.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The De Dolphijn house was built around 1600. The exact year is not known; only that it must have been between 1599 and 1602.

facts.text: The poet Hendrik Laurensz Mirror commissioned this residence during his lifetime.

facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The client was the poet Hendrik Laurensz. Mirror (1549-1612).

features.opening: The house De Dolphijn is a canal house at Singel 140-142 in Amsterdam.

features.name: Kriterion

facts.text: About a thousand Jewish children were saved from the nursery school opposite the Hollandsche Schouwburg.
facts.sourceQuote: Samen met andere verzetsgroepen redde men ongeveer duizend Joodse kinderen uit de crèche tegenover de Hollandsche Schouwburg aan de Plantage Middenlaan, waar de kinderen verbleven in afwachting van transport naar Duitsland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Together with other resistance groups, about a thousand Jewish children were saved from the nursery school opposite the Hollandsche Schouwburg on Plantage Middenlaan, where the children were staying in anticipation of transport to Germany.

facts.text: The resistance group consisted largely of students forced to stop their studies due to war conditions.
facts.sourceQuote: De verzetsgroep bestond grotendeels uit studenten, die door de oorlogsomstandigheden gedwongen waren met hun studie te stoppen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The resistance group consisted largely of students, who were forced to stop their studies due to the war conditions.

facts.text: Piet Meerburg planned a theater where students could work and graduate without parental or government support.
facts.sourceQuote: Ruim voor het einde van de Tweede Wereldoorlog vatte de 25-jarige Meerburg het plan op om na de bevrijding een filmtheater te realiseren waar studenten konden werken, om alsnog te kunnen afstuderen zonder van hun ouders of de overheid afhankelijk te zijn.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Well before the end of World War II, the 25-year-old Meerburg conceived the plan to realize a movie theater after the liberation where students could work, so that they could still graduate without being dependent on their parents or the government.

facts.text: Kriterion emerged from student resistance activities during World War II.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is voortgekomen uit het studentenverzet tijdens de Tweede Wereldoorlog.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It emerged from the student resistance during World War II.

features.opening: Film theater Kriterion, officially the Association for Mutual Student Support Kriterion (V.O.S.S. Kriterion), is a student-run cinema and student association…

features.name: Oosterparkkerk

facts.text: The inauguration occurred on a working day within a closed circle to prevent disorder.
facts.sourceQuote: Omdat de doopsgezinde gemeente uit 5.000 leden bestond, ”had de kerkenraad, teneinde wanordelijkheden en teleurstelling te voorkomen, goedgevonden de eenvoudige plechtigheid op een werkdag en in besloten kring te doen plaats hebben.” Zowel de Kleine Courant als de Zondagsbode berichten over de opening.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because the Baptist church consisted of 5,000 members, "in order to prevent disorder and disappointment, the church council decided to hold the simple ceremony on a working day and in a closed circle." Both the Kleine Courant and the Zondagsbode report on the opening.

facts.text: Brown glazed brick bands and natural stone frames enliven the church's brick facades.
facts.sourceQuote: De bakstenen gevels zijn verlevendigd met banden van bruin verglaasde bakstenen en natuurstenen lijsten en ornamenten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The brick facades are enlivened with bands of brown glazed bricks and natural stone frames and ornaments.

facts.text: Corner facades sit slightly behind the roofline to create a small courtyard between fences.

facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The free facades on the corner are slightly behind the roofline, so that a small 'courtyard' is created between the wrought iron fences and the building. In this way, the church takes a recognizable place among the other buildings.

features.opening: The Oosterparkkerk stands on the west side of the Oosterpark in Amsterdam, in the Oosterparkbuurt.

features.name: Muiderpoort

facts.text: The original gate sank sixteen feet after slipping from its foundation in 1769.
facts.sourceQuote: In de nacht van 29 op 30 januari 1769 gleed de poort van zijn fundering en zakte zestien voet.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the night of January 29 to 30, 1769, the gate slipped from its foundation and sank sixteen feet.

facts.text: The exterior side features columns interrupted by bands, contrasting with the rustic background of the city-side pilasters.
facts.sourceQuote: De achtergrond van de pilasters is in rustica uitgevoerd. Aan de land- of buitenzijde zijn zuilen toegepast die door banden onderbroken worden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The background of the pilasters is executed in rustic style. Columns have been applied to the land or exterior side, which are interrupted by bands.

facts.text: The old city coat of arms on the city side depicts a medieval ship hull rather than the commonly assumed cannonball.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de landzijde is het nieuwe Amsterdamse stadswapen met de drie Andreaskruisen in het fronton aangebracht, aan de stadskant het oude stadswapen met een middeleeuws schip (een hulk en niet een kogge, zoals vaak wordt aangenomen).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the land side, the new Amsterdam city coat of arms with the three Andrew crosses is attached to the pediment, on the city side the old city coat of arms with a medieval ship (a hull and not a cannonball, as is often assumed).

facts.text: A raised central section crowned by an octagonal cupola tower sits above gate openings resembling a triumphal arch.
facts.sourceQuote: De poortopeningen suggereren een triomfboog. Het verhoogde middengedeelte met balustrade wordt bekroond door een achtkantige koepeltoren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The gate openings suggest a triumphal arch. The raised central section with balustrade is crowned by an octagonal cupola tower.

features.opening: The Muiderpoort in Amsterdam is a city gate on Alexanderplein, at the intersection of Plantage Middenlaan and Sarphatistraat.

Schippers, launched the campaign "Bouw es wat anders" to prevent this from happening. The city council was persuaded, and a good destination for the building was found in art center De Balie in 1982.
