facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Calvinist kerkeraad (church council) of the municipality, however, attempted to stop the theatre opening, but were only temporarily successful, for the theatre was in the end still opened on 3 January 1638, with Vondel's play.

features.opening: The Theatre of Van Campen (Dutch: Schouwburg van Van Campen, pronounced [ˈsxʌubʏr(ə)x fɑɱ vɑŋ ˈkɑmpə(n)]) was a theatre located at Keizersgracht 384 in…

features.name: Anne Frank House

facts.text: The rear extension is called the Achterhuis, meaning back house in Dutch.
facts.sourceQuote: The Achterhuis (Dutch for "back house") or Secret Annex – as it was called in The Diary of a Young Girl, an English translation of the diary – is the rear extension of the building.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Achterhuis (Dutch for "back house") or Secret Annex – as it was called in The Diary of a Young Girl, an English translation of the diary – is the rear extension of the building.

facts.text: A large radio used by those hiding was surrendered to Nazis in 1943 during confiscations.
facts.sourceQuote: The rear office held a large radio that the people in hiding used until 1943, after which the radio was handed in by the employees when the Nazis began confiscating Dutch radios.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The rear office held a large radio that the people in hiding used until 1943, after which the radio was handed in by the employees when the Nazis began confiscating Dutch radios.

facts.text: Despite only 450 square feet of space, Anne described the rooms as relatively luxurious.
facts.sourceQuote: Though the total amount of floor space in the inhabited rooms came to only about 450 square feet (42 m2), Anne Frank wrote in her diary that it was relatively luxurious compared to other hiding places they had heard about.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Though the total amount of floor space in the inhabited rooms came to only about 450 square feet (42 m2), Anne Frank wrote in her diary that it was relatively luxurious compared to other hiding places they had heard about.

facts.text: Miep Gies and Bep Voskuijl returned after the arrest to rescue personal belongings against police orders.
facts.sourceQuote: Before the building was cleared, Miep Gies and Bep Voskuijl, who had helped hide the families, returned to the hiding place against the orders of the Dutch police and rescued some personal effects.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Before the building was cleared, Miep Gies and Bep Voskuijl, who had helped hide the families, returned to the hiding place against the orders of the Dutch police and rescued some personal effects.

facts.text: In 2017, this site welcomed 1.27 million visitors.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2017, the museum had 1.27 million visitors and was the third most visited museum in the Netherlands, after the Van Gogh Museum and the Rijksmuseum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2017, the museum had 1.27 million visitors and was the third most visited museum in the Netherlands, after the Van Gogh Museum and the Rijksmuseum.

facts.text: Anne Frank and four others hid in rear rooms of this house before she died during the war.
facts.sourceQuote: During World War II, when the Netherlands was occupied by Germany, Anne Frank hid from Nazi persecution with her family and four other people in hidden rooms, in the rear building, of the 17th-century canal house, later known as the Secret Annex (Dutch: Achterhuis). She did not survive the war but her wartime diary was published in 1947.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During World War II, when the Netherlands was occupied by Germany, Anne Frank hid from Nazi persecution with her family and four other people in hidden rooms, in the rear building, of the 17th-century canal house, later known as the Secret Annex (Dutch: Achterhuis). She did not survive the war but her wartime diary was published in 1947.

features.opening: The Anne Frank House (Dutch: Anne Frank Huis) is a writer's house and biographical museum dedicated to Jewish wartime diarist Anne Frank.

features.name: Moskee El-Hijra

facts.text: A sculpture named Flying Bird by Wessel Couzijn once hung on the exterior wall.
facts.sourceQuote: Een door Wessel Couzijn in 1955 gemaakte sculptuur, Vliegende vogel, die sinds 1956 buiten aan de linker zijmuur van deze kerk hing, is hier verwijderd en herplaatst naar boven de ingang aan de Herengracht van de Doopsgezinde Singelkerk in het centrum van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A sculpture by Wessel Couzijn made in 1955, Flying bird, which has hung outside on the left side wall of this church since 1956, has been removed here and relocated above the entrance on the Herengracht of the Baptist Singelkerk in the center of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The original organ was crafted by Willem van Leeuwen in 1957.
facts.sourceQuote: Het in 1957 door Willem van Leeuwen gebouwde en in deze kerk geplaatste orgel is in 1996 overgenomen door de hervormde kerk in Sirjansland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The organ built by Willem van Leeuwen in 1957 and placed in this church was taken over by the Reformed Church in Sirjansland in 1996.

features.opening: The Olive Branch was built in 1956 as a Baptist church on Arthur van Schendelstraat in the garden city of Slotermeer in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

features.name: Concertgebouw

facts.text: 2,186 wooden piles drove 40 to 43 feet deep into the soil to support the structure.
facts.sourceQuote: A total of 2,186 wooden piles, 12 to 13 metres (40 to 43 ft) long, were emplaced in the soil.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A total of 2,186 wooden piles, 12 to 13 metres (40 to 43 ft) long, were emplaced in the soil.

facts.text: The grand opening was delayed until April 1888 due to municipal infrastructure issues.
facts.sourceQuote: The Concertgebouw was completed in late 1886, however due to the difficulties with the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel – filling in a small canal, paving the access roads and installing street lights – the grand opening of the building was delayed. The hall opened on 11 April 1888 with an inaugural concert, in which an orchestra of 120 musicians and a chorus of 500 singers participated, performing works of Wagner, Handel, Bach, and Beethoven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Concertgebouw was completed in late 1886, however due to the difficulties with the municipality of Nieuwer-Amstel – filling in a small canal, paving the access roads and installing street lights – the grand opening of the building was delayed. The hall opened on 11 April 1888 with an inaugural concert, in which an orchestra of 120 musicians and a chorus of 500 singers participated, performing works of Wagner, Handel, Bach, and Beethoven.

facts.text: An inaugural concert featured a massive ensemble of 120 musicians and 500 singers.
facts.sourceQuote: The hall opened on 11 April 1888 with an inaugural concert, in which an orchestra of 120 musicians and a chorus of 500 singers participated, performing works of Wagner, Handel, Bach, and Beethoven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The hall opened on 11 April 1888 with an inaugural concert, in which an orchestra of 120 musicians and a chorus of 500 singers participated, performing works of Wagner, Handel, Bach, and Beethoven.

facts.text: The Dutch name Concertgebouw translates directly to concert building.
facts.sourceQuote: The Dutch term "concertgebouw" translates into English as "concert building".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Dutch term "concertgebouw" translates into English as "concert building".

facts.text: Queen Beatrix granted the royal title Koninklijk on April 11, 2013.
facts.sourceQuote: In celebration of the building's 125th anniversary, Queen Beatrix bestowed the royal title "Koninklijk" upon the building on 11 April 2013, as she had on the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra upon its 100th in 1988.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In celebration of the building's 125th anniversary, Queen Beatrix bestowed the royal title "Koninklijk" upon the building on 11 April 2013, as she had on the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra upon its 100th in 1988.

features.opening: The Royal Concertgebouw (Dutch: het Koninklijk Concertgebouw, pronounced [ət ˈkoːnɪŋklə kɔnˈsɛrtxəˌbʌu]) is a concert hall in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

features.name: Dorpskerk Durgerdam

facts.text: A 17th-century oak baptismal canopy was shortened to fit inside the narrower modern nave.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook andere bouwelementen en voorwerpen stammen uit de oude kerk, dit zijn: De eikenhouten preekstoel, met knoppen van ebbenhout en met een koperen doopvont, uit 1646 Het doophek, eveneens van eikenhout en uit de 17e eeuw stammend, dat moest worden ingekort omdat de huidige kerk minder breed is Drie koperen kroonluchters, aangeschaft in 1666 en 1667, elk met zestien kaarshouders De luidklok van Pieter Hemony uit 1672 Een bord ter herinnering aan Gerrit Frederickszoon, een van de kapiteins in de Zeeslag bij Duins in 1639
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Other building elements and objects also come from the old church, these are: The oak pulpit, with ebony knobs and with a copper baptismal font, from 1646 The baptismal canopy, also made of oak and dating from the 17th century, which had to be shortened because the current church is less wide Three copper chandeliers, purchased in 1666 and 1667, each with sixteen candle holders Pieter Hemony's bell from 1672 A plaque in memory of Gerrit Frederickszoon, one of the captains in the Battle of the Sea at Duins in 1639

facts.text: A plaque honors Gerrit Frederickszoon, a captain in the 1639 Battle of the Sea at Duins.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook andere bouwelementen en voorwerpen stammen uit de oude kerk, dit zijn: De eikenhouten preekstoel, met knoppen van ebbenhout en met een koperen doopvont, uit 1646 Het doophek, eveneens van eikenhout en uit de 17e eeuw stammend, dat moest worden ingekort omdat de huidige kerk minder breed is Drie koperen kroonluchters, aangeschaft in 1666 en 1667, elk met zestien kaarshouders De luidklok van Pieter Hemony uit 1672 Een bord ter herinnering aan Gerrit Frederickszoon, een van de kapiteins in de Zeeslag bij Duins in 1639
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Other building elements and objects also come from the old church, these are: The oak pulpit, with ebony knobs and with a copper baptismal font, from 1646 The baptismal canopy, also made of oak and dating from the 17th century, which had to be shortened because the current church is less wide Three copper chandeliers, purchased in 1666 and 1667, each with sixteen candle holders Pieter Hemony's bell from 1672 A plaque in memory of Gerrit Frederickszoon, one of the captains in the Battle of the Sea at Duins in 1639

features.opening: The Dorpskerk Durgerdam, originally the Reformed church of Durgerdam, is the Protestant church of Durgerdam in Amsterdam-Noord.

features.name: Houten Huis

facts.text: The name Houten Huis means 'Wooden House' because it retains a rare wooden facade.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is een van de oudste huizen van Amsterdam en naast een pand aan het begin van de Zeedijk een van de twee overgebleven huizen met een houten voorgevel van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is one of the oldest houses in Amsterdam and, along with a building at the beginning of the Zeedijk, one of the two remaining houses with a wooden facade from Amsterdam.

facts.text: Research in 2012 corrected its age to 1528, disproving the long-held belief that it dated to 1420.
facts.sourceQuote: Er werd voorheen dan ook altijd aangenomen dat het pand uit 1420 stamde. Nader onderzoek gaf echter in 2012 de bouwdatum van 1528 of kort daarna.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was therefore always assumed that the building dates back to 1420. However, further research in 2012 gave the construction date of 1528 or shortly thereafter.

facts.text: Traditionally, only single women, originally beguines, were permitted to live within these walls.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Houten Huys staat op het Begijnhof en is van oudsher alleen bewoond door alleenstaande vrouwen (aanvankelijk begijnen, tegenwoordig is religieuze affiliatie niet meer verplicht).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Het Houten Huys is located on the Begijnhof and has traditionally been inhabited only by single women (originally beguines, today religious affiliation is no longer mandatory).

features.opening: Het Houten Huys is a building dating from 1528 or shortly thereafter on the Begijnhof in Amsterdam.

features.name: Elthetokerk

facts.text: Architect Kruyswijk also designed three other Amsterdam churches still in use today.
facts.sourceQuote: Drie andere door Kruyswijk ontworpen kerken in Amsterdam zijn nog wel in gebruik, dit zijn de Willem de Zwijgerkerk in Amsterdam-Zuid en twee kerken van het Apostolisch Genootschap, één aan de Archimedesweg in Amsterdam-Oost (Watergraafsmeer) en één aan de Clematisstraat in Amsterdam-Noord.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Three other churches designed by Kruyswijk in Amsterdam are still in use, these are the Willem de Zwijgerkerk in Amsterdam-Zuid and two churches of the Apostolic Society, one on the Archimedesweg in Amsterdam-Oost (Watergraafsmeer) and one on the Clematisstraat in Amsterdam-North.

facts.text: Construction funding of ƒ 150,000 was gathered between 1924 and 1929.
facts.sourceQuote: Voor de bouw was tussen 1924 en 1929 een bedrag van ƒ 150.000 bijeengebracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: An amount of ƒ 150,000 was raised between 1924 and 1929 for the construction.

facts.text: Cornelis Kruyswijk designed the structure built in 1929.
facts.sourceQuote: De kerk is gebouwd in 1929 naar ontwerp van Cornelis Kruyswijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church was built in 1929 to the design of Cornelis Kruyswijk.

features.opening: The former Elthetokerk was a Reformed church building at the corner of Insulindeweg and Kramatweg in the Indische Buurt in Amsterdam-Oost.

features.name: Begijnhofkapel

facts.text: Unmarried women lived there without lifelong vows, keeping their own possessions and leaving anytime to marry.
facts.sourceQuote: They were unmarried women who made a vow of chastity and promised obedience to the parish priest, but since they were not expected to make a vow of poverty, they were free to dispose of their own possessions as they wished. They could renounce their vows at any moment and leave the Beguinage, for instance, to get married.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were unmarried women who made a vow of chastity and promised obedience to the parish priest, but since they were not expected to make a vow of poverty, they were free to dispose of their own possessions as they wished. They could renounce their vows at any moment and leave the Beguinage, for instance, to get married.

facts.text: A house was ceded to the community on St Peter's Eve in 1346 by a man named Cope van der Laene.
facts.sourceQuote: Another document, dated 31 July 1346, speaks of the Beghijnhuis (house of the Beguines) ceded to them by one Cope van der Laene on St Peter’s Eve.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Another document, dated 31 July 1346, speaks of the Beghijnhuis (house of the Beguines) ceded to them by one Cope van der Laene on St Peter’s Eve.

facts.text: The Begijnhofkapel honors Saint John and Saint Ursula as its dedicated patrons.
facts.sourceQuote: The Begijnhof Chapel, dedicated to Saint John and Saint Ursula, is a Roman Catholic chapel run by the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament, in the St Nicholas Parish of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Begijnhof Chapel, dedicated to Saint John and Saint Ursula, is a Roman Catholic chapel run by the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament, in the St Nicholas Parish of Amsterdam.

facts.text: A yearly procession for the Miracle of Amsterdam begins at this church.
facts.sourceQuote: The Miracle of Amsterdam is commemorated yearly with a procession starting from this church.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Miracle of Amsterdam is commemorated yearly with a procession starting from this church.

features.opening: The Begijnhof Chapel, dedicated to Saint John and Saint Ursula, is a Roman Catholic chapel run by the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament, in the St Nicholas…

features.name: Pianola Museum

facts.text: Pianola history runs parallel to silent films, leading to performances with old footage.
facts.sourceQuote: De geschiedenis van de pianola loopt parallel met die van de stomme film. Al jarenlang organiseert het museum voorstellingen met oude filmbeelden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The history of the pianola runs parallel to that of the silent film. For years, the museum has been organizing performances with old film footage.

facts.text: Theo de Boer and Kasper Janse founded the foundation managing the collection in 1981.
facts.sourceQuote: Door Theo de Boer en Kasper Janse werd in 1981 de Stichting Nederlands Piano Museum opgericht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1981, Theo de Boer and Kasper Janse founded the Stichting Nederlands Piano Museum.

facts.text: The pianola was a self-playing instrument built between 1900 and around 1935.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Pianola Museum in de Jordaan is een muziekmuseum in Amsterdam dat een overzicht biedt van de geschiedenis en de manier van spelen van de pianola, een 'zelfspelend' muziekinstrument dat tussen 1900 en circa 1935 werd gebouwd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Pianola Museum in the Jordaan is a music museum in Amsterdam that offers an overview of the history and playing method of the pianola, a 'self-playing' musical instrument that was built between 1900 and around 1935.

features.opening: The Pianola Museum in the Jordaan is a music museum in Amsterdam that offers an overview of the history and way of playing the pianola, a 'self-playing'…

features.name: Lekstraatsynagoge

facts.text: The Lekstraatsynagoge was officially inaugurated on November 30, 1937.
facts.sourceQuote: De plannen ontstonden in het begin van de jaren 30, in 1932 was het ontwerp klaar en op 30 november 1937 werd de Lekstraatsynagoge ingewijd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The plans were conceived in the early 1930s, the design was completed in 1932 and the Lekstraatsynagoge was inaugurated on November 30, 1937.

facts.text: Jewish residents in the area grew from 4,000 in 1930 to approximately 17,000 by 1940.
facts.sourceQuote: Omdat er steeds meer Joodse bewoners kwamen - van 4000 in 1930 tot rond de 17.000 in 1940 - wilde men een echte sjoel (synagoge) bouwen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because more and more Jewish residents were coming - from 4000 in 1930 to around 17,000 in 1940 - they wanted to build a real synagogue (synagogue).

facts.text: During WWII, Jews could purchase Star of David symbols at Lekstraatsynagoge.
facts.sourceQuote: Tijdens de Tweede Wereldoorlog konden joden in de Lekstraatsynagoge gele Davidsterren kopen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During World War II, Jews could buy the Star of David in the Lekstraatsynagoge.

facts.text: From 1943, the building stored furniture belonging to deported Jews after closing.
facts.sourceQuote: Later sloot de synagoge haar deuren, en vanaf 1943 deed het gebouw dienst als opslagplaats van meubels van weggevoerde joden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Later, the synagogue closed its doors, and from 1943, the building served as a storage facility for furniture belonging to deported Jews.

features.opening: The Lekstraat Synagogue stands at Lekstraat 63 in the Rivierenbuurt in Amsterdam.

features.name: Djame Masdjied Taibah

facts.text: Locals proudly call it 'the pearl of the Bijlmer' due to its distinctive look.
facts.sourceQuote: Many visitors and residents are proud to call the building and therefore 'the pearl of the Bijlmer‟.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Many visitors and residents are proud to call the building and therefore 'the pearl of the Bijlmer‟.

facts.text: The prayer leader is Hazrat Allama Mufti Shafiq-ur-Rehman Mishabi Noorani.
facts.sourceQuote: Hazrat Allama Mufti Shafiq-ur-Rehman Mishabi Noorani, a Barelvi graduate from Jamia Ashrafia, Mubarakpur is prayer leader (Imam) of the mosque.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Hazrat Allama Mufti Shafiq-ur-Rehman Mishabi Noorani, a Barelvi graduate from Jamia Ashrafia, Mubarakpur is prayer leader (Imam) of the mosque.

features.opening: The Taibah Mosque is a (Indo-Surinamese) mosque in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

features.name: Eye Filmmuseum

facts.text: Weekly screenings began in the 1950s at the Stedelijk Museum under the concept of cinema as a seventh art.
facts.sourceQuote: The second gallery space is dedicated to experimental cinema or expanded cinema, a commitment which dates back to the Filmmuseum's founding and the weekly screenings it organized at the Stedelijk Museum in the 1950s under the emerging aegis of cinema as a "seventh art." Past exhibitions in this space have focused on auteurs and cinematographers, as well as video artists and visual artists like Ryoji Ikeda and Anthony McCall.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The second gallery space is dedicated to experimental cinema or expanded cinema, a commitment which dates back to the Filmmuseum's founding and the weekly screenings it organized at the Stedelijk Museum in the 1950s under the emerging aegis of cinema as a "seventh art." Past exhibitions in this space have focused on auteurs and cinematographers, as well as video artists and visual artists like Ryoji Ikeda and Anthony McCall.

facts.text: Eye restored the lost 1922 silent film Beyond the Rocks starring Gloria Swanson.
facts.sourceQuote: Recent silent film Eye restorations include the formerly lost film Beyond the Rocks (1922) starring Gloria Swanson, J'accuse! (1919) by Abel Gance, The Seashell and the Clergyman (1928) by Germain Dulac, Raskolnikov (1923) by Robert Wiene, Flower of Evil (1915) by Carmine Gallone, and Shoes (1916) by Lois Weber.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Recent silent film Eye restorations include the formerly lost film Beyond the Rocks (1922) starring Gloria Swanson, J'accuse! (1919) by Abel Gance, The Seashell and the Clergyman (1928) by Germain Dulac, Raskolnikov (1923) by Robert Wiene, Flower of Evil (1915) by Carmine Gallone, and Shoes (1916) by Lois Weber.

features.opening: Eye Filmmuseum is a film archive, museum, and cinema in Amsterdam that preserves and presents both Dutch and foreign films screened in the Netherlands.

features.name: Zuiderkerk

facts.text: Architect Hendrick de Keyser designed the church and was buried there in 1621.
facts.sourceQuote: The design of the church in Amsterdam Renaissance style is by Hendrick de Keyser, who was also buried in the church in 1621.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The design of the church in Amsterdam Renaissance style is by Hendrick de Keyser, who was also buried in the church in 1621.

facts.text: During the 1944 hunger winter, the church served as a temporary morgue for the dead.
facts.sourceQuote: During the final (1944-1945) winter of World War II, known as the hongerwinter ("hunger winter") in the Netherlands because food was so scarce, the church was in use as a temporary morgue because people were dying faster than they could be buried.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the final (1944-1945) winter of World War II, known as the hongerwinter ("hunger winter") in the Netherlands because food was so scarce, the church was in use as a temporary morgue because people were dying faster than they could be buried.

facts.text: Three of Rembrandt's children were buried inside this church near his former home.
facts.sourceQuote: Three of Rembrandt's children were buried in the Zuiderkerk, which is very near to Rembrandt's house in the Jodenbreestraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Three of Rembrandt's children were buried in the Zuiderkerk, which is very near to Rembrandt's house in the Jodenbreestraat.

facts.text: The Wall of Fame honors Dutch celebrities like Johan Cruijff and Inge de Bruijn.
facts.sourceQuote: Since June 2006, the church also houses the "Wall of Fame", a homage to Dutch celebrities who have made a positive contribution to society, such as charitable work. The honourees include Amsterdam mayor Job Cohen, renowned former soccer player Johan Cruijff and four-time Olympic swimming champion Inge de Bruijn.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since June 2006, the church also houses the "Wall of Fame", a homage to Dutch celebrities who have made a positive contribution to society, such as charitable work. The honourees include Amsterdam mayor Job Cohen, renowned former soccer player Johan Cruijff and four-time Olympic swimming champion Inge de Bruijn.

facts.text: Claude Monet painted the Zuiderkerk as a subject of his work.
facts.sourceQuote: The church played an important part in the life of Rembrandt and was the subject of a painting by Claude Monet.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church played an important part in the life of Rembrandt and was the subject of a painting by Claude Monet.

features.opening: The Zuiderkerk (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈzœydərˌkɛr(ə)k], "southern church") is a 17th-century Reformed Protestant church in the Nieuwmarkt area of Amsterdam,…

features.name: Allendemonument

facts.text: Ton Blommerde stacked concrete parts without adhesive, inspired by Inca methods.
facts.sourceQuote: Blommerde, die zich ook wel bediende van de naam Blommende, liet zich inspireren door de Inca's, hij stapelde de betonnen delen zonder voegmiddel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Blommerde, who also used the name Blommende, was inspired by the Incas, he stacked the concrete parts without adhesive.

facts.text: A plaque erroneously claims Allende was murdered, though he actually committed suicide.
facts.sourceQuote: Lang werd gedacht dat hij vermoord zou zijn (deze tekst staat dus abusievelijk op de plaquette). In 2011 werd na uitgebreid onderzoek officieel meegedeeld dat hij zelfmoord pleegde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For a long time it was thought that he had been murdered (this text is therefore erroneously on the plaque). In 2011, after extensive research, it was officially announced that he committed suicide.

features.opening: The Allendemonument is a statue/monument in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

features.name: Theater Amsterdam

facts.text: The venue opened on May 8, 2014 with a performance titled Anne based on Anne Frank's diary.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 8 mei 2014 opende het theater met de voorstelling Anne, naar het dagboek van Anne Frank.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On May 8, 2014, the theater opened with the performance Anne, based on the diary of Anne Frank.

features.opening: Theater Amsterdam is a theater in Amsterdam.

features.name: Koningin Emma

facts.text: Vandals stripped the statue of its head and shoulders in September 1987 before it was restored.
facts.sourceQuote: In september 1987 werd het beeld door vandalen ontdaan van hoofd en schouders. Spoedig nadat het vorstelijk hoofd in de bosjes werd aangetroffen, werd het beeld hersteld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In September 1987, the statue was stripped of its head and shoulders by vandals. Shortly after the princely head was found in the woods, the statue was restored.

facts.text: The statue was created by sculptor Lambertus Zijl, who lived from 1866 to 1947.
facts.sourceQuote: Het beeld is ontworpen door beeldhouwer Lambertus Zijl (1866 - 1947) en werd onthuld in 1938.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The statue was designed by sculptor Lambertus Zijl (1866 - 1947) and was unveiled in 1938.

facts.text: Koningin Emma received its public unveiling in the year 1938.
facts.sourceQuote: Het beeld is ontworpen door beeldhouwer Lambertus Zijl (1866 - 1947) en werd onthuld in 1938.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The statue was designed by sculptor Lambertus Zijl (1866 - 1947) and was unveiled in 1938.

features.opening: Statue and memorial in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

features.name: National Monument

facts.text: A temporary monument with eleven soil urns stood on the square from 1947 until the permanent one was revealed.
facts.sourceQuote: While planning was ongoing, a temporary monument was erected on the Dam in 1947, designed by A. J. van de Steur and Auke Komter. It consisted of 11 urns with soil from World War II execution grounds and war cemeteries in each of the Dutch provinces.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: While planning was ongoing, a temporary monument was erected on the Dam in 1947, designed by A. J. van de Steur and Auke Komter. It consisted of 11 urns with soil from World War II execution grounds and war cemeteries in each of the Dutch provinces.

facts.text: During a 1990s restoration the entire structure was disassembled to replace its brick interior with concrete.
facts.sourceQuote: The monument has undergone two restorations, in 1965 and in 1997–1998. During the restoration in the 1990s, the entire monument was disassembled, and the brick interior of the central pillar was replaced with concrete.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The monument has undergone two restorations, in 1965 and in 1997–1998. During the restoration in the 1990s, the entire monument was disassembled, and the brick interior of the central pillar was replaced with concrete.

facts.text: A 22-metre white travertine pillar forms the monument's central concrete cone.
facts.sourceQuote: The central element of the monument is a concrete conical pillar 22 metres (72 ft) in height, covered entirely by white travertine stone.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The central element of the monument is a concrete conical pillar 22 metres (72 ft) in height, covered entirely by white travertine stone.

facts.text: Dutch architect Jacobus Oud designed the structure while sculptor John Rädecker created its figures.
facts.sourceQuote: The monument was designed by Dutch architect Jacobus Oud; the monument's sculptures are by John Rädecker and his sons Han and Jan Willem Rädecker.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The monument was designed by Dutch architect Jacobus Oud; the monument's sculptures are by John Rädecker and his sons Han and Jan Willem Rädecker.

facts.text: Eleven urns hold soil from execution grounds across Dutch provinces plus one from Indonesia.
facts.sourceQuote: The wall contains eleven urns with soil from World War II execution grounds and war cemeteries in each of the Dutch provinces. and a twelfth urn with soil from the Dutch East Indies, present-day Indonesia.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The wall contains eleven urns with soil from World War II execution grounds and war cemeteries in each of the Dutch provinces. and a twelfth urn with soil from the Dutch East Indies, present-day Indonesia.

facts.text: Willem Bogtman's painted ceiling and stained-glass windows were restored to their original state.

facts.text: The University of Amsterdam was born within these walls.

facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church, dedicated to the martyr Sint Agnes, was built between 1919 and 1932 according to a design by architect Jan Stuyt and was designated a Rijksmonument in 1996.

facts.text: Construction of the building took place between 1919 and 1932.

facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Embassy of the Free Mind was opened in October 2017 by author Dan Brown.

facts.text: Amsterdam businessman Joost Ritman founded the collection as a private library in 1958.

facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is a scientific research library with a collection of 25,000 books and its own publisher, and dates to 1958—when Amsterdam-based businessman Joost Ritman started it as a private library.

facts.text: The collection includes alchemical, astrological, and kabbalistic texts alongside Rosicrucian images.

facts.text: Over two million visitors have explored the exhibition since it opened in 1985.
facts.sourceQuote: According to the museum, more than two million visitors have visited the exhibition since it opened in 1985.

facts.text: A second location named Hash Marihuana Cáñamo & Hemp Museum opened in Barcelona in 2012.

facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2012 the museum opened a second location in Barcelona, the Hash Marihuana Cáñamo & Hemp Museum.

facts.text: An 1836 Dutch Bible printed entirely on hemp paper is part of the collection.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum includes a live cannabis garden in various stages of growth, pipe and roach clip collections, an 1836 Dutch Bible made of hemp, and many other accessories made from the industrial crop.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The museum includes a live cannabis garden in various stages of growth, pipe and roach clip collections, an 1836 Dutch Bible made of hemp, and many other accessories made from the industrial crop.

facts.text: A 1660 painting by David Teniers the Younger depicts peasants smoking in a smoke house.
facts.sourceQuote: The museum also contains artwork, including David Teniers the Younger's painting, Hemp-Smoking Peasants in a Smoke House (1660), and one of the fake I.D's of the famous cannabis smuggler Howard Marks.

features.name: Thomaskerk

facts.text: A wavy roof symbolizes the sea where God led Israelites through under Moses.
facts.sourceQuote: De zandstenen vloer is een verwijzing naar de tocht van het volk Israël door de woestijn en het golvende dak symboliseert de zee waar God de Israëlieten onder leiding van Mozes doorheen leidde. twaalf vierkante ruiten verwijzen naar de twaalf apostelen, voorts is er in het plafond een prisma met raam zichtbaar, verwijzend naar de drie-eenheid.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The sandstone floor is a reference to the journey of the people of Israel through the desert and the wavy roof symbolizes the sea where God led the Israelites through under the leadership of Moses. twelve square windows refer to the twelve apostles, furthermore there is a prism with window visible in the ceiling, referring to the Trinity.

facts.text: Architect Karel Sijmons paid for a 1967 crucifixion window by Antonio Saura himself.
facts.sourceQuote: De kerk heeft een glas-in-loodraam dat in 1967 ontworpen is door de Spaanse kunstenaar Antonio Saura waarin de kruisiging van Jezus wordt afgebeeld. De architect heeft het zelf betaald omdat hij het stuk per se in de kerk wilde hebben.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church has a stained glass window designed in 1967 by the Spanish artist Antonio Saura depicting the crucifixion of Jesus. The architect paid for it himself because he absolutely wanted to have the piece in the church.

facts.text: Sijmons could not enjoy the church's special muted acoustics because he was almost deaf.
facts.sourceQuote: De Amsterdamkalender 2024 maakte melding van een gedempte akoestiek, die de concerten bijzonder maken. Sijmons kon daar niet van genieten; hij was (bijna) doof.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Amsterdam calendar 2024 reported on a muted acoustics, which makes the concerts special. Sijmons could not enjoy that; he was (almost) deaf.

facts.text: The architect drew inspiration from Le Corbusier's Notre Dame du Haut chapel with its wavy roof.
facts.sourceQuote: De architect liet zich inspireren door de kapel Notre Dame du Haut in het Franse Ronchamp van architect Le Corbusier. Deze kapel heeft ook een golvend dak.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The architect was inspired by the Notre Dame du Haut chapel in the French Ronchamp by architect Le Corbusier. This chapel also has a wavy roof.

facts.text: A concrete structure hung on the facade serves as a bell tower rather than an actual tower.
facts.sourceQuote: Een van de weinige tekenen van de stijl aan de buitenkant is de “klokkentoren”, hier geen daadwerkelijk toren, maar een betonnen geheel dat aan de gevel gehangen is.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: One of the few signs of the style on the outside is the "bell tower", here no actual tower, but a concrete structure hung on the facade.

facts.text: Interior walls, stairs, and pulpit are rough concrete with framing relief and hardly any decoration.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de binnenzijde is het een en al beton met door de bekisting nagelaten reliëf, slechts onderbroken door grof hout. De betonnen wanden, trappen, kansel, balustrades voor het orgel en doopvont zijn in die vorm dus nauwelijks afgewerkt of verfraaid.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the inside it is all concrete with relief left by the framing, only interrupted by rough wood. The concrete walls, stairs, pulpit, balustrades for the organ and baptismal font are therefore hardly finished or decorated in that form.

features.opening: The Thomaskerk, or De Thomas, on the Prinses Irenestraat in Amsterdam-Zuid was built in 1966 and belongs to the Protestant Church of Amsterdam.

features.name: International Institute of Social History

facts.text: Most archives were stolen by Nazi agents and stored in Germany for a planned party school.
facts.sourceQuote: During the war, most remaining IISG archives were transported to Nazi Germany between June 1942 and September 1944 by agents of the Reichsleiter Rosenberg Taskforce led by Eberhard Kautter. They were not destroyed, but stored for eventual inclusion in the Advanced School of the NSDAP.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the war, most remaining IISG archives were transported to Nazi Germany between June 1942 and September 1944 by agents of the Reichsleiter Rosenberg Taskforce led by Eberhard Kautter. They were not destroyed, but stored for eventual inclusion in the Advanced School of the NSDAP.

facts.text: Some lost papers were rediscovered in Moscow in 1991 before being returned to Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: Most of the papers were rediscovered in Hannover in 1946, and some other parts were later found in archives in Moscow in 1991, and returned to Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Most of the papers were rediscovered in Hannover in 1946, and some other parts were later found in archives in Moscow in 1991, and returned to Amsterdam.

facts.text: The Press Museum moved out in 2017 to become part of the Dutch Institute for Image and Sound.
facts.sourceQuote: This building also housed the Press Museum but in 2017 that museum became a part of the Dutch Institute for Image and Sound (Nederlands Instituut voor Beeld en Geluid) in Hilversum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This building also housed the Press Museum but in 2017 that museum became a part of the Dutch Institute for Image and Sound (Nederlands Instituut voor Beeld en Geluid) in Hilversum.

facts.text: The International Institute of Social History was established as an independent scientific institute in 1935.
facts.sourceQuote: The IISH was founded in 1935 by Nicolaas Posthumus as an independent scientific institute.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The IISH was founded in 1935 by Nicolaas Posthumus as an independent scientific institute.

features.opening: The International Institute of Social History (IISH/IISG) is one of the largest archives of labor and social history in the world.

features.name: Boomkerk

facts.text: Concerts resumed on the monumental organ dating back to 1774 after the building was restored.
facts.sourceQuote: Op het monumentale orgel uit 1774 wordt na de restauratie weer geconcerteerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the restoration, concerts will again be held on the monumental organ from 1774.

features.opening: De Boom, or Boomkerk, is the usual name for the Roman Catholic Church of St Francis of Assisi in Amsterdam Bos en Lommer.

features.name: Amsterdam Public Library Oosterdok

facts.text: After the PTT left, almost all existing buildings were demolished to make way for new construction after 2003.
facts.sourceQuote: De PTT vertrok er na nog geen halve eeuw en de gemeente Amsterdam begon de terreinen te herontwikkelen. (Bijna) Alle bestaande gebouwen werden daarbij gesloopt en er kwam na 2003 nieuwbouw naar een stratenplan van Erick van Egeraat met relatief hoge gebouwen en nauwe straatjes daartussen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The PTT left after less than half a century and the municipality of Amsterdam began redeveloping the sites. (Almost) All existing buildings were demolished and new buildings were built after 2003 according to a street plan by Erick van Egeraat with relatively high buildings and narrow streets between them.

facts.text: New structures rose on a street plan by Erick van Egeraat featuring relatively high buildings and narrow streets.
facts.sourceQuote: De PTT vertrok er na nog geen halve eeuw en de gemeente Amsterdam begon de terreinen te herontwikkelen. (Bijna) Alle bestaande gebouwen werden daarbij gesloopt en er kwam na 2003 nieuwbouw naar een stratenplan van Erick van Egeraat met relatief hoge gebouwen en nauwe straatjes daartussen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The PTT left after less than half a century and the municipality of Amsterdam began redeveloping the sites. (Almost) All existing buildings were demolished and new buildings were built after 2003 according to a street plan by Erick van Egeraat with relatively high buildings and narrow streets between them.

features.name: Wereldmuseum Amsterdam

facts.text: Researchers originally studied the colony to improve production of coffee beans, rattan, and paraffin.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1871 the institute began research to increase profits made off the colonies. This included attempting to develop improved means of producing coffee beans, rattan and paraffin.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1871 the institute began research to increase profits made off the colonies. This included attempting to develop improved means of producing coffee beans, rattan and paraffin.

facts.text: A children's wing added in the early 1970s is now known as Tropenmuseum Junior.
facts.sourceQuote: In the early 1970s a new wing for children was added. This wing is now called Tropenmuseum Junior.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the early 1970s a new wing for children was added. This wing is now called Tropenmuseum Junior.

facts.text: The institution began in Haarlem in 1864 as the Koloniaal Museum before moving to Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: It was originally founded in Haarlem, Netherlands in 1864 under the name Koloniaal Museum (English: Colonial Museum) and later renamed Tropenmuseum (English: Museum of the Tropics).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was originally founded in Haarlem, Netherlands in 1864 under the name Koloniaal Museum (English: Colonial Museum) and later renamed Tropenmuseum (English: Museum of the Tropics).

facts.text: Wereldmuseum Amsterdam was called Tropenmuseum (Museum of the Tropics) from 1950 until 2023.
facts.sourceQuote: The Wereldmuseum Amsterdam, previously known as Tropenmuseum between 1950 and 2023, is an ethnographic museum with its headquarters in Amsterdam, Netherlands. It was originally founded in Haarlem, Netherlands in 1864 under the name Koloniaal Museum (English: Colonial Museum) and later renamed Tropenmuseum (English: Museum of the Tropics).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Wereldmuseum Amsterdam, previously known as Tropenmuseum between 1950 and 2023, is an ethnographic museum with its headquarters in Amsterdam, Netherlands. It was originally founded in Haarlem, Netherlands in 1864 under the name Koloniaal Museum (English: Colonial Museum) and later renamed Tropenmuseum (English: Museum of the Tropics).

features.opening: The Wereldmuseum Amsterdam, previously known as Tropenmuseum between 1950 and 2023, is an ethnographic museum with its headquarters in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

features.name: Singelkerk

facts.text: A major 1839 renovation replaced the roof and Herengracht facade with their current form.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1839 wordt bij een grote verbouwing door Martinus Gerardus Tétar van Elven het dak vervangen, waarmee het gebouw de vorm krijgt die het nu nog heeft. Ook de voorgevel aan de Herengracht dateert uit die tijd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1839, during a major renovation by Martinus Gerardus Tétar van Elven, the roof was replaced, giving the building the shape it still has today. The facade on the Herengracht also dates from that time.

facts.text: The Singelkerk is a hidden church that cannot be recognized as a church from the outside.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is een zogenaamde schuilkerk, een kerk die aan de buitenkant niet herkenbaar is als kerk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is a so-called hidden church, a church that is not recognizable as a church from the outside.

features.opening: The Singelkerk is a church of the Mennonite congregation in Amsterdam, lying between the Singel and the Herengracht.

features.name: Homomonument

facts.text: Police removed a wreath from the National Monument in 1970, declaring it insulting to the dead.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1970, a year before the complete decriminalization of homosexuality in the Netherlands, a group of gay activists were arrested for trying to lay a wreath at the National Monument to the Victims of World War II on Dam Square, Amsterdam. The flowers were removed from the memorial by the police and declared insulting to the memory of the dead.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1970, a year before the complete decriminalization of homosexuality in the Netherlands, a group of gay activists were arrested for trying to lay a wreath at the National Monument to the Victims of World War II on Dam Square, Amsterdam. The flowers were removed from the memorial by the police and declared insulting to the memory of the dead.

facts.text: Activist Jef Last once proposed a monument stating no flame burns for unknown homophiles.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1961, activist Jef Last suggested a 'monument to the unknown gay': "No one knows how many there were, no statistics indicate how many of them were beaten to death in those camps or starved or otherwise succumbed. No flame burns for unknown homophiles".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1961, activist Jef Last suggested a 'monument to the unknown gay': "No one knows how many there were, no statistics indicate how many of them were beaten to death in those camps or starved or otherwise succumbed. No flame burns for unknown homophiles".

facts.text: Three pink granite triangles connect to form one large triangle with a 36-meter side.
facts.sourceQuote: The memorial is a composition of three equilateral triangles of pink granite with edge lengths of 10 meters, which are interconnected by thin lines of similar material, thus forming one large equilateral triangle with a side length of 36 meters.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The memorial is a composition of three equilateral triangles of pink granite with edge lengths of 10 meters, which are interconnected by thin lines of similar material, thus forming one large equilateral triangle with a side length of 36 meters.

facts.text: A triangle on the canal points directly at Dam Square where the WWII national monument stands.
facts.sourceQuote: The top of the triangle, projecting into the canal, points to Dam Square, where the National Monument to the Victims of World War II is located.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The top of the triangle, projecting into the canal, points to Dam Square, where the National Monument to the Victims of World War II is located.

facts.text: Visitors often sit on steps near the water while flowers and candles are regularly laid there.
facts.sourceQuote: Here people can often be seen sitting on the steps, and on the platform resting near the water, flowers are regularly laid and candles are lit.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Here people can often be seen sitting on the steps, and on the platform resting near the water, flowers are regularly laid and candles are lit.

features.opening: The Homomonument is a memorial in the centre of Amsterdam, the capital of the Netherlands.

features.name: Nieuwendammerkerk

facts.text: A smaller church was replaced by this hall church built between 1848 and 1849.
facts.sourceQuote: De Nieuwendammerkerk is een zaalkerk, gebouwd in 1848-1849, ter vervanging van een kleiner en ouder kerkgebouw.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Nieuwendammerkerk is a hall church, built in 1848-1849, to replace a smaller and older church building.

features.opening: The Nieuwendammerkerk is the village church of the dyke village of Nieuwendam in Amsterdam-Noord.

features.name: West Indian Warehouse

facts.text: The WIC used this site as its headquarters for trade in gold, sugar, and slaves.
facts.sourceQuote: Tussen 1647 en 1674 diende het pand als hoofdkwartier van de WIC. Vanuit dit pand waren de bevelhebbers verantwoordelijk voor alle handelsactiviteiten, waaronder de handel in goud, suiker en slaven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1647 and 1674, the building served as the headquarters of the WIC. From this building, the commanders were responsible for all trade activities, including the trade in gold, sugar and slaves.

facts.text: Commanders ran New Amsterdam from here until the English took over in 1664.
facts.sourceQuote: Vanaf 1647 waren zij ook formeel verantwoordelijk voor het reilen en zeilen van Nieuw-Amsterdam, tot de nederzetting in 1664 door de Engelsen werd ingenomen en de naam New York kreeg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1647 onwards, they were also formally responsible for the running of New Amsterdam, until the settlement was taken over by the English in 1664 and the name New York was given.

facts.text: From 1647, these commanders were formally responsible for running New Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: Vanaf 1647 waren zij ook formeel verantwoordelijk voor het reilen en zeilen van Nieuw-Amsterdam, tot de nederzetting in 1664 door de Engelsen werd ingenomen en de naam New York kreeg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1647 onwards, they were also formally responsible for the running of New Amsterdam, until the settlement was taken over by the English in 1664 and the name New York was given.

facts.text: The facade letters GWC stand for the Geoctroyeerde West-Indische Compagnie.
facts.sourceQuote: De letters GWC op de gevel staan voor de officiële naam, 'Geoctroyeerde West-Indische Compagnie'.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The letters GWC on the facade stand for the official name, 'Geoctroyeerde West-Indische Compagnie'.

features.opening: The West Indian Warehouse in Amsterdam dates back to 1642 and is located on the western part of Rapenburg, where the Oudeschans flows into the Oosterdok.

features.name: Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder

facts.text: Catholics built this clandestine church on the top three floors during the 1660s.
facts.sourceQuote: The Catholic church was built on the top three floors of the canal house during the 1660s. It is an important example of a "schuilkerk", or "clandestine church" in which Catholics and other religious dissenters from the seventeenth-century Dutch Reformed Church, unable to worship in public, held services.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Catholic church was built on the top three floors of the canal house during the 1660s. It is an important example of a "schuilkerk", or "clandestine church" in which Catholics and other religious dissenters from the seventeenth-century Dutch Reformed Church, unable to worship in public, held services.

facts.text: Since April 28, 1888, the hidden church has operated as a museum for eighty-five thousand visitors yearly.
facts.sourceQuote: The church has been open as a museum since 28 April 1888, and has 85,000 visitors annually.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church has been open as a museum since 28 April 1888, and has 85,000 visitors annually.

facts.text: Between 1661 and 1663, the top three floors became a hidden house church.
facts.sourceQuote: Between 1661 and 1663 the top three floors of the house were changed into a house church.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1661 and 1663 the top three floors of the house were changed into a house church.

features.opening: Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder (OLHOS; English: Our Lord in the Attic) is a 17th-century canal house, house church, and museum in the city center of Amsterdam, The…

features.name: Vredeskerk

facts.text: Vredeskerk means 'Peace Church' and honors Our Lady Queen of Peace, a devotion popular after World War I.
facts.sourceQuote: Als beschermheilige werd Onze-Lieve-Vrouwe Koningin van de Vrede gekozen. De devotie tot de Maagd Maria als Koningin van de Vrede was zeer populair in de jaren tijdens en na de Eerste Wereldoorlog.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Our Lady Queen of Peace was chosen as the patron saint. The devotion to the Virgin Mary as Queen of Peace was very popular in the years during and after World War I.

features.opening: The Parish Church of Our Lady Queen of Peace or Vredeskerk is a Roman Catholic church between Pijnackerstraat and Van Hilligaertstraat in the southwest corner…

facts.text: The Mozes en Aäronkerk takes its name from the two adjacent houses, 'Moyses' and 'Aäron', purchased to house the church.
facts.sourceQuote: So in 1641 the Franciscans went to the Joodenbuurt ["Jewish Quarter"], then at the outskirts of the east side of Amsterdam, and opened a house church, the second of its kind in the city, at a house called the "Moyses" (Moses), at the back of the present church. In 1682, the house was joined by the neighboring house "Aäron" (Aaron) with the purchase by Dr.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: So in 1641 the Franciscans went to the Joodenbuurt ["Jewish Quarter"], then at the outskirts of the east side of Amsterdam, and opened a house church, the second of its kind in the city, at a house called the "Moyses" (Moses), at the back of the present church. In 1682, the house was joined by the neighboring house "Aäron" (Aaron) with the purchase by Dr.

facts.text: Catholic services remained hidden behind house gables until prohibitions were lifted in the early nineteenth century.
facts.sourceQuote: But it remained hidden under the gables of the two houses until the early 19th century, when the prohibitions against the Catholic Church were finally lifted.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: But it remained hidden under the gables of the two houses until the early 19th century, when the prohibitions against the Catholic Church were finally lifted.

facts.text: The original site held Amsterdam's first municipal cemetery, established in 1640 before being lost in 1866.
facts.sourceQuote: The church even lost its namesake cemetery in 1866. Established in 1640, it was the first municipal cemetery in Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The church even lost its namesake cemetery in 1866. Established in 1640, it was the first municipal cemetery in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Constructed between 1837 and 1841, this structure served originally as a Water Management Church.
facts.sourceQuote: The present building was built as a "Water Management Church" (Dutch: Waterstaatskerk), between 1837 and 1841 from a design by Tilman-François Suys (1783–1861) in the style of neoclassicism, with three aisles and a recessed rectangular choir.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The present building was built as a "Water Management Church" (Dutch: Waterstaatskerk), between 1837 and 1841 from a design by Tilman-François Suys (1783–1861) in the style of neoclassicism, with three aisles and a recessed rectangular choir.

features.name: Pathé City

facts.text: The cinema hosted the 23rd Amsterdam Fantastic Film Festival in April 2007.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 31 januari 2007 vond de voorlopig laatste reguliere voorstelling plaats en van 18 tot 25 april 2007 was de bioscoop gastheer van het 23e Amsterdam Fantastic Film Festival.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On January 31, 2007, the penultimate regular performance took place and from April 18 to 25, 2007, the cinema was the host of the 23rd Amsterdam Fantastic Film Festival.

facts.text: Conductor Lex van Weren led the City Theater Orchestra before screenings began.
facts.sourceQuote: De bioscoop had de beschikking over een orkestbak met het City Theater Orkest dat onder leiding van dirigent Lex van Weren voorafgaand aan de film muziek verzorgde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The cinema had access to an orchestra pit with the City Theater Orchestra that provided music before the film under the direction of conductor Lex van Weren.

facts.text: An orchestra pit originally allowed live music to play before films started.
facts.sourceQuote: De bioscoop had de beschikking over een orkestbak met het City Theater Orkest dat onder leiding van dirigent Lex van Weren voorafgaand aan de film muziek verzorgde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The cinema had access to an orchestra pit with the City Theater Orchestra that provided music before the film under the direction of conductor Lex van Weren.

facts.text: Seven arthouse rooms opened when the venue reopened in December 2010.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 2 december 2010 openden de deuren opnieuw, met zeven zalen voor arthousefilms.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On December 2, 2010, the doors reopened again, with seven rooms for arthouse films.

facts.text: Englishman Reginald Foort was the first permanent organist when the theater opened.
facts.sourceQuote: Bij de opening speelde de eerste vaste organist van het theater, de Engelsman Reginald Foort.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the opening, the first permanent organist of the theater, the Englishman Reginald Foort, played.

facts.text: A lowered ceiling during the 1970s renovation largely closed off the upper organ room.
facts.sourceQuote: Bij de verbouwing van de zaal in het begin van de jaren zeventig werd de bovenste orgelkamer grotendeels afgesloten door een verlaagd plafond.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the renovation of the hall at the beginning of the 1970s, the upper organ room was largely closed off by a lowered ceiling.

features.opening: The Pathé City is a Pathé cinema at Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen 15-19 in Amsterdam, 40 meters from Leidseplein and diagonally opposite De Balie.

features.name: Central Station

facts.text: A pedestrian tunnel and the road in front vanished when a metro tunnel was built in the late 1970s.
facts.sourceQuote: With the construction of the metro tunnel in the late 1970s, both the pedestrian tunnel and the road in front of the station disappeared.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: With the construction of the metro tunnel in the late 1970s, both the pedestrian tunnel and the road in front of the station disappeared.

facts.text: In 1996, a third center roof by Jan Garvelink covered all platforms between two existing ones.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1996, a third, 'centre roof' designed by Jan Garvelink, architect at Holland Rail Consult, was built between the two existing roofs, whereby all platforms at the station were now covered.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1996, a third, 'centre roof' designed by Jan Garvelink, architect at Holland Rail Consult, was built between the two existing roofs, whereby all platforms at the station were now covered.

facts.text: The central hall and middle tunnel were considerably widened and modernized in the early 1980s.
facts.sourceQuote: In the early 1980s, the central hall and middle tunnel were considerably widened and modernized.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the early 1980s, the central hall and middle tunnel were considerably widened and modernized.

facts.text: Tracks on the western side expanded to increase capacity toward Sloterdijk station alongside a new signaling post.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 1990s, a new signaling post was built on the western side of the station. In addition, the number of tracks on that side was expanded in order to increase capacity in the direction of Sloterdijk station.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 1990s, a new signaling post was built on the western side of the station. In addition, the number of tracks on that side was expanded in order to increase capacity in the direction of Sloterdijk station.

facts.text: Contractor Philipp Holzmann built the station while architect Pierre Cuypers focused on decoration.
facts.sourceQuote: While Cuypers was the principal architect, it is believed that he focused mostly on the decoration of the station building and left the structural design to railway engineers. The station was built by contractor Philipp Holzmann.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: While Cuypers was the principal architect, it is believed that he focused mostly on the decoration of the station building and left the structural design to railway engineers. The station was built by contractor Philipp Holzmann.

facts.text: Local experts called the waterfront location a catastrophic attack on the capital's beauty.
facts.sourceQuote: In his book on the history of city, Amsterdam historian Geert Mak writes that: Almost all of Amsterdam's own experts and others involved thought this to be a catastrophic plan, 'the most disgusting possible attack on the beauty and glory of the capital'.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In his book on the history of city, Amsterdam historian Geert Mak writes that: Almost all of Amsterdam's own experts and others involved thought this to be a catastrophic plan, 'the most disgusting possible attack on the beauty and glory of the capital'.

features.name: Petruskerk

facts.text: Fishing proceeds from the Slootermeer were legally assigned to the church as early as 1479.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 24 maart 1479 kwamen bovendien de opbrengsten van de rijke visvangst uit het Slootermeer voortaan ten goede aan de Sint-Petruskerk van Sloterdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On March 24, 1479, in addition, the proceeds from the rich fishing catch from Slootermeer were henceforth to benefit the Sint-Petruskerk of Sloterdijk.

features.opening: The Petruskerk is a Protestant church in the former village of Sloterdijk, now part of Amsterdam-West.

features.name: Monument Indië-Nederland

facts.text: Surplus funds from a mausoleum project funded this monument's construction in Amsterdam and Batavia.
facts.sourceQuote: After the mausoleum was completed, there was still a bit of the collected money left, with which the committee responsible for its construction decided to build two more monuments to him, one in Batavia and the other in Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the mausoleum was completed, there was still a bit of the collected money left, with which the committee responsible for its construction decided to build two more monuments to him, one in Batavia and the other in Amsterdam.

facts.text: Architect Gijsbert Friedhoff and sculptor Frits van Hall won the contest to design the work.
facts.sourceQuote: This contest was won by the architect Gijsbert Friedhoff and the sculptor Frits van Hall.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This contest was won by the architect Gijsbert Friedhoff and the sculptor Frits van Hall.

facts.text: A female figure flanked by two lions symbolizes Dutch supremacy over conquered peoples.
facts.sourceQuote: The monument consists of a female character with a lion on each side, meant to symbolise Dutch supremacy over the conquered people of the Dutch East Indies.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The monument consists of a female character with a lion on each side, meant to symbolise Dutch supremacy over the conquered people of the Dutch East Indies.

facts.text: Political pressure changed its name to Monument Indië-Nederland in 2004.
facts.sourceQuote: Because of political pressure the name was changed in 2004 to Monument Indië-Nederland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because of political pressure the name was changed in 2004 to Monument Indië-Nederland.

facts.text: Originally a memorial for General J. B. van Heutsz, it was renamed in 2004.
facts.sourceQuote: The monument was originally a memorial for General J. B. van Heutsz, who was the commandant of the Royal Netherlands East Indies Army and is also known for conquering Aceh for the Kingdom of the Netherlands in 1903 following the Aceh War. Because of political pressure the name was changed in 2004 to Monument Indië-Nederland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The monument was originally a memorial for General J. B. van Heutsz, who was the commandant of the Royal Netherlands East Indies Army and is also known for conquering Aceh for the Kingdom of the Netherlands in 1903 following the Aceh War. features.opening: The Monument Indië-Nederland is located near the Olympiaplein in the southern part of Amsterdam.

facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Three of the colocations of the Amsterdam Internet Exchange are at the institutes SURFsara, NIKHEF, and Equinix-AM3 at the science park.

features.name: Molen van Sloten

facts.text: The attic features a Rembrandt presentation with washing images of his characters.
facts.sourceQuote: In de molen is veel te zien over de molentechniek en de geschiedenis van Sloten en Oud Osdorp, maar er is ook een presentatie Rembrandt op zolder, met daarin wassen beelden van Rembrandt en diverse van zijn personages.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the mill there is much to see about milling technology and the history of Sloten and Oud Osdorp, but there is also a Rembrandt presentation on the attic, with washing images of Rembrandt and various of his characters.

facts.text: A glassmaking museum opened here in April 2005 but closed permanently in 2020.
facts.sourceQuote: In april 2005 werd het complex uitgebreid met een Kuiperijmuseum, waarin veel te zien was over het oude ambacht van de kuiperij. Het Kuiperijmuseum is in 2020 gesloten en ontruimd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In April 2005, the complex was expanded with a Kuiperij museum, in which there was much to see about the old craft of glassmaking. The Kuiperij Museum was closed and evacuated in 2020.

facts.text: Brouwerij De 7 Deugden brewery began operations at the site in April 2018.
facts.sourceQuote: In april 2018 is naast de molen de Brouwerij De 7 Deugden geopend.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In April 2018, in addition to the mill, the Brouwerij De 7 Deugden was opened.

facts.text: Carpentry artifacts from this mill were relocated to the Brabants Museum Oud-Oosterhout.
facts.sourceQuote: De voorwerpen die betrekking hebben op het kuipersambacht zijn verhuisd naar het Brabants Museum Oud-Oosterhout.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The objects related to the carpentry trade have been moved to the Brabants Museum Oud-Oosterhout.

features.opening: The Molen van Sloten is a polder mill in the village of Sloten near Amsterdam.

features.name: Torenfort aan de Ossenmarkt

facts.text: The moat was filled in during 1876 to better protect the structure from newer cannons.
facts.sourceQuote: Om het fort beter te beschermen tegen nieuwe, zwaardere en trefzekerder kanonnen werd in 1876 de gracht gedempt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1876, the moat was filled in to better protect the fort from new, heavier and more accurate cannons.

facts.text: Renovation involved excavating the earthen embankment and restoring the canal and bridge.
facts.sourceQuote: De aarden dekkingswal werd afgegraven en de gracht en brug werden hersteld.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The earthen embankment was excavated and the canal and bridge were restored.

facts.text: A music school and a historical society now operate within the reopened fort.
facts.sourceQuote: In Fort aan de Ossenmarkt, dat in 1992 feestelijk werd heropend, zijn onder andere de Kreatieve Groep Weesp, een muziekschool en de Historische Kring Weesp gevestigd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In Fort aan de Ossenmarkt, which was reopened in 1992 in a festive manner, the Kreatieve Groep Weesp, a music school and the Historische Kring Weesp are among others located.

facts.text: An exhibition space occupies the original 1877 genieloods building today.
facts.sourceQuote: In de genieloods uit 1877 is nu een expositieruimte.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 1877 genieloods there is now an exhibition space.

features.opening: The Torenfort aan de Ossenmarkt is a tower fort in Weesp in the province of North Holland.

features.name: Monument Haarlemmerweg

facts.text: The current monument features three amber trees symbolizing the future and life.
facts.sourceQuote: Drie amberbomen staande voor de toekomst en het leven completeren het monument.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Three amber trees standing for the future and life complete the monument.

facts.text: A police officer's father and son were among those shot dead at this location.
facts.sourceQuote: Politieagent Elias vader en zoon Verkuijl werden hier door de Duitse bezetter doodgeschoten als vergelding voor een verzetsdaad op het spoortraject Amsterdam-Haarlem.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Police officer Elias' father and son Verkuijl were shot dead here by the German occupiers as revenge for a resistance act on the Amsterdam-Haarlem railway line.

features.opening: The Monument on the Haarlemmerweg is a monument for war victims, placed on the Haarlemmerweg, Amsterdam Nieuw-West between the pedestrian and bicycle bridges…

features.name: Boom Chicago

facts.text: A video titled SpongeBob SquarePants in China went viral on YouTube with over 108 million views.
facts.sourceQuote: 2007: Comedy Central Netherlands launches "Comedy Central News" (75 episodes). "Highly Dubious News" shines at MIPCOM. "SpongeBob SquarePants in China" goes viral on YouTube (108 million views), sparking political controversy.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 2007: Comedy Central Netherlands launches "Comedy Central News" (75 episodes). "Highly Dubious News" shines at MIPCOM. "SpongeBob SquarePants in China" goes viral on YouTube (108 million views), sparking political controversy.

facts.text: Ike Barinholtz won the Celebrity Jeopardy championship in 2023 and donated his million-dollar prize to charity.
facts.sourceQuote: He also won the Celebrity Jeopardy championship in 2023, and donated his million dollar prize to his charity.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: He also won the Celebrity Jeopardy championship in 2023, and donated his million dollar prize to his charity.

features.name: Auschwitz Memorial

facts.text: The monument moved from Oosterbegraafplaats to Wertheimpark in 1993 as a larger version.
facts.sourceQuote: Het monument werd oorspronkelijk geplaatst op de Oosterbegraafplaats. In 1993 is het monument in grotere vorm verplaatst naar het Wertheimpark.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The monument was originally placed on the Oosterbegraafplaats. In 1993, the monument was moved in a larger form to Wertheimpark.

facts.text: Glass plates were replaced because sand on shoes scratched them and made them dull.
facts.sourceQuote: De glazen platen hadden krassen (er wordt wel op gelopen met zand en grind aan de schoenen) en waren dof geworden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The glass plates had scratches (people walk on them with sand and gravel on their shoes) and had become dull.

features.opening: The Auschwitzmonument, also known as the mirror monument 'Nooit Meer Auschwitz' or Broken Mirrors, is a Dutch memorial in the Wertheimpark in Amsterdam to…

features.name: Raw Aron Schuster Synagoge

facts.text: Raw Aron Schuster Synagoge was named after Rabbi Aron Schuster when he retired in 1973.
facts.sourceQuote: Toen rabbijn Aron Schuster (1907-1994) in 1973 zijn werkzaamheden als opperrabbijn neerlegde en Amsterdam verliet om in Jeruzalem te gaan wonen, werd de synagoge, die zijn standplaats was geweest vanaf zijn benoeming per 1 januari 1942 in het Rabbinaat van Amsterdam, naar hem vernoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When Rabbi Aron Schuster (1907-1994) retired from his work as chief rabbi in 1973 and left Amsterdam to live in Jerusalem, the synagogue, which had been his place of residence since his appointment on January 1, 1942 in the Rabbinate of Amsterdam, was named after him.

facts.text: The first post-war service occurred on Rosh Hashanah 1945 using reassembled pre-war sofas.
facts.sourceQuote: Na de Tweede Wereldoorlog werd de Obrechtsjoel het centrum van het religieus-joodse leven in Amsterdam. De eerste dienst in het gebouw kon plaatsvinden op Rosj Hasjana 1945, zij het met een provisorisch interieur. De gedemonteerde vooroorlogse banken konden nadien worden teruggeplaatst.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After World War II, the Obrechts Synagogue became the center of religious Jewish life in Amsterdam. The first service in the building could take place on Rosh Hashanah 1945, albeit with a provisional interior. The disassembled pre-war sofas could then be reassembled.

facts.text: A certificate placed in a lead box behind the Torah cabinet marked the 1927 cornerstone laying.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 27 juni 1927 werd ter gelegenheid van de eerstesteenlegging een oorkonde in een loden koker ingemetseld in de buitenmuur achter de Aron Hakodesj, de kast met de Torarollen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On June 27, 1927, on the occasion of the laying of the first stone, a certificate was set in a lead box into the outer wall behind the Aron Hakodesh, the cabinet with the Torah scrolls.

facts.text: Hans Bloemendal served as the synagogue's cantor from 1949 until 2009.
facts.sourceQuote: Van 1949 tot 2009 was Hans Bloemendal de voorzanger (chazan) van de Raw Aron Schuster Synagoge.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1949 to 2009, Hans Bloemendal was the cantor (chazan) of the Raw Aron Schuster Synagoge.

features.opening: The Raw Aron Schuster Synagoge or the Obrechtsjoel (בית כנסת רב אהרן שוסטר) is the largest still functioning Ashkenazi synagogue (shoe) in Amsterdam.

features.name: Koningskerk

facts.text: The exterior brickwork resembles a crossword puzzle according to some observers.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de buitenzijde geeft het volgens sommigen het uiterlijk van een kruiswoordraadsel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the outside, according to some, it gives the appearance of a crossword puzzle.

facts.text: Since 1994, the building has served the Evangelical Brotherhood Church with many Surinamese attendees.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 1994 wordt de kerk gebruikt door de Evangelische Broedergemeente. Als zodanig komen er veel mensen uit de Surinaamse gemeenschap.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1994, the church has been used by the Evangelical Brotherhood Church. As such, many people come from the Surinamese community.

facts.text: Architects and organ builder Mense Ruiter disagreed over whether organ pipes should remain visible.
facts.sourceQuote: Het orgel stamt uit 1960 en werd gebouwd door Mense Ruiter te Groningen. De architecten van de kerk wilden de pijpen niet zichtbaar in het orgelfront zien. Dit gaf meningsverschil met de orgelbouwer die dat wél wilde.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The organ dates back to 1960 and was built by Mense Ruiter in Groningen. The architects of the church did not want the pipes to be visible in the organ front. This caused a disagreement with the organ builder who did want that.

features.opening: The Koningskerk is a church in the Amsterdam district of Watergraafsmeer.

features.name: De Schreeuw

facts.text: Theo van Gogh was assassinated nearby in 2004, inspiring the work.
facts.sourceQuote: Theo van Gogh was assassinated on 2 November 2004 in the Linnaeusstraat in Amsterdam, just a few steps away from the Oosterpark.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Theo van Gogh was assassinated on 2 November 2004 in the Linnaeusstraat in Amsterdam, just a few steps away from the Oosterpark.

facts.text: Mohammed Bouyeri killed Theo van Gogh just steps from Oosterpark.
facts.sourceQuote: Theo van Gogh was assassinated on 2 November 2004 in the Linnaeusstraat in Amsterdam, just a few steps away from the Oosterpark. The assassin was Mohammed Bouyeri.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Theo van Gogh was assassinated on 2 November 2004 in the Linnaeusstraat in Amsterdam, just a few steps away from the Oosterpark. The assassin was Mohammed Bouyeri.

facts.text: Artist Henneman created this sculpture in 2007 as a symbol of free speech.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2007 Henneman created the sculpture as symbol of freedom of speech.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2007 Henneman created the sculpture as symbol of freedom of speech.

facts.text: The stainless steel statue stands 4.5 metres tall with a face screaming on one side and closed on the other.
facts.sourceQuote: The 4.5-metre-tall (15 ft) heat-blasted stainless steel statue is in the form of a stylized profile of a face that screams on one side and has a closed mouth on the other.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The 4.5-metre-tall (15 ft) heat-blasted stainless steel statue is in the form of a stylized profile of a face that screams on one side and has a closed mouth on the other.

facts.text: Designer Jeroen Henneman intended the image to remind viewers of Theo van Gogh's murder and his cry for mercy.
facts.sourceQuote: The designer, Jeroen Henneman, said on the occasion of the unveiling that he hopes the image will remind passers-by of the moment of the murder; "to Theo van Gogh, who cries out for mercy".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The designer, Jeroen Henneman, said on the occasion of the unveiling that he hopes the image will remind passers-by of the moment of the murder; "to Theo van Gogh, who cries out for mercy".

features.opening: De Schreeuw (The Scream) is a sculpture in the Oosterpark in Amsterdam that commemorates the assassinated Dutch film-maker Theo van Gogh.

features.name: De Boom die alles zag

facts.text: De Boom die alles zag (The Tree That Saw It All) earned its name from eye-shaped patterns on its trunk.
facts.sourceQuote: Due to the eye-shaped patterns on its trunk, the tree was considered to be an eyewitness of the accident and its aftermath.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Due to the eye-shaped patterns on its trunk, the tree was considered to be an eyewitness of the accident and its aftermath.

facts.text: Two cables attached to neighboring trees support the tree after it lost roots during soil cleanup.
facts.sourceQuote: The tree lost a part of its roots during the clean-up of the soil, which made it necessary to support it with two cables attached to neighbouring trees.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tree lost a part of its roots during the clean-up of the soil, which made it necessary to support it with two cables attached to neighbouring trees.

facts.text: Soil replacement in 2017 improved the tree's condition despite ongoing cable support needs.
facts.sourceQuote: The soil under it was replaced in 2017 to stimulate root growth, which according to pulling tests four years later improved its condition, but the tree is still supported by the cables to prevent it from falling.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The soil under it was replaced in 2017 to stimulate root growth, which according to pulling tests four years later improved its condition, but the tree is still supported by the cables to prevent it from falling.

features.name: Museum De Dageraad

facts.text: Architects Michel de Klerk and Piet Kramer built 294 houses and six shops for the socialist association in 1920.
facts.sourceQuote: De socialistische woningbouwvereniging 'De Dageraad' gaf in 1920 de architecten Michel de Klerk en Piet Kramer opdracht voor de bouw van 294 woningen en zes winkels.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The socialist housing association 'De Dageraad' commissioned the architects Michel de Klerk and Piet Kramer in 1920 to build 294 houses and six shops.

features.opening: De Dageraad is a residential complex in Amsterdam-Zuid.

features.name: Plaquette 7 mei 1945

facts.text: Plaquette 7 mei 1945 marks the day thousands gathered on Dam square to celebrate the war's end.
facts.sourceQuote: On 7 May, thousands of people gathered on the Dam, the central square of the city, to celebrate the end of the war and welcome the Allied soldiers.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On 7 May, thousands of people gathered on the Dam, the central square of the city, to celebrate the end of the war and welcome the Allied soldiers.

facts.text: A German reconnaissance convoy narrowly passed the British cars near Dam before quickly disappearing.
facts.sourceQuote: A convoy of German vehicles, also carrying out reconnaissance, narrowly passed the British vehicles near the Dam, but quickly disappeared again.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A convoy of German vehicles, also carrying out reconnaissance, narrowly passed the British vehicles near the Dam, but quickly disappeared again.

facts.text: Dutch resistance forces had already seized the Royal Palace and post office by midday without major trouble.
facts.sourceQuote: Meanwhile the Dutch resistance (Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten) had successfully disarmed most of the Germans, without much trouble. By midday they had taken possession of three key locations: the Royal Palace, the main money office and the main post office (Operation Three Castles).
