facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The dam built around 2008 lies between the Houthaven and the Nieuwe Houthaven and forms the connection between the mainland (Dantzigerkade) and a much older stretch dam between the Houthavens and IJ.

facts.text: Haparandadam honors Haparanda, a Swedish port on the Gulf of Bothnia bordering Finland.
facts.sourceQuote: De dam is vernoemd naar de Zweedse havenstad Haparanda aan de Botnische Golf, op de grens met Finland, waar veel hout vandaan naar Amsterdam kwam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The dam is named after the Swedish port city of Haparanda on the Gulf of Bothnia, on the border with Finland, where much wood came from to Amsterdam.

features.opening: The Haparandadam is a dam in Amsterdam-West.

features.name: Petemayenbrug

facts.text: The name Petemayenbrug derives from petemoeien, meaning stepmother or old women.
facts.sourceQuote: De naam zou afgeleid zijn van petemoeien (peetmoeder), tevens aanduiding van oude vrouwtjes.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name would be derived from petemoeien (stepmother), also indicating old women.

facts.text: An iron replacement for the wooden structure was completed in 1897.
facts.sourceQuote: De houten ophaalbrug werd in 1897 vervangen door een ijzeren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The wooden loading bridge was replaced by an iron one in 1897.

facts.text: Jacob Olie captured the new iron bridge just months after its opening.
facts.sourceQuote: Men had toen het idee dat het toepassen van ijzer voor hameipoort, de balans en liggers een besparing zou opleveren (ten opzichte van een houten brug), de brug werd enkele maanden na opening vastgelegd door Jacob Olie.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At that time, the idea was that applying iron to the hameipoort, the balance and struts would result in a savings (compared to a wooden bridge), the bridge was captured a few months after opening by Jacob Olie.

features.opening: The Petemayenbrug is a double pickup bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Havenstraat

facts.text: Havenstraat means 'Harbor Street' and was named for a ship mooring place.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kreeg op 3 april 1912 per raadsbesluit haar naam; een vernoeming naar haven, een ligplaats voor schepen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was given its name on April 3, 1912 by a council decision; a name after the harbor, a mooring place for ships.

facts.text: Nearby streets share shipping themes like Vaartstraat, Vlietstraat, and Zeilstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: Meerdere straten in de buurt zijn vernoemd naar begrippen uit de scheepvaart (Vaartstraat, Vlietstraat, Zeilstraat).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Several streets in the neighborhood are named after concepts from shipping (Vaartstraat, Vlietstraat, Zeilstraat).

facts.text: The council officially named the street on April 3, 1912.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kreeg op 3 april 1912 per raadsbesluit haar naam; een vernoeming naar haven, een ligplaats voor schepen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was given its name on April 3, 1912 by a council decision; a name after the harbor, a mooring place for ships.

facts.text: House number 6, a prison from 1890, became the British School of Amsterdam in 2021.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kent drie opvallende gebouwen: het Huis van Bewaring (II) met huisnummer 6, een ontwerp van architect Willem Metzelaar (werkend voor Justitie), een gevangenis uit 1890, die, nadat er vluchtelingen en dak- en thuislozen waren opgevangen, vanaf 2019 werd verbouwd ten behoeve van de British School of Amsterdam die hier van start is gegaan vanaf het schooljaar 2021-2022.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street has three striking buildings: the Huis van Bewaring (II) with house number 6, a design by architect Willem Metzelaar (working for the Justice Department), a prison from 1890, which, after refugees and homeless people were accommodated, was renovated from 2019 for the British School of Amsterdam, which started here from the 2021-2022 school year.

facts.text: Until 2024, the street held only two odd house numbers: three and five.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kende (tot 2024) slechts twee oneven huisnummers 3 en 5, bestaande uit Romneyloodsen op het terrein achter het Haarlemmermeerstation.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street only had two odd house numbers 3 and 5 (until 2024), consisting of Romney sheds on the site behind the Haarlemmermeer station.

features.opening: The Havenstraat is a street in the Schinkel neighborhood, Amsterdam-Zuid.

features.name: Hoofddorpweg

facts.text: Hoofddorpweg takes its name from the town of Hoofddorp in the Haarlemmermeer.
facts.sourceQuote: De Hoofddorpweg is vernoemd naar Hoofddorp in de Haarlemmermeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Hoofddorpweg is named after Hoofddorp in the Haarlemmermeer.

facts.text: Construction began in the 1920s on land formerly belonging to the municipality of Sloten.
facts.sourceQuote: De Hoofddorpweg in de Hoofddorppleinbuurt van Amsterdam-Zuid werd aangelegd in de jaren 20 op het grondgebied van de in 1921 door Amsterdam geannexeerde gemeente Sloten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Hoofddorpweg in the Hoofddorpplein neighborhood of Amsterdam-Zuid was built in the 1920s on the territory of the municipality of Sloten, annexed by Amsterdam in 1921.

facts.text: The Zeilbrug has linked Hoofddorpweg to Zeilstraat and Amstelveenseweg since 1927.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 1927 is de Hoofddorpweg via de Zeilbrug verbonden met de Zeilstraat en verdere omgeving van de Amstelveenseweg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1927, the Hoofddorpweg has been connected to Zeilstraat and the surrounding area of the Amstelveenseweg via the Zeilbrug.

facts.text: Other streets in this neighborhood are also named after places located southwest of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: Andere straten in de Hoofddorppleinbuurt zijn eveneens vernoemd naar plaatsen ten zuidwesten van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Other streets in the Hoofddorpplein neighborhood are also named after places southwest of Amsterdam.

features.opening: The Hoofddorpweg in the Hoofddorpplein neighborhood of Amsterdam-Zuid was built in the 1920s on the territory of the municipality of Sloten, which was annexed…

features.name: Stadionplein

facts.text: Between 2005 and 2008, over 900 homes were built on former sports fields here.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Olympisch Kwartier aan de noordwestkant van het plein is gebouwd op de plaats van vroegere sportvelden en de Frans Ottenhal. Tussen 2005 en 2008 werden hier in totaal ruim 900 woningen opgeleverd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Olympic Quarter on the northwest side of the square was built on the site of former sports fields and the Frans Ottenhal. Between 2005 and 2008, a total of more than 900 homes were delivered here.

facts.text: Architecture follows Amsterdam School styles and Berlage's ideas using six closed blocks.
facts.sourceQuote: Het stedenbouwkundige plan en de architectuur zijn gebaseerd op de Amsterdamse School en de ideeën van Berlage. De zes nieuwe gesloten bouwblokken zijn ontworpen door architectenbureaus als Mulleners & Mulleners (langs de Afroditekade), Lafour en Wijk (langs de binnenstraten) en Rudy Uytenhaak (langs de Laan der Hesperiden).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The urban planning plan and architecture are based on the Amsterdam School and the ideas of Berlage. The six new closed building blocks were designed by architectural firms such as Mulleners & Mulleners (along the Afroditekade), Lafour and Wijk (along the inner streets) and Rudy Uytenhaak (along the Laan der Hesperiden).

facts.text: Part of Stadionplein became Laan der Hesperiden due to the district's construction.
facts.sourceQuote: In verband met de bouw van deze wijk is een deel van het Stadionplein hernoemd tot Laan der Hesperiden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Due to the construction of this district, part of Stadionplein has been renamed Laan der Hesperiden.

facts.text: Two Febo snack bars operated in former Olympic ticket offices from 1971 until redevelopment forced their removal in 2013.
facts.sourceQuote: Midden op het plein waren van 1971 tot 2013 een tweetal filialen van Febo gevestigd in een tweetal voormalige kaartverkoophuisjes van het Olympisch Stadion. Door de herontwikkeling van het plein moesten ze na 42 jaar verdwijnen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the middle of the square, from 1971 to 2013, two branches of Febo were located in two former ticket offices of the Olympic Stadium. Due to the redevelopment of the square, they had to disappear after 42 years.

facts.text: Cirque du Soleil premiered its European Quidam show on this square in 1999.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1999 beleefde de voorstelling Quidam van Cirque du Soleil op het plein zijn Europese premiére.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1999, the show Quidam by Cirque du Soleil on the square had its European premiere.

facts.text: A 2018 plan to rename the square Johan Cruijffplein was abandoned after neighbor protests revealed flawed decision-making.
facts.sourceQuote: De Gemeente Amsterdam heeft het voornemen gehad om het Stadionplein in 2018 om te dopen tot het Johan Cruijffplein, maar na protest van buurtbewoners kwamen onzorgvuldigheden in de besluitvorming aan het licht, waarna men hier uiteindelijk van af heeft gezien.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Municipality of Amsterdam had the intention of renaming the Stadionplein to Johan Cruijffplein in 2018, but after protests from neighbors, careless practices in decision-making came to light, after which it was ultimately decided not to do so.

features.opening: The Stadionplein is a square in Amsterdam-Zuid, which was built in the 1920s at the intersection of Stadionweg and Amstelveenseweg to better control car…

features.name: Sint Antoniesbreestraat

facts.text: Rembrandt lived on Sint Antoniesbreestraat from 1631 to 1635 at the home of art dealer Hendrick van Uylenburgh.
facts.sourceQuote: In the early 17th century, the street was popular with immigrants and artists such as the painter Rembrandt, who lived there from 1631 to 1635, at the home of art dealer Hendrick van Uylenburgh. (From 1639 to 1656 he lived in his own home, now the Rembrandt House Museum.) Other painters who lived in the street, near the Guild of Saint Luke in the former Sint Anthoniespoort, include Pieter Isaacsz, Esaias Boursse, who lived next door to Rembrandt, Nicolaes Eliaszoon Pickenoy, Cornelis van der Voort, Roelant Savery, Pieter Lastman (in whose workshop Rembrandt served as apprentice), Adriaen van Nieulandt, Pieter Codde, Willem Kick, Justus and Johannes Vingboons, and their father David Vinckboons.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the early 17th century, the street was popular with immigrants and artists such as the painter Rembrandt, who lived there from 1631 to 1635, at the home of art dealer Hendrick van Uylenburgh. (From 1639 to 1656 he lived in his own home, now the Rembrandt House Museum.) Other painters who lived in the street, near the Guild of Saint Luke in the former Sint Anthoniespoort, include Pieter Isaacsz, Esaias Boursse, who lived next door to Rembrandt, Nicolaes Eliaszoon Pickenoy, Cornelis van der Voort, Roelant Savery, Pieter Lastman (in whose workshop Rembrandt served as apprentice), Adriaen van Nieulandt, Pieter Codde, Willem Kick, Justus and Johannes Vingboons, and their father David Vinckboons.

facts.text: Sint Antoniesbreestraat translates to "St. Anthony's Broad Street".
facts.sourceQuote: The Sint Antoniesbreestraat ("St. Anthony's Broad Street") is a street in the centre of Amsterdam in the Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Sint Antoniesbreestraat ("St. Anthony's Broad Street") is a street in the centre of Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

features.opening: The Sint Antoniesbreestraat ("St. Anthony's Broad Street") is a street in the centre of Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

features.name: Frederiksstraat

facts.text: Amsterdam annexed the area in 1896 but allowed the name to remain since no other Frederiksstraat existed.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1896 annexeerde de gemeente Amsterdam dit gebied. Aangezien Amsterdam nog geen Frederiksstraat had, mocht de straat haar naam behouden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1896, the municipality of Amsterdam annexed this area. Since Amsterdam did not yet have a Frederiksstraat, the street was allowed to retain its name.

facts.text: Revolutionary construction caused all buildings to share great similarity except two on the park edge.
facts.sourceQuote: Er kwam hier revolutiebouw, waardoor alle panden grote gelijkenis vertonen. Uitzonderingen zijn twee gebouwen aan de rand van het Vondelpark.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There was revolutionary construction here, which caused all the buildings to have great similarity. Exceptions are two buildings on the edge of Vondelpark.

facts.text: The largest building with this address sits behind others on an internal site rather than on the street itself.
facts.sourceQuote: Het grootste gebouw met het adres Frederiksstraat staat niet aan de straat zelf; het ligt achter de bebouwing aan de even zijde op een binnenterrein. Het is gebouw Frederiksstraat 18a.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The largest building with the address Frederiksstraat is not on the street itself; it is located behind the buildings on the opposite side on an internal site. It is building Frederiksstraat 18a.

features.opening: The Frederiksstraat is a relatively short street in Amsterdam Oud-West.

features.name: Ringweg-West

facts.text: Two lanes reverse direction based on peak traffic flow to manage congestion.
facts.sourceQuote: The tunnel consists of three fixed lanes and two reversible lanes, which are opened in the direction where traffic is the heaviest.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tunnel consists of three fixed lanes and two reversible lanes, which are opened in the direction where traffic is the heaviest.

facts.text: Construction commenced in September 2009 and the tunnel opened in July 2014.
facts.sourceQuote: Total costs of the project are estimated at 1.2 billion euros and construction started on September 7, 2009. The tunnel was officially opened on July 21, 2014.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Total costs of the project are estimated at 1.2 billion euros and construction started on September 7, 2009. The tunnel was officially opened on July 21, 2014.

facts.text: The entire project cost an estimated 1.2 billion euros.
facts.sourceQuote: Total costs of the project are estimated at 1.2 billion euros and construction started on September 7, 2009.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Total costs of the project are estimated at 1.2 billion euros and construction started on September 7, 2009.

features.opening: The Second Coen Tunnel is a tunnel under the North Sea Canal, next to the Coen Tunnel in Amsterdam.

features.name: Plantage Doklaan

facts.text: A Dutch Railways goods yard operated here from 1904 until the 1980s.
facts.sourceQuote: Langs de Plantage Doklaan lag van 1904 tot de jaren tachtig van de 20e eeuw een goederenemplacement van de Nederlandse Spoorwegen (voorheen HSM).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Along the Plantage Doklaan, from 1904 until the 1980s of the 20th century, there was a goods yard of the Dutch Railways (formerly HSM).

facts.text: New trams were delivered by rail to this spot during three separate periods between 1972 and 1981.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1972-1973, 1974-1975 en in 1979-1981 werden de nieuwe middenbakken en nieuwe Amsterdamse trams hier per spoor afgeleverd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1972-1973, 1974-1975 and in 1979-1981, the new midbays and new Amsterdam trams were delivered here by rail.

facts.text: Tram lines 6, 7, 14, and 20 once ran through Plantage Doklaan until 2006.
facts.sourceQuote: Tussen 1931 en 2006 hebben (o.a.) de tramlijnen 6, 7, 14 en 20 door de Plantage Doklaan naar de Plantage Parklaan gereden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1931 and 2006, tram lines 6, 7, 14 and 20 ran through the Plantage Doklaan to Plantage Parklaan.

facts.text: The tram tracks here are now used only for detours rather than regular service.
facts.sourceQuote: De tramsporen zijn hier nu nog alleen in gebruik voor omleidingen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tram tracks are still only in use here for detours.

facts.text: Tram line 20 served this area as a stop starting in 1997 before ending in 2002.
facts.sourceQuote: Plantage Parklaan was vanaf 1997 een pauzestopplaats van de in 2002 opgeheven tramlijn 20.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Plantage Parklaan was a stop on the tram line 20, which was discontinued in 2002, from 1997.

features.opening: The Plantage Doklaan is a street in the Plantagebuurt of Amsterdam.

features.name: IJsbaanpad

facts.text: The IJsbaanpad name dates to 1949, honoring a former ice field where winter waters created a skating sheet.
facts.sourceQuote: De Amsterdamsche IJsclub (AIJC) had een terrein bij de Schinkel in gebruik, dat onder water werd gezet in de winter om een ijsvlakte te laten ontstaan. De weg daarheen kreeg daarom in 1949 de naam IJsbaanpad.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Amsterdamsche IJsclub (AIJC) had a field near the Schinkel in use, which was submerged in winter to create an ice sheet. The road to it was therefore named IJsbaanpad in 1949.

facts.text: Bridge 999, the white Post-Print Happiness Bridge, links the street to the Olympic Stadium since 2009.
facts.sourceQuote: De witte "Na-Druk-Geluksbrug" (brug 999) over de Stadiongracht, ontworpen door René van Zuuk, verbindt sinds 2009 het IJsbaanpad met het Amsterdamse Olympisch Stadion.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The white "Post-Print Happiness Bridge" (bridge 999) over the Stadiongracht, designed by René van Zuuk, has been connecting the IJsbaanpad with the Amsterdam Olympic Stadium since 2009.

facts.text: Living arches or boats rest on piers near the Schinkelsluis lock at the street's end.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan het eind van het IJsbaanpad bevindt zich de Nieuwe Meersluis of Schinkelsluis, die Schinkel met Nieuwe Meer verbindt. Nabij deze sluis bevinden zich woonarken ("woonboten"), de meeste daarvan zijn aan steigers gelegen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the end of the IJsbaanpad is the Nieuwe Meersluis or Schinkelsluis, which connects Schinkel to Nieuwe Meer. Near this lock are living arches ("living boats"), most of which are located on piers.

features.opening: The IJsbaanpad is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, between the Amstelveenseweg and the Schinkel.

features.name: Van Kinsbergenstraat

facts.text: In 2003, riots following a police shooting led to vandalism against houses along this stretch of the street.
facts.sourceQuote: Op 6 augustus 2003 gooiden vernielzuchtige jongeren tussen het Mercatorplein en de Van Kinsbergenstraat ruiten van huizen in met bakstenen en fietsen na rellen op het Mercatorplein nadat een jongen door een politieagent werd doodgeschoten toen hij deze met een mes wilde aanvallen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On August 6, 2003, vandals threw bricks and bicycles at the windows of houses between Mercatorplein and Van Kinsbergenstraat after riots on Mercatorplein after a boy was shot dead by a police officer when he tried to attack him with a knife.

facts.text: A 2005 event installed pavement art promoting neighborhood respect with symbols like talking quietly and not honking.
facts.sourceQuote: Midden op dit kruispunt is het woord "buurtrespect" aangebracht. Op de vier hoeken bevinden zich telkens vier symbolen van de afspraken die in het kader daarvan waren gemaakt, zoals "rustig praten", "niet nafluiten" en "niet vernielen". Dit alles werd aangebracht tijdens een officiële gebeurtenis op 21 december 2005.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the middle of this intersection, the word "neighborhood respect" is written. At each of the four corners are four symbols of the agreements made in that context, such as "talking quietly", "not honking" and "not destroying". All of this was applied during an official event on December 21, 2005.

facts.text: The new De Wending residential complex features an Amsterdam School style with 120 apartments on Witte de Withplein.
facts.sourceQuote: Na de sloop van de bebouwing tussen de Van Kinsbergenstraat, de Witte de Withstraat, de Lodewijk Boisotstraat en de Admiralengracht (het "Admiralenblok"), is in oktober 2009 begonnen met de bouw van nieuwbouwproject De Wending, dit is een wooncomplex geïnspireerd door de stijl van de Amsterdamse School, met 120 appartementen aan het nieuwe Witte de Withplein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the demolition of the buildings between the Van Kinsbergenstraat, the Witte de Withstraat, the Lodewijk Boisotstraat and the Admiralengracht (the "Admiralenblok"), construction began in October 2009 on the new construction project De Wending, this is a residential complex inspired by the style of the Amsterdam School, with 120 apartments on the new Witte de Withplein.

features.opening: The Van Kinsbergenstraat is a street in the Chassébuurt of Amsterdam-West.

features.name: Binnen Dommersstraat

facts.text: Wooden drawbridges fell out of fashion by 1898, prompting a replacement with iron spans.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1898 was de brug opnieuw aan vervangen toe; houten ophaalbruggen waren toen uit de mode; er moest een ijzeren ophaalbrug komen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1898, the bridge was again due for replacement; wooden drawbridges were out of fashion at the time; an iron drawbridge had to be built.

facts.text: A 1625 map shows a bridge leading north to nowhere across undeveloped land between canals.
facts.sourceQuote: Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode tekende daarom in zijn kaart van 1625 twee bruggen: een klein bruggetje over de Palm Graft (die uiteraard na de demping daarvan verdween) en een lange brug over de Brouwers Graft. De brug leidde toen naar het noorden nog nergens naartoe; het gebied tussen Brouwersgracht en de huidige Haarlemmerstraat was nog onbebouwd op een enkel kavel na.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode therefore drew two bridges on his map of 1625: a small bridge over the Palm Graft (which of course disappeared after its damping) and a long bridge over the Brouwers Graft. The bridge then led north to nowhere; the area between Brouwersgracht and the current Haarlemmerstraat was still undeveloped except for a single plot.

facts.text: An earlier Dommersbrug connected Haarlemmer Houttuinen and Prinseneiland across the Eilandsgracht around 1615.
facts.sourceQuote: Deze Dommersbrug (ook in het verlengde van de Dommersstraten) verzorgde sinds omstreeks 1615 de verbinding tussen de Haarlemmer Houttuinen (Hout Tuynen) en het Prinseneiland (Prince Eylandt), ze overspande daarbij de Eilandsgracht (Eylands Graft).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This Dommersbrug (also along the Dommersstraten) provided the connection between the Haarlemmer Houttuinen (Hout Tuynen) and the Prinseneiland (Prince Eylandt) since around 1615, spanning the Eilandsgracht (Eylands Graft) in the process.

features.opening: Bridge 148 is a lift bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Zeilstraat

facts.text: The Zeilstraat was named in 1908 after the sail of a sailing boat, the canvas for catching wind on vessels.
facts.sourceQuote: De Zeilstraat werd in 1908 vernoemd naar het zeil van een zeilboot ("het doek voor de opvang van wind op vaartuigen").
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Zeilstraat was named in 1908 after the sail of a sailing boat ("the canvas for catching wind on vessels").

facts.text: A bridge over the Schinkel has connected the street to Hoofddorpweg since 1927.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 1927 ligt voor de Zeilstraat een brug over de Schinkel die meestal de Zeilbrug wordt genoemd en een verbinding vormt met de Hoofddorpweg, die in het verlengde van de Zeilstraat ligt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1927, a bridge over the Schinkel has been built for the Zeilstraat, which is usually called the Zeilbrug and forms a connection with the Hoofddorpweg, which lies along the Zeilstraat.

facts.text: The Zeilbrug is the usual name for the bridge built over the Schinkel in 1927.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 1927 ligt voor de Zeilstraat een brug over de Schinkel die meestal de Zeilbrug wordt genoemd en een verbinding vormt met de Hoofddorpweg, die in het verlengde van de Zeilstraat ligt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1927, a bridge over the Schinkel has been built for the Zeilstraat, which is usually called the Zeilbrug and forms a connection with the Hoofddorpweg, which lies along the Zeilstraat.

features.opening: The Zeilstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, between the Amstelveenseweg and the Schinkel.

features.name: Koninginneweg

facts.text: A bridge called Zeilbrug over the Schinkel has connected this route since 1927.
facts.sourceQuote: Sinds 1927 ligt voor de Zeilstraat een brug over de Schinkel die meestal de Zeilbrug wordt genoemd en een verbinding vormt met de Hoofddorpweg, die in het verlengde van de Zeilstraat ligt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1927, a bridge over the Schinkel has been built for the Zeilstraat, which is usually called the Zeilbrug and forms a connection with the Hoofddorpweg, which lies along the Zeilstraat.

features.opening: The Zeilstraat is a street in Amsterdam-Zuid, between the Amstelveenseweg and the Schinkel.

features.name: Ferdinand Bolstraat

facts.text: A bakery intended for Ferdinand Bolstraat opened in 1941 as the original Maison FEBO.
facts.sourceQuote: The chain started in 1941 as a bakery called Maison FEBO. However, this bakery was not actually located on Ferdinand Bolstraat, although it was originally intended to be located there.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The chain started in 1941 as a bakery called Maison FEBO. However, this bakery was not actually located on Ferdinand Bolstraat, although it was originally intended to be located there.

facts.text: A bridge replaced a ferry in 1875, connecting the street to Amsterdam's city centre.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1875, a bridge replaced the ferry over the Singelgracht canal, connecting the Ferdinand Bolstraat to the city centre.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1875, a bridge replaced the ferry over the Singelgracht canal, connecting the Ferdinand Bolstraat to the city centre.

facts.text: Local activists successfully stopped plans from the 1960s to demolish the street for a broad boulevard.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 1960s, the city government planned to demolish the street and replace it with a broad boulevard. However, these plans were abandoned after protests from local activists, such as the politician Jan Schaefer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 1960s, the city government planned to demolish the street and replace it with a broad boulevard. However, these plans were abandoned after protests from local activists, such as the politician Jan Schaefer.

features.opening: The Ferdinand Bolstraat is a street south of the city centre of Amsterdam, named after the artist Ferdinand Bol in 1872.

features.name: Dijkgraafplein

facts.text: Line 17 returned to terminate here in 2001 after running elsewhere for thirty years.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2001, line 1 began running via a new tram track to De Aker and line 17 was again extended to the Dijkgraafplein, just as between 1962 and 1971.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2001, line 1 began running via a new tram track to De Aker and line 17 was again extended to the Dijkgraafplein, just as between 1962 and 1971.

facts.text: The surrounding neighborhood features streets named after various waterways within De Punt.
facts.sourceQuote: The Dijkgraafplein lies in the neighborhood that is now known as 'De Punt' and where many streets are named after waterways.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Dijkgraafplein lies in the neighborhood that is now known as 'De Punt' and where many streets are named after waterways.

features.opening: The Dijkgraafplein is a square in Amsterdam-Osdorp in the Netherlands, lying at the end of Tussen Meer.

features.name: Vrijheidslaan

facts.text: Vrijheidslaan means Freedom Avenue, renamed in 1956 after the Soviet invasion of Hungary.
facts.sourceQuote: Na de Sovjet-Russische inval in Hongarije in 1956 werd de straat op 14 november van dat jaar omgedoopt in Vrijheidslaan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the Soviet-Russian invasion of Hungary in 1956, the street was renamed Vrijheidslaan on November 14 of that year.

facts.text: A wide central lawn originally present here disappeared after 1950 when trams began stopping on the right.
facts.sourceQuote: Oorspronkelijk was er een breed middenplantsoenmaar in tegenstelling tot bij de Churchilllaan is dit na 1950 verdwenen toen de trams rechts gingen houden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Originally there was a wide central lawn but unlike Churchilllaan, this disappeared after 1950 when the trams started to stop on the right.

facts.text: German troops entered Amsterdam via this avenue in May 1940.
facts.sourceQuote: In mei 1940 trok de Duitse Wehrmacht via deze route de stad in, in mei 1945 volgden de Canadezen deze route en bij een herdenkingsrit in 1980 en 1985 werd dit nog eens herhaald met Canadese veteranen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In May 1940, the German Wehrmacht entered the city via this route, in May 1945 the Canadians followed this route and during a commemorative ride in 1980 and 1985 this was repeated again with Canadian veterans.

facts.text: A 1995 parade marked exactly fifty years after the city's liberation.
facts.sourceQuote: Precies 50 jaar na de bevrijding, op 7 mei 1995, werd deze optocht herhaald.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Exactly 50 years after the liberation, on May 7, 1995, this parade was repeated.

facts.text: Sixty years later, 350 veterans rode 100 World War II military vehicles down the street.
facts.sourceQuote: Nog weer tien jaar later, 60 jaar na de bevrijding, werd op 7 mei 2005 door 350 veteranen die ooit Amsterdam hadden bevrijd opnieuw een intocht gehouden. Zij reden mee op 100 militaire voertuigen uit de Tweede Wereldoorlog.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Ten years later, 60 years after the liberation, another parade was held on May 7, 2005, by 350 veterans who had once liberated Amsterdam. They rode with 100 military vehicles from World War II.

features.opening: The Vrijheidslaan (formerly Amstellaan and Stalinlaan) is a main street in Amsterdam-Zuid, which together with the Berlagebrug forms the eastern entrance to…

features.name: Westergasbrug

facts.text: A 1956 replacement moved a 1919 lifting bridge originally built for the NSM site in Amsterdam-North.
facts.sourceQuote: Die brug voldeed in 1956 niet meer en werd vervangen door een ophaalbrug uit 1919, die tot 1956 haar werk had gedaan bij het NSM-terrein in Amsterdam-Noord over het Zijkanaal I, zij werd daar vervangen door de brede NSM-brug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: That bridge no longer served in 1956 and was replaced by a lifting bridge from 1919, which had been doing its job at the NSM site in Amsterdam-North over the Side Canal I until 1956, it was replaced there by the wide NSM bridge.

facts.text: Wichert Arend de Graaf designed this structure while serving as director of the Department of Public Works.
facts.sourceQuote: De Westergasbrug is een ontwerp van Wichert Arend de Graaf, directeur van de Dienst der Publieke Werken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Westergasbrug is a design by Wichert Arend de Graaf, director of the Department of Public Works.

features.opening: The Westergasbrug (bridge 193) is an iron lifting bridge in Amsterdam-West.

features.name: Spaarndammerstraat

facts.text: The Spaarndammerstraat takes its name from the village of Spaarndam and a former municipality on the Noorder Buiten Spaarne.
facts.sourceQuote: De Spaarndammerstraat is per raadsbesluit van 20 november 1878 (geherdefinieerd in 1909 en 1913) vernoemd naar het dorp Spaarndam en voormalige gemeente aan het Noorder Buiten Spaarne.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Spaarndammerstraat was named after the village of Spaarndam and former municipality on the Noorder Buiten Spaarne by a council decision of November 20, 1878 (redefined in 1909 and 1913).

facts.text: Despite nearby expansions, the area remains underdeveloped and lacks a modern shopping appeal.
facts.sourceQuote: Ondanks de uitbreidingen van de Houthavens ten noorden van de Spaarndammerstraat lijkt de straat zijn volkse karakter te hebben behouden. Het blijft wel daardoor in ontwikkeling en uitstraling achter bij een moderne winkelstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Despite the expansions of the Houthavens north of the Spaarndammerstraat, the street seems to have retained its popular character. As a result, it remains underdeveloped and lacks the appeal of a modern shopping street.

facts.text: Supermarket chains and catering establishments have settled here within the last decade.
facts.sourceQuote: De nodige supermarktketens en horecagelegenheden hebben zich de afgelopen 10 jaar gevestigd in deze straat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The necessary supermarket chains and catering establishments have settled in this street in the past 10 years.

features.opening: The Spaarndammerstraat is a residential and shopping street in the Spaarndammerbuurt in Amsterdam Oud-West.

features.name: Lies Bakhuyzenlaan

facts.text: A garden park called VAT was built here in 1955 on former sports fields and a farm.
facts.sourceQuote: Ter plaatse kwam in 1955 hier op de plek van sportvelden en een boerderij het Tuinpark Verenigde Amateur Tuinders (VAT) te liggen, dat afkomstig was uit Slotervaart waar gebouwd werd aan de Maassluisstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On site, in 1955, the Tuinpark Verenigde Amateur Tuinders (VAT) was built here on the site of sports fields and a farm, which came from Slotervaart where construction was carried out on Maassluisstraat.

facts.text: A narrow path to the garden park became known as VAT lane due to immediate construction.
facts.sourceQuote: Om vanaf de Sloterweg het tuinpark te kunnen bereiken liep er ten westen van Sloterweg 1267-1267-C (het gebouw staat haaks op de Sloterweg) een pad dat de bijnaam VAT-laantje kreeg. Het was een vrij nauw pad, want na de opening kwam er direct weer bebouwing.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In order to reach the garden park from Sloterweg, there was a path west of Sloterweg 1267-1267-C (the building is perpendicular to Sloterweg) that was nicknamed VAT lane. It was a fairly narrow path, because after the opening there was immediately more construction.

features.opening: Lies Bakhuyzenlaan is a street in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

features.name: Coen Tunnel

facts.text: The Coen Tunnel honors Jan Pieterszoon Coen, a 17th-century colonizer.
facts.sourceQuote: The tunnel is named for the 17th-century colonizer Jan Pieterszoon Coen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tunnel is named for the 17th-century colonizer Jan Pieterszoon Coen.

facts.text: Queen Juliana officially opened the tunnel on June 21, 1966.
facts.sourceQuote: The opening of the tunnel was inaugurated on 21 June 1966 by Queen Juliana.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The opening of the tunnel was inaugurated on 21 June 1966 by Queen Juliana.

features.opening: The Coentunnel (1966) is a tunnel in the A10 motorway under the North Sea Canal in western Amsterdam.

features.name: Diepenbrockstraat

facts.text: Gretta Duisenberg repeatedly hung a Palestinian flag on her villa balcony despite protests from Jewish neighbors.
facts.sourceQuote: Zijn echtgenote Gretta trok veel bekijks door aan het balkon van hun villa aan de straatkant een Palestijnse vlag te hangen. Hiermee wilde ze haar steun betuigen aan de Palestijnen in het Midden-Oostenconflict. Na protesten van Joodse buren die de vlag provocerend vonden is de vlag weer verwijderd en een aantal keren teruggeplaatst.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: His wife Gretta attracted a lot of attention by hanging a Palestinian flag on the balcony of their villa on the street side. She wanted to express her support for the Palestinians in the Middle East conflict with this. After protests from Jewish neighbors who found the flag provocative, the flag was removed again and re-installed several times.

facts.text: Alphons Diepenbrockstraat honors composer Alphons Diepenbrock, who lived from 1862 to 1921.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat werd op 30 september 1931 vernoemd naar de componist Alphons Diepenbrock (1862-1921).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was named after the composer Alphons Diepenbrock (1862-1921) on September 30, 1931.

features.opening: The Diepenbrockstraat is a street in Amsterdam - Zuid.

features.name: Jodenbreestraat

facts.text: The southern section became Jodenbreestraat, meaning Jewish Broad Street, after 17th-century Portuguese and Spanish Jewish settlers arrived.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 17th century, many Jewish emigrants from Portugal and Spain settled in the neighbourhood, and in the second half of the century, the southern section of the Sint Antoniesbreestraat came to be known as Jodenbreestraat ("Jewish Broad Street").
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 17th century, many Jewish emigrants from Portugal and Spain settled in the neighbourhood, and in the second half of the century, the southern section of the Sint Antoniesbreestraat came to be known as Jodenbreestraat ("Jewish Broad Street").

facts.text: Rembrandt lived in a house built in 1606 on this street from 1639 to 1656, which now serves as the Rembrandthuis museum.
facts.sourceQuote: Rembrandt lived in this street, from 1631 to 1635, at the home of art dealer Hendrick van Uylenburgh, and again from 1639 to 1656, in his own house, built in 1606 and still standing today. It now houses the Rembrandthuis museum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Rembrandt lived in this street, from 1631 to 1635, at the home of art dealer Hendrick van Uylenburgh, and again from 1639 to 1656, in his own house, built in 1606 and still standing today. It now houses the Rembrandthuis museum.

facts.text: In 1893, city officials forced merchants to move their stalls from this marketplace to nearby Waterlooplein square.
facts.sourceQuote: The street served as a marketplace until the late 19th century. In 1893, the city government ordered the merchants to move their stalls to nearby Waterlooplein square.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street served as a marketplace until the late 19th century. In 1893, the city government ordered the merchants to move their stalls to nearby Waterlooplein square.

facts.text: Jodenbreestraat translates to Jewish Broad Street.
facts.sourceQuote: The Jodenbreestraat ("Jewish Broad Street") is a street in the centre of Amsterdam, which connects the Sint Antoniesluis sluice gates to the Mr.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Jodenbreestraat ("Jewish Broad Street") is a street in the centre of Amsterdam, which connects the Sint Antoniesluis sluice gates to the Mr.

facts.text: Philosopher Baruch Spinoza was born where the Mozes en Aäronkerk church now stands.
facts.sourceQuote: The philosopher Baruch Spinoza was born in a house that stood where the Mozes en Aäronkerk church now stands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The philosopher Baruch Spinoza was born in a house that stood where the Mozes en Aäronkerk church now stands.

features.opening: The Jodenbreestraat ("Jewish Broad Street") is a street in the centre of Amsterdam, which connects the Sint Antoniesluis sluice gates to the Mr. Visserplein…

features.name: Zocherstraat

facts.text: Zocherstraat honors Louis Paul Zocher, who died just days before the street received its name.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kreeg op 10 oktober 1915 haar naam, een vernoeming naar de op 7 september 1915 overleden landschapsarchitect Louis Paul Zocher, die samen met zijn vader Jan David Zocher het ontwerp maakte voor het Vondelpark.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was named on October 10, 1915, after landscape architect Louis Paul Zocher, who died on September 7, 1915, and together with his father Jan David Zocher designed the Vondelpark.

facts.text: Three other Dutch cities—Leiden, Rotterdam, and Haarlem—also feature a street named Zocherstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: Ook Leiden, Rotterdam en Haarlem kennen een Zocherstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Leiden, Rotterdam and Haarlem also have a Zocherstraat.

facts.text: A bend was added in 1918 to allow trams to enter the street from the Amstelveenseweg.
facts.sourceQuote: Die bocht was nodig om per 15 mei 1918 de trams de straat in te laten rijden richting stad (richting stad uit reden ze via de Amstelveenseweg).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: That bend was necessary to allow the trams to enter the street towards the city as of May 15, 1918 (they drove towards the city via the Amstelveenseweg).

facts.text: The tram-related bend disappeared after the Amstelveenseweg was widened between 1963 and 1964.
facts.sourceQuote: Na verbreding van de Amstelveenseweg in 1963/1964 verdween die flauwe bocht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the widening of the Amstelveenseweg in 1963/1964, that faint bend disappeared.

features.opening: The Zocherstraat is a street in Amsterdam-West.

features.name: IJburglaan

facts.text: Shallow water forced builders to use pontoons instead of floating cranes for assembly.
facts.sourceQuote: The shallowness of the water at the bridge site made it impossible to use floating cranes to lift the pre-assembled arches of the bridge into position during construction. The problem was solved by using pontoons and crawler cranes.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The shallowness of the water at the bridge site made it impossible to use floating cranes to lift the pre-assembled arches of the bridge into position during construction. The problem was solved by using pontoons and crawler cranes.

facts.text: The segmented structure resembles the skeleton of a crab.
facts.sourceQuote: The segmented appearance is based on the skeleton of a crab.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The segmented appearance is based on the skeleton of a crab.

facts.text: Alongside the Nescio Bridge, it stands as one of the neighborhood's most recognizable landmarks.
facts.sourceQuote: Alongside the Nescio Bridge which is a cycle and footbridge connecting IJburg to East Amsterdam, it is one of the neighbourhood's best known landmarks.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Alongside the Nescio Bridge which is a cycle and footbridge connecting IJburg to East Amsterdam, it is one of the neighbourhood's best known landmarks.

features.opening: The Enneüs Heerma Bridge (Dutch: Enneüs Heermabrug) is a bridge in Amsterdam, Netherlands located in the new neighbourhood of IJburg, built on seven artificial…

features.name: Blauwbrug

facts.text: Blauwbrug (Blue bridge) kept its name after 1883, honoring a vanished wooden structure painted like the Dutch flag.
facts.sourceQuote: The bridge owes its name to a wooden "blue bridge" that was there from around 1600 but no longer exists and which was painted the characteristic blue of the Dutch flag. It kept the name after 1883 when it was replaced by the spans of a new bridge which is inspired by the architecture of several of the bridges over the Seine in Paris such as Pont Alexandre III.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge owes its name to a wooden "blue bridge" that was there from around 1600 but no longer exists and which was painted the characteristic blue of the Dutch flag. It kept the name after 1883 when it was replaced by the spans of a new bridge which is inspired by the architecture of several of the bridges over the Seine in Paris such as Pont Alexandre III.

facts.text: Stone bases mimic ship bows and support columns topped with leaf motifs, masks, and the Imperial Crown of Austria.
facts.sourceQuote: The stone bridge has three openings for ships and is richly decorated. The bases are formed like ships' bows and on top columns with leaf-motifs, masks and finally the Imperial Crown of Austria, as also present in the city's coat of arms.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The stone bridge has three openings for ships and is richly decorated. The bases are formed like ships' bows and on top columns with leaf-motifs, masks and finally the Imperial Crown of Austria, as also present in the city's coat of arms.

facts.text: Lantern poles feature shipping decorations while the lanterns themselves are shaped like crowns.
facts.sourceQuote: Also the lantern poles have shipping decorations and the lanterns themselves are again in the shape of crowns.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Also the lantern poles have shipping decorations and the lanterns themselves are again in the shape of crowns.

features.opening: The Blauwbrug (English: Blue bridge) is a historic bridge in Amsterdam, Netherlands over the river Amstel.

features.name: Purmerplein

facts.text: Tuindorp Nieuwendam expanded between 1924 and 1934 to house workers.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Purmerplein vormt het centrum van Tuindorp Nieuwendam, een uitbreidingswijk met voornamelijk arbeiderswoningen die tussen 1924 en 1934 werd gebouwd onder regie van de Gemeentelijke Woningdienst Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Purmerplein forms the center of Tuindorp Nieuwendam, an expansion district with mainly worker's homes that was built between 1924 and 1934 under the direction of the Municipal Housing Service Amsterdam.

facts.text: The Municipal Housing Service Amsterdam directed the district's construction.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Purmerplein vormt het centrum van Tuindorp Nieuwendam, een uitbreidingswijk met voornamelijk arbeiderswoningen die tussen 1924 en 1934 werd gebouwd onder regie van de Gemeentelijke Woningdienst Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Purmerplein forms the center of Tuindorp Nieuwendam, an expansion district with mainly worker's homes that was built between 1924 and 1934 under the direction of the Municipal Housing Service Amsterdam.

facts.text: The Purmerweg and Purmerplein were ready when Tuindorp Nieuwendam construction began.
facts.sourceQuote: De Purmerweg en het Purmerplein (dat een onderbreking is van de Purmerweg) kwamen gereed aan het begin van de aanleg van Tuindorp Nieuwendam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Purmerweg and the Purmerplein (which is a break in the Purmerweg) were ready at the beginning of the construction of Tuindorp Nieuwendam.

facts.text: The Volendammerweg appeared in the 1930s as an alternative to the overloaded Nieuwendammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuote: De Volendammerweg volgde in de jaren 30, waarmee een alternatieve route ontstond voor de smalle en overbelaste Nieuwendammerdijk richting Zunderdorp, Schellingwoude en andere dorpen in Waterland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Volendammerweg followed in the 1930s, which created an alternative route for the narrow and overloaded Nieuwendammerdijk towards Zunderdorp, Schellingwoude and other villages in Waterland.

features.opening: The Purmerplein in Amsterdam-North is a square in the village of Nieuwendam, which has belonged to the municipality of Amsterdam since 1921.

features.name: Prinses Irenestraat

facts.text: Prinses Irenestraat honors Princess Irene, daughter of Queen Juliana.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat kreeg zijn naam in 1953 en werd genoemd naar Prinses Irene, dochter van de toenmalige koningin Juliana.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was named in 1953 and was named after Prinses Irene, daughter of the then queen Juliana.

facts.text: A pentagonal playground known as the Pentagon sits between the street and Zuidplein.
facts.sourceQuote: Tussen de straat en het Zuidplein, bij het eind van de Minervalaan, ligt een vijfhoekig speelterrein (soms "Pentagon" genoemd).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between the street and the Zuidplein, at the end of the Minervalaan, there is a pentagonal playground (sometimes called "Pentagon").

features.opening: The Prinses Irenestraat is a street in the Amsterdam district of Zuid, on the edge of the Zuidas.

features.name: Weteringpoort

facts.text: Two passages into the city were built in the Schans in 1657.
facts.sourceQuote: De sluis dateert van 1657 toen er in de Schans twee doorgangen stad-in werden aangelegd; de ander was de Leidsepoortsluis (gesloopt in 1880).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The lock dates back to 1657 when two passages into the city were built in the Schans; the other was the Leidsepoortsluis (demolished in 1880).

facts.text: A commissioner's house was built in 1842 to gain access to the city.
facts.sourceQuote: Om toegang te kunnen krijgen tot de stad werd in 1842 een commiezenhuis, later Weteringschans 30 en rijksmonument, gebouwd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In order to gain access to the city, a commissioner's house was built in 1842, later Weteringschans 30 and a national monument.

facts.text: The lock was renovated in 1858, adjusting its length, width and threshold.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1858 werd de sluis vernieuwd, waarbij lengte, breedte en drempel werden aangepast.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1858, the lock was renovated, adjusting its length, width and threshold.

facts.text: The lock is quite useless in the 20th and 21st centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: In de 20e en 21e eeuw is de sluis vrij nutteloos.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 20th and 21st centuries, the lock is quite useless.

features.opening: The Water Management Lock (lock 209) is a lock in the center of Amsterdam between Lijnbaansgracht and Singelgracht.

features.name: Nieuwe Keizersgracht

facts.text: Nieuwe Keizersgracht is also known as the Jewish Keizersgracht.
facts.sourceQuote: This last part, the Nieuwe Keizersgracht (also called the Jewish Keizersgracht ), was located in the prosperous part of the Amsterdam Jewish quarter, as were the Nieuwe Herengracht and the Nieuwe Prinsengracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This last part, the Nieuwe Keizersgracht (also called the Jewish Keizersgracht ), was located in the prosperous part of the Amsterdam Jewish quarter, as were the Nieuwe Herengracht and the Nieuwe Prinsengracht.

features.opening: The Nieuwe Keizersgracht is a canal in Amsterdam, part of the eastern Grachtengordel (canal belt).

features.name: Leliegracht

facts.text: Leliegracht was dug after 1612 as part of the canal belt south of Brouwersgracht.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal was dug after 1612 when the canal belt was created south of the Brouwersgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was dug after 1612 when the canal belt was created south of the Brouwersgracht.

facts.text: A lock remains on the Prinsengracht side to manage different water levels.
facts.sourceQuote: The remains of a lock can be recognized on the Prinsengracht side. That lock was necessary because the water of the Prinsengracht (along with the rest of the Jordaan Canals) remained at the polder level, while the water level in the Leliegracht, Keizersgracht and Herengracht was at the higher city level.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The remains of a lock can be recognized on the Prinsengracht side. That lock was necessary because the water of the Prinsengracht (along with the rest of the Jordaan Canals) remained at the polder level, while the water level in the Leliegracht, Keizersgracht and Herengracht was at the higher city level.

facts.text: The Astoria building at the Leliegracht corner features Art Nouveau architecture built in 1905.
facts.sourceQuote: The 'Astoria' building on the corner of the Leliegracht and the Keizersgracht is an example of Art Nouveau architecture. It was built in 1905 by order of the 'Eerste Hollandse Levensverzekerings-Bank' after designs by architects Gerrit van Arkel and Herman Hendrik Baanders.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The 'Astoria' building on the corner of the Leliegracht and the Keizersgracht is an example of Art Nouveau architecture. It was built in 1905 by order of the 'Eerste Hollandse Levensverzekerings-Bank' after designs by architects Gerrit van Arkel and Herman Hendrik Baanders.

facts.text: Architects Gerrit van Arkel and Herman Hendrik Baanders designed the structure for a bank.
facts.sourceQuote: It was built in 1905 by order of the 'Eerste Hollandse Levensverzekerings-Bank' after designs by architects Gerrit van Arkel and Herman Hendrik Baanders.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was built in 1905 by order of the 'Eerste Hollandse Levensverzekerings-Bank' after designs by architects Gerrit van Arkel and Herman Hendrik Baanders.

facts.text: Twin buildings at numbers 9-11 display a clock façade in Louis Quinze style with slight width differences.
facts.sourceQuote: Leliegracht 9-11 is a typical example of a 'twin building', with a clock façade in Louis Quinze style. Although it is a twin building, the building at Leliegracht 11 is just a little wider.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Leliegracht 9-11 is a typical example of a 'twin building', with a clock façade in Louis Quinze style. Although it is a twin building, the building at Leliegracht 11 is just a little wider.

facts.text: A twin building from around 1725 at numbers 41-43 showcases neck gables in Style Louis XIV.
facts.sourceQuote: Leliegracht 41-43 (built around 1725 ) is a twin building with neck gables in Style Louis XIV.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Leliegracht 41-43 (built around 1725 ) is a twin building with neck gables in Style Louis XIV.
