features.name: IJ

facts.text: Sand bars blocked access to Amsterdam by the seventeenth century as ships grew larger.
facts.sourceQuote: By the seventeenth century, however, access to the IJ became difficult due to sand bars across its mouth, and ships becoming bigger, and it was nearly impossible for seafaring vessels to reach the city of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: By the seventeenth century, however, access to the IJ became difficult due to sand bars across its mouth, and ships becoming bigger, and it was nearly impossible for seafaring vessels to reach the city of Amsterdam.

facts.text: Oranjesluizen locks divide the waterway into an inner section connected to the North Sea and an outer extension of the IJmeer.
facts.sourceQuote: Today, the IJ is divided into two parts: To the west of the Oranjesluizen (Oranje Locks), the Binnen-IJ (inner IJ), or Afgesloten-IJ (closed IJ), is directly connected to the North Sea Canal, where the port of IJmuiden and the North Sea can be reached. To the east of the Oranjesluizen, the Buiten-IJ (outer IJ) is an extension of the IJmeer which is itself an extension of the Markermeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Today, the IJ is divided into two parts: To the west of the Oranjesluizen (Oranje Locks), the Binnen-IJ (inner IJ), or Afgesloten-IJ (closed IJ), is directly connected to the North Sea Canal, where the port of IJmuiden and the North Sea can be reached. To the east of the Oranjesluizen, the Buiten-IJ (outer IJ) is an extension of the IJmeer which is itself an extension of the Markermeer.

features.opening: The IJ (Dutch: [ɛi] ; sometimes shown on old maps as Y or Ye) is a body of water, formerly a bay, in the Dutch province of North Holland.

features.name: Sluis Haarlemmervaart

facts.text: Sluis Haarlemmervaart has been a protected national monument since 2003.
facts.sourceQuote: De sluis en het gemaal zijn sinds 2003 beschermd als rijksmonument.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The lock and the pumping station have been protected as a national monument since 2003.

features.opening: The Schutsluis Haarlemmervaart stands in the Haarlemmervaart in Amsterdam-West at Van Slingelandtstraat.

features.name: Blauwburgwal

facts.text: The name Blauwburgwal references the nearby Blauwe Brug, now known as Lijnbaansbrug.
facts.sourceQuote: When a new Lijnbaansgracht was created during the expansion, the name was changed to Blauwburgwal naar de Blauwe Brug. The Blauwe Brug (Blue Bridge) across the Singel is now called the Lijnbaansbrug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When a new Lijnbaansgracht was created during the expansion, the name was changed to Blauwburgwal naar de Blauwe Brug. The Blauwe Brug (Blue Bridge) across the Singel is now called the Lijnbaansbrug.

facts.text: Before 1612, this waterway was named Blauwburgwal Lijnbaansgracht as an extension of a street.
facts.sourceQuote: Before the city expansion of 1612, the Blauwburgwal was called Blauwburgwal Lijnbaansgracht as an extension of Lijnbaanssteeg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Before the city expansion of 1612, the Blauwburgwal was called Blauwburgwal Lijnbaansgracht as an extension of Lijnbaanssteeg.

facts.text: Blauwburgwal 22 features a unique raised bell gable with curved walls ornamented by fruit and urns.
facts.sourceQuote: It is the only example of a raised bell gable: an extra step with a small claw piece. The gable has curved side walls ornamented with fruit and urns.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is the only example of a raised bell gable: an extra step with a small claw piece. The gable has curved side walls ornamented with fruit and urns.

features.opening: The Blauwburgwal (literally: Dutch: blue fortress wall) is a canal in Amsterdam between the Singel (at Lijnbaanssteeg) and the Herengracht (at Herenstraat).

features.name: Oranjesluizen

facts.text: In 1971, eighty thousand vessels passed through locks that still required forty-two human employees to operate by hand.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1971 80,000 vessels passed the locks, but they were still operated by hand, requiring 42 employees.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1971 80,000 vessels passed the locks, but they were still operated by hand, requiring 42 employees.

facts.text: The dam's base spanned 45 meters while its top narrowed to just 4 meters.
facts.sourceQuote: The dam through the IJ was 45 m wide at the base, and 4 m at the top.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The dam through the IJ was 45 m wide at the base, and 4 m at the top.

facts.text: Construction began with an interwoven fascine mattress laid over the entire dam breadth.
facts.sourceQuote: The dam was constructed by first putting a 2 ft 6 in (0.8 m) thick mattress of interwoven fascines (rijshout) over the whole breadth of the dam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The dam was constructed by first putting a 2 ft 6 in (0.8 m) thick mattress of interwoven fascines (rijshout) over the whole breadth of the dam.

facts.text: Two sections of the foundational grondstukken later broke, causing significant sinking.
facts.sourceQuote: In two places these grondstukken would later break, causing considerable sinkage.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In two places these grondstukken would later break, causing considerable sinkage.

features.opening: The Oranje Locks are a group of locks and other water management facilities just east of Amsterdam.

features.name: Korte Prinsengracht

facts.text: A bridge known as Unicorn Lock stands alongside lock number 103 here.
facts.sourceQuote: 103) is een schutsluis in de Haarlemmerdijk tussen de Prinsengracht en de Korte Prinsengracht in Amsterdam. De sluis en bijbehorende brug Eenhoornsluis (brug nr.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 103) is a sluice gate in the Haarlemmerdijk between the Prinsengracht and the Korte Prinsengracht in Amsterdam. The lock and associated bridge Unicorn Lock (bridge no.

facts.text: Until 1872, this canal section connected directly to the Zuiderzee via the IJ.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot de bouw van de Oranjesluizen (in gebruik genomen in 1872) stond dit deel van de Korte Prinsengracht via het IJ in open verbinding met de Zuiderzee.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until the construction of the Orange Locks (put into use in 1872), this part of the Korte Prinsengracht was in open connection with the Zuiderzee via the IJ.

facts.text: A second surviving Huddesteen was discovered in 2013 during demolition work at De Nieuwe Brug.
facts.sourceQuote: Jarenlang dacht men dat alleen in deze Eenhoornsluis een Huddesteen bewaard is gebleven, tot in 2013 tijdens de sloop van De Nieuwe Brug over het Damrak een tweede overgebleven exemplaar werd aangetroffen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For years it was thought that only in this Unicorn Lock had a Huddesteen been preserved, until in 2013 during the demolition of De Nieuwe Brug over the Damrak a second remaining specimen was found.

features.opening: The Unicorn Lock (lock no. 103) is a lock in the Haarlemmerdijk between the Prinsengracht and the Korte Prinsengracht in Amsterdam.

features.name: Abcouder Meer

facts.text: Amsterdam acquired the southern half of Abcouder Meer in 1904 after decades of private ownership.
facts.sourceQuote: Na de opheffing van het kapittel Sint-Pieter zijn diverse particulieren eigendom van het zuidelijk deel van het meer geweest, tot Amsterdam in 1904 ook dit deel wist te verwerven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the dissolution of the chapter of St. Peter, several private individuals owned the southern part of the lake, until Amsterdam also managed to acquire this part in 1904.

facts.text: Plans to drain Abcouder Meer were proposed in the 1940s as part of work expansion measures.
facts.sourceQuote: In de jaren veertig van de twintigste eeuw waren er plannen om het meer droog te leggen in het kader van werkverruimende middelen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 1940s of the twentieth century, there were plans to drain the lake as part of work expansion measures.

facts.text: The lake reaches a maximum depth of only four meters.
facts.sourceQuote: Het Abcoudermeer is maximaal 4 meter diep.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Abcoudermeer is a maximum of 4 meters deep.

facts.text: An indoor swimming pool closed in 2016 before Abcoude opened a new one next to the station in 2021.
facts.sourceQuote: Het binnenzwembad is in 2016 eveneens gesloten en de bezoekers werden verwezen naar het binnenzwembad in Mijdrecht. Sinds 2021 beschikt Abcoude weer over een eigen zwembad, maar nu vlak naast het station.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The indoor swimming pool was also closed in 2016 and visitors were referred to the indoor swimming pool in Mijdrecht. Since 2021, Abcoude has again had its own swimming pool, but now right next to the station.

facts.text: A rocky shallow area is separated from deeper water by two rows of underwater gully valleys.
facts.sourceQuote: Het ondiepe gedeelte van het meer met een rotsachtige bodem is afgescheiden door een tweetal rijen dukdalfen, deels onder water, waarna het diepe gedeelte wordt bereikt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The shallow part of the lake with a rocky bottom is separated by two rows of gully valleys, partly underwater, after which the deep part is reached.

facts.text: The northern bank marks the border between the provinces of Utrecht and North Holland.
facts.sourceQuote: De noordoever van het Abcoudermeer vormt de grens tussen de provincies Utrecht en Noord-Holland.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The northern bank of the Abcoudermeer forms the border between the provinces of Utrecht and North Holland.

features.opening: Lake in the Netherlands.

features.name: Haarlemmertrekvaart

facts.text: A railway built in 1839 rendered passenger transport on the canal obsolete.
facts.sourceQuote: A railway parallel to the canal was built in 1839 which rendered passenger transport on the Haarlemmertrekvaart obsolete.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A railway parallel to the canal was built in 1839 which rendered passenger transport on the Haarlemmertrekvaart obsolete.

facts.text: Haarlemmertrekvaart means Haarlem's Tow-Canal.
facts.sourceQuote: The Haarlemmertrekvaart [ˌhaːrlɛmərˈtrɛkfaːrt] (Haarlem's Tow-Canal) is a canal between Amsterdam and Haarlem in the province of North Holland, the Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Haarlemmertrekvaart [ˌhaːrlɛmərˈtrɛkfaːrt] (Haarlem's Tow-Canal) is a canal between Amsterdam and Haarlem in the province of North Holland, the Netherlands.

facts.text: Towpaths along the edge allowed animals or people to pull barges called trekschuit.
facts.sourceQuote: Travel on such canals was historically done by barges (or trekschuit in Dutch) which were towed by animals (and sometimes by man-power) on a path along the canal's edge (towpath).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Travel on such canals was historically done by barges (or trekschuit in Dutch) which were towed by animals (and sometimes by man-power) on a path along the canal's edge (towpath).

features.opening: The Haarlemmertrekvaart [ˌhaːrlɛmərˈtrɛkfaːrt] (Haarlem's Tow-Canal) is a canal between Amsterdam and Haarlem in the province of North Holland, the Netherlands.

features.name: Nieuwe Herengracht

facts.text: Since 1874, this canal has served as a direct shipping link between the Amstel and the Oosterdok.
facts.sourceQuote: From 1874 the Nieuwe Herengracht has been part of the shipping connection between the Amstel and the Oosterdok and the IJ respectively.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1874 the Nieuwe Herengracht has been part of the shipping connection between the Amstel and the Oosterdok and the IJ respectively.

facts.text: The waterway ran through the prosperous section of Amsterdam's historic Jewish quarter.
facts.sourceQuote: This part, the Nieuwe Herengracht, like the Nieuwe Keizersgracht and the Nieuwe Prinsengracht, ran through the prosperous part of Amsterdam's Jewish quarter.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This part, the Nieuwe Herengracht, like the Nieuwe Keizersgracht and the Nieuwe Prinsengracht, ran through the prosperous part of Amsterdam's Jewish quarter.

facts.text: A cycle tunnel on the south bank dives beneath the busy Weesperstraat road to connect districts.
facts.sourceQuote: On the south bank, a cycle tunnel dives under the busy two-lane road of Weesperstraat, to connect the Amstel with the Plantage.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the south bank, a cycle tunnel dives under the busy two-lane road of Weesperstraat, to connect the Amstel with the Plantage.

facts.text: The Hortus Botanicus moved to Nieuwe Herengracht in 1682 as a medicinal herb garden.
facts.sourceQuote: For example, in 1682 the Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam, originally intended by the Amsterdam city council as a medicinal herb garden, was moved to the Nieuwe Herengracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For example, in 1682 the Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam, originally intended by the Amsterdam city council as a medicinal herb garden, was moved to the Nieuwe Herengracht.

facts.text: Amstelhof served as a nursing home for the elderly until it closed in 2007.
facts.sourceQuote: Around 1682, at the behest of the Diaconie of the Netherlands Reformed Congregations, the Amstelhof was built between Nieuwe Herengracht and Nieuwe Keizersgracht in monumental classical style as a home for the elderly in need. The construction was made possible by a bequest and the donation of the building land by the city administration. It remained in use as a nursing home until 2007.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Around 1682, at the behest of the Diaconie of the Netherlands Reformed Congregations, the Amstelhof was built between Nieuwe Herengracht and Nieuwe Keizersgracht in monumental classical style as a home for the elderly in need. The construction was made possible by a bequest and the donation of the building land by the city administration. It remained in use as a nursing home until 2007.

features.opening: The Nieuwe Herengracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˌniu.ə ˈɦeːrə(ŋ)ˌɣrɑxt]) is a canal in Centrum district of Amsterdam.

features.name: Smallepadsgracht

facts.text: No bridges cross this canal, and no quay runs along its banks.
facts.sourceQuote: Unusually, there are no bridges over this canal, nor is there a quay that runs along the canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Unusually, there are no bridges over this canal, nor is there a quay that runs along the canal.

facts.text: Maurice, Prince of Orange advised on the defenses where this canal originated.
facts.sourceQuote: Smallepadsgracht originated in the defenses of Amsterdam added outside the Haarlemmerdijk and Hogendijk during the expansion of the city, with the active advice of Maurice, Prince of Orange.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Smallepadsgracht originated in the defenses of Amsterdam added outside the Haarlemmerdijk and Hogendijk during the expansion of the city, with the active advice of Maurice, Prince of Orange.

features.opening: The Smallepadsgracht (Narrow path canal in Dutch) is a short and narrow canal in the Amsterdam-Centrum district of Amsterdam.

features.name: Nieuwe Meersluis

facts.text: The complex originally included a lock keeper's house, two control houses at the gates, and a transformer house.
facts.sourceQuote: Het complex werd opgeleverd inclusief een sluiswachterhuis (aan de zijkant van de kolk), twee bedieningshuisjes (bij elke sluisdeur een) en een transformatorhuisje.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The complex was delivered including a lock keeper's house (on the side of the lock), two control houses (one at each lock gate) and a transformer house.

facts.text: A new control center was later built halfway over the old lock keeper's post in the late 20th century.
facts.sourceQuote: Eind 20e eeuw was er een nieuwe bedieningscentrale nodig; deze werd half over de oude sluiswachterpost heen gebouwd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the end of the 20th century, a new control center was needed; this was built halfway over the old lock keeper's post.

facts.text: Sliding sluice doors on rails also serve as the structural carriers for the bridge decks above.
facts.sourceQuote: De sluisdeuren zijn schuifdeuren op rails, de sluisdeuren zijn tevens de dragers van brugdekken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The sluice doors are sliding doors on rails, the sluice doors are also the carriers of bridge decks.

facts.text: Hunting Path runs along the west side while Ice Skating Path lies directly to the east of the lock.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de westkant van de sluis loopt het Jaagpad en aan de oostkant het IJsbaanpad.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the west side of the lock runs the Hunting Path and on the east side the Ice Skating Path.

features.opening: The Nieuwe Meersluis, also known as Schinkelsluis, is a sluice gate in the Dutch municipality of Amsterdam.

features.name: Schippersgracht

facts.text: Drinking water installation began on Schippersgracht in April 1854.
facts.sourceQuote: In April 1854 the Amsterdamsche Duinwater-Maatschappij started installation of drinking water on the Schippersgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In April 1854 the Amsterdamsche Duinwater-Maatschappij started installation of drinking water on the Schippersgracht.

facts.text: Tram line 2 ended at Schippersgracht around 1906 before being shortened.
facts.sourceQuote: Around 1906 the end of tram line 2 was on the Schippersgracht. This was canceled after six months and shortened to Central Station.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Around 1906 the end of tram line 2 was on the Schippersgracht. This was canceled after six months and shortened to Central Station.

facts.text: Herman Hendrik Baanders designed the building at number 5 in 1897.
facts.sourceQuote: The Amsterdam architect Herman Hendrik Baanders (1849–1905) designed Schippersgracht 5 (1897).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Amsterdam architect Herman Hendrik Baanders (1849–1905) designed Schippersgracht 5 (1897).

facts.text: Monumental structures from the seventeenth century stand at numbers fourteen and fifteen.
facts.sourceQuote: There are a number of monumental buildings from the 17th century on Schippersgracht, including numbers 14 and 15.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are a number of monumental buildings from the 17th century on Schippersgracht, including numbers 14 and 15.

facts.text: The architect Herman Hendrik Baanders was primarily active within Amsterdam itself.
facts.sourceQuote: Baanders was mainly active in Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Baanders was mainly active in Amsterdam.

features.opening: The Schippersgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈsxɪpərsˌxrɑxt]) is a canal and street in the Centrum district of Amsterdam that runs from the Rapenburgerplein to…

features.name: Schellingwouderbreek

facts.text: Until 1921, this lake lay within Ransdorp before that municipality was annexed by Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot 1921 lag het meertje in de gemeente Ransdorp (grenzend aan Nieuwendam) die dat jaar door Amsterdam werd geannexeerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 1921, the lake was located in the municipality of Ransdorp (adjacent to Nieuwendam) which was annexed by Amsterdam that year.

facts.text: Two small islands on the north side connect to each other and the mainland via a path.
facts.sourceQuote: In de waterpartij bevinden zich aan de noordzijde een tweetal eilandjes die onderling en met de vaste wal zijn verbonden met een pad.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the north side of the water area there are two small islands connected to each other and to the mainland by a path.

facts.text: A plaque featuring a bursting 'IJ' appeared in 2020 to highlight the crack's formation history.
facts.sourceQuote: In 2020 hebben de 'Vrienden van het Schellingwouderbreekpark' aan de kant van de Volendammerweg een gedenkplaat met een barstend 'IJ' geplaatst om te attenderen op de ontstaansgeschiedenis van de breek.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 2020, the 'Friends of the Schellingwouderbreekpark' on the side of the Volendammerweg placed a plaque with a bursting 'IJ' to draw attention to the history of the formation of the crack.

facts.text: Grassy banks serve as resting spots for many waterfowl species.
facts.sourceQuote: De grazige oevers worden door veel watervogels als rustplaats gebruikt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The grassy banks are used as a resting place by many waterfowl.

features.opening: The Schellingwouderbreek is a lake in Amsterdam-North.

features.name: Mercuriushaven

facts.text: Mercuriushaven honors Mercury, the god and personification of trade.
facts.sourceQuote: De Mercuriushaven is gegraven in het laatste deel van de 19e eeuw en is genoemd naar Mercurius als god/personificatie van de handel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Mercuriushaven was dug in the latter part of the 19th century and is named after Mercury as god/personification of trade.

features.opening: The Mercuriushaven is a port in the Amsterdam port area.

features.name: Houthaven

facts.text: Houthaven was the first Amsterdam port dug from scratch rather than using existing waters.
facts.sourceQuote: It was the first port in Amsterdam to be dug out (the earlier ones using existing waters).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was the first port in Amsterdam to be dug out (the earlier ones using existing waters).

facts.text: Parts of Houthaven were filled with sand in 1945 as lumber transport shifted to roads.
facts.sourceQuote: As lumber was increasingly transported by road, parts of the port were filled up with sand to be used for other purposes in 1945.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: As lumber was increasingly transported by road, parts of the port were filled up with sand to be used for other purposes in 1945.

facts.text: The Minervahaven section kept handling wood while other port activities sharply declined.
facts.sourceQuote: The Minervahaven remained in use for lumber transhipment and wood processing industry was located there but port-related activities decreased strongly over time.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Minervahaven remained in use for lumber transhipment and wood processing industry was located there but port-related activities decreased strongly over time.

facts.text: Houthaven literally translates to lumber port.
facts.sourceQuote: Literally meaning "lumber port", Houthaven is a port situated along the IJ in Amsterdam's western port.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Literally meaning "lumber port", Houthaven is a port situated along the IJ in Amsterdam's western port.

facts.text: The harbour consists of four distinct sections stretching from east to west.
facts.sourceQuote: The harbour is made up out of four parts (from east to west): Oude Houthaven (Old Lumber Port), Houthaven, Nieuwe Houthaven (New Lumber Port) and Minervahaven (Minerva Port).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The harbour is made up out of four parts (from east to west): Oude Houthaven (Old Lumber Port), Houthaven, Nieuwe Houthaven (New Lumber Port) and Minervahaven (Minerva Port).

features.opening: Houthaven is a neighbourhood of Amsterdam, Netherlands situated in the West borough.

features.name: Nieuwe Prinsengracht

facts.text: Until 1866, the canal extended east of the Muidergracht all the way to the Entrepotdok.
facts.sourceQuote: Until 1866 the Nieuwe Prinsengracht ran east of the Muidergracht to the Entrepotdok.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 1866 the Nieuwe Prinsengracht ran east of the Muidergracht to the Entrepotdok.

facts.text: Three ponds within the Artis zoo site remain from the section of this canal that was later filled in.
facts.sourceQuote: The three ponds within the Artis zoo site still remain from the filled-in section of the canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The three ponds within the Artis zoo site still remain from the filled-in section of the canal.

facts.text: A 1924 plate bridge spans the canal at Roetersstraat.
facts.sourceQuote: 258, a so-called plate bridge from 1924) spans the Nieuwe Prinsengracht at the Roetersstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 258, a so-called plate bridge from 1924) spans the Nieuwe Prinsengracht at the Roetersstraat.

facts.text: Buildings numbered 86 through 94 feature special architecture.
facts.sourceQuote: Due to their special architecture, the Nieuwe Prinsengracht 86-94 buildings are on the municipal monument list .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Due to their special architecture, the Nieuwe Prinsengracht 86-94 buildings are on the municipal monument list .

features.opening: The Nieuwe Prinsengracht is a canal in the Plantage neighborhood of Amsterdam, an extension of the Prinsengracht in the eastern Grachtengordel (canal belt).

features.name: Hans Snoekfontein

facts.text: Hans Snoekfontein honors Hans Snoek, founder of the Scapino Ballet, who funded its construction via a legacy.
facts.sourceQuote: De fontein is vernoemd naar Hans Snoek, oprichtster van het Scapino Ballet, die via een legaat financieel bijdroeg aan de bouw van de fontein en het opknappen van het plein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The fountain is named after Hans Snoek, founder of the Scapino Ballet, who financially contributed to the construction of the fountain and the renovation of the square through a legacy.

features.opening: The Hans Snoekfontein is a work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Bijleveldschesluis

facts.text: The tunnel runs under the Nieuwmarkt and the southeastern part of the historic Waag building.
facts.sourceQuote: Daarmee loopt ze onder de Nieuwmarkt en ook het zuidoostelijke deel van het historische gebouw Waag.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This runs under the Nieuwmarkt and also the southeastern part of the historic Waag building.

facts.text: Amsterdam took over management of the lock in July 1492 after it fell under Bijleveld control.
facts.sourceQuote: De sluis onder de Sint-Anthoniespoort (Waag) viel aanvankelijk onder het beheer van Bijleveld, maar ging in juli 1492 over naar Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The lock under the Sint-Anthoniespoort (Waag) initially fell under the management of Bijleveld, but was transferred to Amsterdam in July 1492.

facts.text: Old remains of the structure were discovered when the Nieuwmarkt was demolished between 1988 and 1990.
facts.sourceQuote: Die geschiedenis was nog deels terug te vinden toen in de periode 1988-1990 de Nieuwmarkt op de schop ging, men vond oude resten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: That history could still be found in part when the Nieuwmarkt was demolished in the period 1988-1990, old remains were found.

features.opening: The Bijleveldschesluis (bridge 495) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum.

features.name: Nieuwe Achtergracht

facts.text: Construction occurred during Amsterdam's final canal expansion east of the Amstel River.
facts.sourceQuote: The Nieuwe Achtergracht was constructed as an extension of the Achtergracht during the last expansion of the canal belt east of the Amstel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Nieuwe Achtergracht was constructed as an extension of the Achtergracht during the last expansion of the canal belt east of the Amstel.

facts.text: Economist and resistance fighter Felix Halverstad names bridge 260.
facts.sourceQuote: 260, (Nieuwe Achtergracht / Roetersstraat) is named after the economist and resistance fighter Felix Halverstad.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 260, (Nieuwe Achtergracht / Roetersstraat) is named after the economist and resistance fighter Felix Halverstad.

features.opening: The Nieuwe Achtergracht is a canal in Amsterdam in the east of the Grachtengordel (canal belt) in the Amsterdam-Centrum district.

features.name: Westerkanaalschutsluis

facts.text: The original lock culvert measured 122 meters to accommodate large ships.
facts.sourceQuote: Er kwamen grote schepen binnen, dus het werd een vrij grote schutsluis; de sluiskolk werd 122 meter.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Large ships came in, so it became a fairly large lock; the lock culvert was 122 meters long.

facts.text: A 1959 renovation extended the sluice pool to 165 meters for larger vessels.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1959 werd dan ook besloten dat de schutsluis en de onder de Westerkeersluis (brug) liggende Westerkeersluis gereed te maken voor schepen tot 2000 ton. De noordelijke sluisdeuren verhuisden verder naar het noorden tussen de Houtmandwarsstraat en de Zoutkeetsgracht; de sluiskolk werd opgerekt tot 165 meter en er kwamen aan die zijde twee doorvaarten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1959, it was therefore decided that the lock and the Westerkeersluis located under the Westerkeersluis (bridge) should be prepared for ships up to 2000 tons. The northern sluice gates were further moved north between the Houtmandwarsstraat and the Zoutkeetsgracht; the sluice pool was extended to 165 meters and two through passages were added on that side.

features.opening: The Westerkanaalschutsluis is a lock in the Westerkanaal, Amsterdam-West.

features.name: Erasmusgracht

facts.text: Seven distinct bridges span the waterway, including a railway and metro bridge crossing the Ringspoorbaan.
facts.sourceQuote: Over de gracht liggen zeven bruggen: Wil de Graaffbrug (brug 393, voetgangersbrug Wachterliedplantsoen), Saïdja en Adindabrug (brug 162, in Hoofdweg), Erasmusgrachtbrug (142P, in Einsteinweg), Voet- en fietsbrug Erasmusgracht (nabij Jacob van Arteveldestraat), Camera Obscurabrug (brug 322, fietsbrug in Leeuwendalersweg) en de spoor- en metrobrug in de Ringspoorbaan.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are seven bridges over the canal: Wil de Graaffbrug (bridge 393, pedestrian bridge Wachterliedplantsoen), Saïdja and Adindabrug (bridge 162, in Hoofdweg), Erasmusgrachtbrug (142P, in Einsteinweg), Erasmusgracht foot and bicycle bridge (near Jacob van Arteveldestraat), Camera Obscurabrug (bridge 322, bicycle bridge in Leeuwendalersweg) and the railway and metro bridge in the Ringspoorbaan.

facts.text: A helophyte filter near a pumping building features a mural titled Zuiver installed in 2021.
facts.sourceQuote: In dat doodlopende stukje gracht ligt een helofytenfilter in de nabijheid van een bemalingsgebouwtje, dat sinds 2021 voorzien is van de muurschildering Zuiver.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In that dead-end canal section, there is a helophyte filter near a pumping building, which has been equipped with the mural Zuiver since 2021.

features.opening: The Erasmusgracht in Amsterdam-West was built in the 1940s as part of the new Bos en Lommer district.

features.name: Entrepotdok

facts.text: Until 1895, goods stored here avoided import duties until released to the market.
facts.sourceQuote: Until 1895, goods could be stored temporarily in this warehouse without having to pay import duties (a type of bonded warehouse). They only had to pay duty when the goods were put on the market.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until 1895, goods could be stored temporarily in this warehouse without having to pay import duties (a type of bonded warehouse). They only had to pay duty when the goods were put on the market.

facts.text: The complex features 84 monumental warehouses built between 1708 and 1829.
facts.sourceQuote: The Entrepotdok has 84 monumental warehouses. They were built between 1708 and 1829.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Entrepotdok has 84 monumental warehouses. They were built between 1708 and 1829.

facts.text: Around 1890, the dock lost its warehouse function after a new facility opened nearby.
facts.sourceQuote: The dock lost its function as a warehouse for undeclared goods around 1890 due to construction of the Nieuwe Entrepotdok on the Cruquiusweg, and the buildings were empty for a long time.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The dock lost its function as a warehouse for undeclared goods around 1890 due to construction of the Nieuwe Entrepotdok on the Cruquiusweg, and the buildings were empty for a long time.

facts.text: The name Entrepotdok translates to Warehouse Dock.
facts.sourceQuote: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name along the northeast side of the canal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Entrepotdok (Warehouse Dock), formerly Nieuwe Rapenburgergracht, is a canal in Amsterdam, and a street and row of former warehouses with the same name along the northeast side of the canal.

facts.text: Construction of these warehouses spanned from 1708 until 1829 across two centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.

facts.text: Squatters occupied the complex during the 1990s before it became residential apartments.
facts.sourceQuote: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: They were constructed between 1708 and 1829, used for storage, squatted in the 1990s and are now converted into apartments.

features.name: Westlandgracht

facts.text: The Westlandgracht honors the Westland region west of Delft and south of The Hague.
facts.sourceQuote: De Westlandgracht is een oppervlaktewater, een straat en tot 1962 de naam van een wijk en is genoemd naar het Westland, het gebied ten westen van Delft en ten zuiden van Den Haag.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Westlandgracht is a surface water, a street and until 1962 the name of a district and is named after the Westland, the area west of Delft and south of The Hague.

facts.text: Amsterdam built this canal in the 1920s on former Sloten territory annexed in 1921.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht kreeg zijn naam in 1933 en werd aangelegd in de jaren 1920 op het grondgebied van de in 1921 geannexeerde gemeente Sloten. Deze gemeente had al plannen voor een nieuwbouwwijk ten westen van de Sloterkade, deze werden in gewijzigde vorm uitgevoerd door de gemeente Amsterdam als onderdeel van Plan West.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was named in 1933 and was built in the 1920s on the territory of the municipality of Sloten, which was annexed in 1921. This municipality already had plans for a new residential area west of the Sloterkade, these were carried out in a modified form by the municipality of Amsterdam as part of Plan West.

facts.text: A sluice near Heemstedestraat separates water levels at NAP -0.40 from polder level at NAP -2.10.
facts.sourceQuote: Nabij de Heemstedestraat en de Delflandlaan ligt de Westlandgrachtschutsluis, die de peilscheiding vormt tussen het stadsboezempeil van de Westlandgracht (NAP -0.40) en de Slotervaart op polderpeil (NAP -2.10).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Near Heemstedestraat and Delflandlaan is the Westlandgrachtschutsluis, which forms the water level separation between the urban basin water level of the Westlandgracht (NAP -0.40) and the Slotervaart at polder level (NAP -2.10).

features.opening: The Westlandgracht is a surface water, a street and until 1962 the name of a district and is named after the Westland, the area west of Delft and south of The…

features.name: Grimburgwal

facts.text: The name Grimburgwal combines 'Grim' for muddy ditch with 'burgwal' for the protective earthen wall.
facts.sourceQuote: The Grimburgwal was originally a tributary of the Amstel, the Grim (meaning "muddy ditch"). In the 14th century it was dug into a moat with an earthen wall ("burgwal") to protect the medieval city.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Grimburgwal was originally a tributary of the Amstel, the Grim (meaning "muddy ditch"). In the 14th century it was dug into a moat with an earthen wall ("burgwal") to protect the medieval city.

facts.text: Rembrandt sketched the Grimnessesluis lock before it was demolished in 1868.
facts.sourceQuote: This lock, sketched by Rembrandt, remained until it was demolished in 1868.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This lock, sketched by Rembrandt, remained until it was demolished in 1868.

facts.text: The Nes canal still runs between buildings today, mimicking the path of the former lock.
facts.sourceQuote: The Nes still runs between buildings to the water, reminiscent of the former lock.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Nes still runs between buildings to the water, reminiscent of the former lock.

facts.text: Huis aan de Drie Grachten features a stepped gable on each of its three canal sides.
facts.sourceQuote: This building from 1610 owes its name to the fact that it is surrounded on three sides by canals: the Grimburgwal on the south side, the Oudezijds Voorburgwal on the west side and the Oudezijds Achterburgwal on the east side. It is a double house with a stepped gable on each canal .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This building from 1610 owes its name to the fact that it is surrounded on three sides by canals: the Grimburgwal on the south side, the Oudezijds Voorburgwal on the west side and the Oudezijds Achterburgwal on the east side. It is a double house with a stepped gable on each canal .

facts.text: During WWII, the August Aimé Balkema bookstore here illegally published literature.
facts.sourceQuote: During World War II the August Aimé Balkema bookstore in the House on the Three Canals was a clandestine publisher of illegal literature.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During World War II the August Aimé Balkema bookstore in the House on the Three Canals was a clandestine publisher of illegal literature.

features.opening: The Grimburgwal is a small canal and street in the center of Amsterdam.

features.name: Kloveniersburgwal

facts.text: Kloveniersburgwal derives its name from the 'kloveniers', a civic guard division armed with arquebus-style guns.
facts.sourceQuote: The name 'Kloveniersburgwal' comes from a division of the civic guards, the 'kloveniers', named after the gun the guards were armed with.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name 'Kloveniersburgwal' comes from a division of the civic guards, the 'kloveniers', named after the gun the guards were armed with.

facts.text: In February 1941, this canal became the border of the segregated Jewish quarter during World War II.
facts.sourceQuote: During the Second World War, starting in February 1941, Kloveniersburgwal was the border of the Jewish quarter, segregated by the Germans.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During the Second World War, starting in February 1941, Kloveniersburgwal was the border of the Jewish quarter, segregated by the Germans.

facts.text: The Trippenhuis at number 29 dates back to 1662.
facts.sourceQuote: There are some historically important monuments located at Kloveniersburgwal, for example: 'The Trippenhuis' (1662), KLoveniersburgwal 29; The former church from the 'Evangelisch-Lutherse Gemeente ', Kloveniersburwal 50; 'The Bushuis' (1890) between 'The Compagnietheater' and Oude Hoogstraat; 'The Huis Joan Poppen' (1642), which is also called 'The Gulden Steur', Kloveniersburgwal 95; A part of the former Binnengasthuis; The entrance of Oudemanhuispoort.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are some historically important monuments located at Kloveniersburgwal, for example: 'The Trippenhuis' (1662), KLoveniersburgwal 29; The former church from the 'Evangelisch-Lutherse Gemeente ', Kloveniersburwal 50; 'The Bushuis' (1890) between 'The Compagnietheater' and Oude Hoogstraat; 'The Huis Joan Poppen' (1642), which is also called 'The Gulden Steur', Kloveniersburgwal 95; A part of the former Binnengasthuis; The entrance of Oudemanhuispoort.

facts.text: Huis Joan Poppen, also known as Gulden Steur, was built in 1642.

facts.text: The Bushuis structure on this street was completed in 1890.

facts.text: A former church once served the Evangelisch-Lutherse Gemeente here.
facts.sourceQuote: There are some historically important monuments located at Kloveniersburgwal, for example: 'The Trippenhuis' (1662), KLoveniersburgwal 29; The former church from the 'Evangelisch-Lutherse Gemeente ', Kloveniersburwal 50; 'The Bushuis' (1890) between 'The Compagnietheater' and Oude Hoogstraat; 'The Huis Joan Poppen' (1642), which is also called 'The Gulden Steur', Kloveniersburgwal 95; A part of the former Binnengasthuis; The entrance of Oudemanhuispoort.

features.name: Plantage Muidergracht

facts.text: A section of the original waterway was filled in 1873 to create Jonas Daniël Meijerplein.
facts.sourceQuote: Part of the Muidergracht was filled in in 1873 and is now the Jonas Daniël Meijerplein and the Hortusplantsoen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Part of the Muidergracht was filled in in 1873 and is now the Jonas Daniël Meijerplein and the Hortusplantsoen.

facts.text: The stretch along Sarphatistraat was formerly known as Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.
facts.sourceQuote: The part of the current Plantage Muidergracht that runs along Sarphatistraat, was an extension of the Lijnbaansgracht and was called the Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The part of the current Plantage Muidergracht that runs along Sarphatistraat, was an extension of the Lijnbaansgracht and was called the Plantage Lijnbaansgracht before 1915.

facts.text: Poet Adriaan Morriën lived at number 3 and titled one of his memoirs after this location.
facts.sourceQuote: The Dutch poet and essayist Adriaan Morriën (1912–2002) lived at Plantage Muidergracht 3 and also named part one of his memoirs: Plantage Muidergracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Dutch poet and essayist Adriaan Morriën (1912–2002) lived at Plantage Muidergracht 3 and also named part one of his memoirs: Plantage Muidergracht.

facts.text: Formerly housing physics and biology courses, these buildings now serve other university faculties.
facts.sourceQuote: On and along the Plantage Muidergracht, near Roeterseiland, are some of the buildings of the University of Amsterdam, originally built for courses or subfaculties of physics, chemistry, biology, environmental science and mathematics, but now used by other faculties.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On and along the Plantage Muidergracht, near Roeterseiland, are some of the buildings of the University of Amsterdam, originally built for courses or subfaculties of physics, chemistry, biology, environmental science and mathematics, but now used by other faculties.

features.opening: The Plantage Muidergracht is a canal and street in the Plantage neighborhood of Amsterdam.

features.name: Rokin

facts.text: A stone column made of chapel remnants was temporarily moved during metro works.
facts.sourceQuote: The Mirakelkolom, which normally stands on the Rokin, was temporarily removed during the construction of the metro line. The Mirakelkolom is a stone column made up of remnants of the Heilige Stede (Nieuwezijds Kapel), a chapel built to commemorate the 1345 Mirakel van Amsterdam (Miracle of the Host).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Mirakelkolom, which normally stands on the Rokin, was temporarily removed during the construction of the metro line. The Mirakelkolom is a stone column made up of remnants of the Heilige Stede (Nieuwezijds Kapel), a chapel built to commemorate the 1345 Mirakel van Amsterdam (Miracle of the Host).

facts.text: A tobacco shop has served as a royal purveyor of cigars since 1826.
facts.sourceQuote: Tobacco shop Hajenius at Rokin 92-96, royal purveyor of cigars and other tobacco goods since 1826.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Tobacco shop Hajenius at Rokin 92-96, royal purveyor of cigars and other tobacco goods since 1826.

facts.text: An optician shop features a rooftop statue of a monkey with binoculars.
facts.sourceQuote: Magazijn De Gouden Bril, the oldest remaining optician in the Netherlands, at Rokin 72. There is a statue of a monkey with binoculars on the rooftop.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Magazijn De Gouden Bril, the oldest remaining optician in the Netherlands, at Rokin 72. There is a statue of a monkey with binoculars on the rooftop.

facts.text: The central bank once occupied the building now housing an antiquities museum.
facts.sourceQuote: The Allard Pierson Museum for antiquities, on the Oude Turfmarkt, in the former headquarters of the Nederlandsche Bank, the Dutch central bank.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Allard Pierson Museum for antiquities, on the Oude Turfmarkt, in the former headquarters of the Nederlandsche Bank, the Dutch central bank.

features.opening: The Rokin is a canal and major street in the centre of Amsterdam.

features.name: Raamgracht

facts.text: Journalist Igor Cornelissen wrote a book titled Raamgracht 4 about his editorship in the 1960s.
facts.sourceQuote: Journalist Igor Cornelissen wrote the book Raamgracht 4 about his time as editor of Vrij Nederland in the 1960s.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Journalist Igor Cornelissen wrote the book Raamgracht 4 about his time as editor of Vrij Nederland in the 1960s.

facts.text: Poet Hugo Claus and actress Sylvia Kristel lived together at Raamgracht 5-7 in the early 1970s.
facts.sourceQuote: In the early 1970s, the poet and writer Hugo Claus, together with his then muse, the actress Sylvia Kristel, occupied the Raamgracht 5-7 building.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the early 1970s, the poet and writer Hugo Claus, together with his then muse, the actress Sylvia Kristel, occupied the Raamgracht 5-7 building.

facts.text: Raamgracht recalls weaving mills where wool was stretched on wooden frames (raamen) to dry.
facts.sourceQuote: At that time there were weaving mills in the area, where after washing, carding, spinning, weaving and dying the woolen fabric was stretched on wooden frames (raamen) to dry and stretch. The names Raamgracht, Ververstraat and Staalstraat recall that period.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At that time there were weaving mills in the area, where after washing, carding, spinning, weaving and dying the woolen fabric was stretched on wooden frames (raamen) to dry and stretch. The names Raamgracht, Ververstraat and Staalstraat recall that period.

facts.text: A 1625 map labeled this waterway Verwers Graft, or Dyers Canal, rather than Raamgracht.
facts.sourceQuote: On a map from 1625 by Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode the canal is called the "Verwers Graft" (Dyers Canal).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On a map from 1625 by Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode the canal is called the "Verwers Graft" (Dyers Canal).

facts.text: The Pentagon building by Theo Bosch now stands where north-side structures were demolished for a metro line.
facts.sourceQuote: Afterwards, part of the buildings on the north side of the Raamgracht was demolished for the construction of the Oostlijn metro line. The Pentagon designed by Theo Bosch was then built here.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Afterwards, part of the buildings on the north side of the Raamgracht was demolished for the construction of the Oostlijn metro line. The Pentagon designed by Theo Bosch was then built here.

features.opening: The Raamgracht (Frame Canal) is a canal in central Amsterdam that runs from the Kloveniersburgwal to the Zwanenburgwal.

features.name: Bickersgracht

facts.text: Bickersgracht takes its name from Jan Bicker, who purchased the island in 1631.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal is named after Jan Bicker, who bought Bickerseiland in 1631.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is named after Jan Bicker, who bought Bickerseiland in 1631.

facts.text: Shipyards and timber sheds were erected along this canal and the Westerdok.
facts.sourceQuote: A number of shipyards, sheds and places to store timber were erected along the Bickersgracht and Westerdok.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A number of shipyards, sheds and places to store timber were erected along the Bickersgracht and Westerdok.

facts.text: A towered house was built on the island for the shipping magnate Bicker.
facts.sourceQuote: In the middle of the island a house with a tower was built for the shipping magnate Bicker.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the middle of the island a house with a tower was built for the shipping magnate Bicker.

facts.text: The towered house was demolished around 1700 to make way for more residences.
facts.sourceQuote: This building was demolished around 1700 to make way for more houses.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This building was demolished around 1700 to make way for more houses.

facts.text: The Galgenbrug changed from a movable bascule bridge to a fixed structure.
facts.sourceQuote: 315) was constructed between Galgenstraat on Prinseneiland and Kleine Bickersstraat on Bickerseiland. From the street and the bridge, originally a bascule bridge, now a fixed bridge, one had a good view of the gallows of the Volewijck, north of the IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 315) was constructed between Galgenstraat on Prinseneiland and Kleine Bickersstraat on Bickerseiland. From the street and the bridge, originally a bascule bridge, now a fixed bridge, one had a good view of the gallows of the Volewijck, north of the IJ.

features.opening: The Bickersgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈbɪkərsˌxrɑxt]) is a canal in the center of Amsterdam at Westelijke Eilanden (Western Islands), but also a street.

features.name: Gaasperplas

facts.text: The lake reaches a depth of 35 metres where sand was extracted for the Bijlmer district.
facts.sourceQuote: Gaasperplas was created with the extraction of sand for the construction of the Bijlmer. At its deepest the lake is 35 metres deep.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Gaasperplas was created with the extraction of sand for the construction of the Bijlmer. At its deepest the lake is 35 metres deep.

facts.text: Official naturism has been permitted on the northern shore since the year 2005.
facts.sourceQuote: The section for naturism (officially since 2005) lies on the northern side.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The section for naturism (officially since 2005) lies on the northern side.

features.opening: Gaasperplas is an artificial lake used for recreational purposes south-east of Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

features.name: Burgemeester Cramergracht

facts.text: Two eight-floor gallery flats built in 1956-58 dominate the street on a garage base.
facts.sourceQuote: De straat wordt gedomineerd door twee in 1956-'58 gebouwde (bijna) identieke galerijflats van acht woonlagen op een onderbouw van garages en bergingen, ontworpen door architect Piet Zanstra.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street is dominated by two (almost) identical gallery flats of eight floors built in 1956-'58 on a base of garages and storage rooms, designed by architect Piet Zanstra.

facts.text: A nearby lock separates the urban water level from the Sloterplas polder level by nearly two meters.
facts.sourceQuote: Nabij de Burgemeester van Tienhovengracht ligt de schutsluis Cramergrachtsluis, die de peilscheiding vormt tussen het stadspeil van de Erasmusgracht / Burgemeester van Tienhovengracht (NAP -0.40) en de Sloterplas op polderpeil (NAP -2.10).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Near the Burgemeester of Tienhovengracht is the Cramergrachtsluis lock, which forms the water level separation between the urban water level of the Erasmusgracht / Burgemeester of Tienhovengracht (NAP -0.40) and the Sloterplas at polder level (NAP -2.10).

facts.text: The name Burgemeester Cramergracht honors Willem Daniël Cramer, who served as Amsterdam's mayor from 1836 to 1841.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht kreeg zijn naam in 1952 en werd genoemd naar Willem Daniël Cramer (1788-1856), burgemeester van Amsterdam van 1836 tot 1841.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was named in 1952 and was named after Willem Daniël Cramer (1788-1856), mayor of Amsterdam from 1836 to 1841.

features.opening: The Burgemeester Cramergracht is a canal and a street running parallel to it in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

features.name: Dijksgracht

facts.text: A railway line to Utrecht runs directly on the dike body itself.
facts.sourceQuote: The railway line from Amsterdam Centraal station to Utrecht and Hilversum is located on the dike body itself.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The railway line from Amsterdam Centraal station to Utrecht and Hilversum is located on the dike body itself.

facts.text: Singer Ramses Shaffy lived in a houseboat here during the 1970s.
facts.sourceQuote: One of the most famous residents of Dijksgracht was singer Ramses Shaffy, who lived in one of these houseboats in the 1970s.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: One of the most famous residents of Dijksgracht was singer Ramses Shaffy, who lived in one of these houseboats in the 1970s.

facts.text: The Kop Dijksgracht end features an indoor climbing wall and vegetable garden.
facts.sourceQuote: The beginning of the Dijksgracht, the so-called Kop Dijksgracht, contains a number of facilities including an indoor climbing wall, a restaurant, the Mediamatic cultural institution and the 'Shaffy's Garden' neighborhood vegetable garden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The beginning of the Dijksgracht, the so-called Kop Dijksgracht, contains a number of facilities including an indoor climbing wall, a restaurant, the Mediamatic cultural institution and the 'Shaffy's Garden' neighborhood vegetable garden.

facts.text: The name Dijksgracht combines Dijk (Dike) and Gracht (Canal).
facts.sourceQuote: The Dijksgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈdɛiksˌxrɑxt]; Dike Canal) is a canal in the center of Amsterdam, north of the three Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern Islands).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Dijksgracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈdɛiksˌxrɑxt]; Dike Canal) is a canal in the center of Amsterdam, north of the three Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern Islands).

facts.text: A street adjacent to the water shares the exact same name.
facts.sourceQuote: It is also the name of the adjacent street.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is also the name of the adjacent street.
