features.name: Nieuwendammersluis

facts.text: A bakery specializing in duivekater sweet bread occupied the stone house at number 301 until 1974.
facts.sourceQuote: Rond de sluis staan vier gebouwen: een houten huis op Nieuwendammerdijk 297, rijksmonument, sinds 1904 is hier het café 't Sluisje gevestigd; een stenen huis op 301, waarin tot 1974 een bakkerij was gevestigd van de familie Kroese, gespecialiseerd in duivekater, een traditioneel soort zoet brood uit de regio; een houten huis op 303, rijksmonument; het stenen sluiswachtershuis op 270, aan de "Grote Haven".
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Around the lock there are four buildings: a wooden house on Nieuwendammerdijk 297, a national monument, since 1904 the café 't Sluisje has been located here; a stone house on 301, in which until 1974 a bakery was located of the Kroese family, specializing in duivekater, a traditional type of sweet bread from the region; a wooden house on 303, a national monument; the stone lock keeper's house on 270, on the "Grote Haven".

facts.text: Sundays in summer feature the Nieuwendammerbootje ferry stopping directly at the lock.
facts.sourceQuote: In de zomermaanden is er op zondag een bootverbinding, het IJ-buurtveer, ook bekend als het Nieuwendammerbootje, met een halte bij de sluis.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the summer months, there is a boat connection on Sundays, the IJ neighborhood ferry, also known as the Nieuwendammerbootje, with a stop at the lock.

facts.text: A fixed bridge integrated into the Nieuwendammerdijk forms part of the lock structure.
facts.sourceQuote: Onderdeel van de sluis is een vaste brug in de Nieuwendammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Part of the lock is a fixed bridge in the Nieuwendammerdijk.

facts.text: Municipal authorities assigned the specific identifier number 368 to this particular bridge section.
facts.sourceQuote: Deze brug heeft van de gemeente Amsterdam het brugnummer 368 gekregen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This bridge has been given the bridge number 368 by the municipality of Amsterdam.

features.opening: The Nieuwendammersluis is a historic lock in the Nieuwendammerdijk in Amsterdam-North.

features.name: Recht Boomssloot

facts.text: The canal was closed in 1538 to block an attack by Guelders without compensation to its builder.
facts.sourceQuote: When Boom was given permission to dig the Rechtboomssloot and Kromboomssloot, he had to allow the Rechtboomssloot to be closed in the event of danger, without the city having to pay compensation to Boom for this. In 1538 the canal was closed due to an impending attack by Guelders.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When Boom was given permission to dig the Rechtboomssloot and Kromboomssloot, he had to allow the Rechtboomssloot to be closed in the event of danger, without the city having to pay compensation to Boom for this. In 1538 the canal was closed due to an impending attack by Guelders.

facts.text: Shipbuilder Cornelis Boom widened two ditches into canals around 1530 to connect his shipyard with the IJ.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal is named after the 16th-century shipbuilder Cornelis Boom. Boom, who lived at the Rechtboomssloot (at numbers 1 to 3), had two ditches, the Rechtboomssloot and Kromboomssloot, widened into canals around 1530 to connect his shipyard on the Lastage with the IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is named after the 16th-century shipbuilder Cornelis Boom. Boom, who lived at the Rechtboomssloot (at numbers 1 to 3), had two ditches, the Rechtboomssloot and Kromboomssloot, widened into canals around 1530 to connect his shipyard on the Lastage with the IJ.

facts.text: The Fa Yin Chinese Association has taught language and hosted activities for seniors at number 5 since 1978.
facts.sourceQuote: The Fa Yin Chinese Association in the Netherlands has been located at Rechtboomssloot 5 since 1978. The association organizes Chinese language education and socio-cultural activities for Chinese elderly people.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Fa Yin Chinese Association in the Netherlands has been located at Rechtboomssloot 5 since 1978. The association organizes Chinese language education and socio-cultural activities for Chinese elderly people.

facts.text: National monuments along the route include De Rode Leeuw from 1726 and De Mouterij from the 19th century.
facts.sourceQuote: There are a number of national monuments along the Rechtboomssloot such as De Rode Leeuw (1726), Recht Boomssloot 36-40 (18th century) and De Mouterij (19th century) at Recht Boomssloot 28 / Zakslootje 16.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are a number of national monuments along the Rechtboomssloot such as De Rode Leeuw (1726), Recht Boomssloot 36-40 (18th century) and De Mouterij (19th century) at Recht Boomssloot 28 / Zakslootje 16.

features.opening: The Rechtboomssloot, or Recht Boomssloot, is a canal in the Lastage (Nieuwmarktbuurt) neighborhood in the center of Amsterdam.

features.name: Buiksloterkanaal

facts.text: Excavation of this canal occurred in 1926 within the Buiksloterham polder.
facts.sourceQuote: Het kanaal werd in 1926 gegraven in de polder Buiksloterham.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal was dug in 1926 in the polder Buiksloterham.

facts.text: Six distinct bridges span the canal, including the Wasknijper and Leeuwenputbrug.
facts.sourceQuote: De Wasknijper (brug 177 in de Distelweg), de Leeuwenputbrug (371) (Grasweg), de Van der Pekbrug (995), de Elsje Christiaensbrug (2474) (Tolhuisweg), de Galgenveldbrug (188) en de Volewijckbrug (2475) overspannen het kanaal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Wasknijper (bridge 177 in the Distelweg), the Leeuwenputbrug (371) (Grasweg), the Van der Pekbrug (995), the Elsje Christiaensbrug (2474) (Tolhuisweg), the Galgenveldbrug (188) and the Volewijckbrug (2475) span the canal.

features.opening: The Buiksloterkanaal in Amsterdam-North is the connection between the (western part of the) Johan van Hasselt Canal and the IJ.

features.name: Oudezijds Voorburgwal

facts.text: The name Oudezijds Voorburgwal reflects its origin as the inner rampart behind the city's original moat.
facts.sourceQuote: To protect the city, a moat was dug on each side with a burgwal behind it, an earthen wall, with a wooden palisade for protection. When new ramparts were constructed behind these ramparts around 1385, on both the old and new sides the existing rampart became the Voorburgwal and the new rampart became the Achterburgwal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: To protect the city, a moat was dug on each side with a burgwal behind it, an earthen wall, with a wooden palisade for protection. When new ramparts were constructed behind these ramparts around 1385, on both the old and new sides the existing rampart became the Voorburgwal and the new rampart became the Achterburgwal.

facts.text: During the 17th and 18th centuries, this canal was commonly known by the name Fluwelenburgwal.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 17th and 18th centuries the canal was usually called the Fluwelenburgwal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 17th and 18th centuries the canal was usually called the Fluwelenburgwal.

facts.text: Golden Age mansions along the canal originally featured private gardens that have since almost entirely vanished.
facts.sourceQuote: When the buildings on the Oudezijds Voorburgwal were built in the Golden Age, canal gardens were laid out behind the mansions. Almost all of them have since disappeared.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When the buildings on the Oudezijds Voorburgwal were built in the Golden Age, canal gardens were laid out behind the mansions. Almost all of them have since disappeared.

facts.text: A single bridge divides the noisy northern Wallendeel from the quiet southern section of this canal.
facts.sourceQuote: The bridge over the OZ Voorburgwal between Damstraat and Oude Doelenstraat (bridge 204) forms a clear dividing line between the noisy northern Wallendeel and the quiet southern part.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bridge over the OZ Voorburgwal between Damstraat and Oude Doelenstraat (bridge 204) forms a clear dividing line between the noisy northern Wallendeel and the quiet southern part.

facts.text: Monumental Golden Age houses stand alongside the remains of medieval monasteries that once occupied this site.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal is also lined with monumental canal houses from the Dutch Golden Age, and the remains of the many monasteries that were located here in the Middle Ages.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is also lined with monumental canal houses from the Dutch Golden Age, and the remains of the many monasteries that were located here in the Middle Ages.

features.opening: The Oudezijds Voorburgwal, often abbreviated to OZ Voorburgwal, is a street and canal in De Wallen in the center of Amsterdam.

features.name: De Kom

facts.text: Hildo Krop created sculptures for all four bridges that cross the waterways at this junction.
facts.sourceQuote: Hildo Krop maakte voor alle vier bruggen beeldhouwwerken.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Hildo Krop made sculptures for all four bridges.

facts.text: Rowing club De Amstel maintains its building alongside the Apollo Hotel and Apollohall at this spot.
facts.sourceQuote: De opvallendste gebouwen aan "De Kom" zijn het Apollo Hotel Amsterdam, de Apollohal en het gebouw van de roeivereniging De Amstel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The most striking buildings on "De Kom" are the Apollo Hotel Amsterdam, the Apollohall and the building of the rowing club De Amstel.

features.opening: De Kom is an unofficial name for a body of water in Amsterdam-Zuid.

features.name: Damrak

facts.text: The name Damrak combines 'dam' with 'rak', a straight river reach.
facts.sourceQuote: The street was located on a rak (reach), a straight part of the Amstel river near a dam; hence the name.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The street was located on a rak (reach), a straight part of the Amstel river near a dam; hence the name.

facts.text: A section of the avenue was filled in during the 19th century.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 19th century, a section of it was filled in.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 19th century, a section of it was filled in.

facts.text: Arriving travelers historically enter the city center along this main street.
facts.sourceQuote: It is the main street where people arriving at the station enter the centre of the city.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is the main street where people arriving at the station enter the centre of the city.

facts.text: Tram lines 4, 9, 16, and 25 all run directly down this thoroughfare.
facts.sourceQuote: Also, it is one of the two GVB tram routes from the station into the centre, with lines 4, 9, 16, and 25 running down it.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Also, it is one of the two GVB tram routes from the station into the centre, with lines 4, 9, 16, and 25 running down it.

facts.text: Damrak became a synonym for the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, much like Wall Street represents New York.
facts.sourceQuote: Because of the former stock exchange building, the monumental Beurs van Berlage, and several other buildings related to financial activities erected there in the early 20th century, the term "Damrak" has come to be a synonym for the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in the same way "Wall Street" is synonymous with the New York Stock Exchange and NASDAQ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Because of the former stock exchange building, the monumental Beurs van Berlage, and several other buildings related to financial activities erected there in the early 20th century, the term "Damrak" has come to be a synonym for the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in the same way "Wall Street" is synonymous with the New York Stock Exchange and NASDAQ.

facts.text: The former stock exchange building Beurs van Berlage now operates as a concert and exhibition hall.
facts.sourceQuote: The Beurs van Berlage now serves as a concert and exhibition hall.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Beurs van Berlage now serves as a concert and exhibition hall.

features.opening: The Damrak is an avenue and partially filled in canal at the centre of Amsterdam, Netherlands, running between Amsterdam Centraal in the north and Dam Square…

features.name: Achtergracht

facts.text: Twelve warehouses on Achtergracht bear the names of calendar months.
facts.sourceQuote: Indeed, there are 13 properties of which 12 are named after the calendar months.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Indeed, there are 13 properties of which 12 are named after the calendar months.

facts.text: Three bridges originally spanned the canal at the Reguliersgracht, Utrechtsestraat, and Amstel quays.
facts.sourceQuote: Three bridges were laid over the canal. The first was in the eastern quay of the Reguliersgracht, a second in Utrechtsestraat and a third in the western quay of the Amstel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Three bridges were laid over the canal. The first was in the eastern quay of the Reguliersgracht, a second in Utrechtsestraat and a third in the western quay of the Amstel.

facts.text: Most of the canal was filled in 1870 to create Falckstraat and part of Frederiksplein.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1870 most of the canal was filled in, with the first two bridges becoming redundant. The filled-in part now forms the Falckstraat and the north side of the Frederiksplein.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1870 most of the canal was filled in, with the first two bridges becoming redundant. The filled-in part now forms the Falckstraat and the north side of the Frederiksplein.

facts.text: A later extension east of the Amstel became known as Nieuwe Achtergracht.
facts.sourceQuote: At the last extension of the canal belt east of the Amstel in the direction of the IJ, the Nieuwe Achtergracht was constructed as an extension of the Achtergracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the last extension of the canal belt east of the Amstel in the direction of the IJ, the Nieuwe Achtergracht was constructed as an extension of the Achtergracht.

features.opening: The Achtergracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈɑxtərˌɣrɑxt]) is a short canal in Amsterdam, located between Frederiksplein and the Amstel, parallel to the…

features.name: Open Havenfront

facts.text: A building called Nieuwe Stadsherberg stood on stilts in this water from 1660 to 1870.
facts.sourceQuote: Van 1660 tot 1870 stond hier de Nieuwe Stadsherberg op palen in het water bij de oude monding van de Amstel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1660 to 1870, the Nieuwe Stadsherberg stood here on stilts in the water near the old mouth of the Amstel.

facts.text: The eastern part features the Noord-Zuid-Hollands Koffiehuis along Stationseiland.
facts.sourceQuote: In het oostelijke deel van het water staat langs het Stationseiland het Noord-Zuid-Hollands Koffiehuis, in het westelijke deel zijn er aanlegplaatsen voor rondvaartboten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the eastern part of the water, along Stationseiland, is the Noord-Zuid-Hollands Koffiehuis, in the western part there are moorings for sightseeing boats.

facts.text: A new bicycle shed opened in January 2023, closing the old bike flat that stood above the water since 2001.
facts.sourceQuote: De nieuwe stalling was mede bedoeld als vervanging van de 'fietsflat', die sinds 2001 aan de westkant van het Stationsplein staat, boven het water van het Open Havenfront. Na de opening van de nieuwe fietsenstalling in januari 2023 werd de fietsflat gesloten.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The new garage was also intended as a replacement for the 'bike flat', which has been located on the west side of Stationsplein since 2001, above the water of the Open Havenfront. After the opening of the new bicycle shed in January 2023, the bicycle flat was closed.

features.opening: The Open Havenfront is the water between the Prins Hendrikkade and the Stationseiland in Amsterdam.

features.name: Amstel

facts.text: Amstel means water and solid ground, combining aam (water) with stelle (dry land).
facts.sourceQuote: The name Amstel and the older form Aemstel are derived from Amestelle, which is a compound of the words aam or ame meaning water and stelle meaning solid, high, and dry ground.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name Amstel and the older form Aemstel are derived from Amestelle, which is a compound of the words aam or ame meaning water and stelle meaning solid, high, and dry ground.

facts.text: The Van Amstel family ruled the region between the twelfth and fourteenth centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: Between the 12th and 14th centuries, the area was developed and ruled by the Van Amstel family.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between the 12th and 14th centuries, the area was developed and ruled by the Van Amstel family.

facts.text: A water board named Amstelland governed the river area from 1525 until 1990.
facts.sourceQuote: Between 1525 and 1990, the water board or hoogheemraadschap of the area through which the river flows was Amstelland (Amstel Land), a name still in use for the region.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1525 and 1990, the water board or hoogheemraadschap of the area through which the river flows was Amstelland (Amstel Land), a name still in use for the region.

facts.text: Settlements like Amsterdam and Nes aan de Amstel were named after the river itself.
facts.sourceQuote: The names of the settlements Amstelhoek (Amstel Bend), Amsterdam (Amstel Dam), Nes aan de Amstel (Headland upon Amstel), and Ouderkerk aan de Amstel (Old Church upon Amstel) on the banks of the Amstel were derived from the river's name.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The names of the settlements Amstelhoek (Amstel Bend), Amsterdam (Amstel Dam), Nes aan de Amstel (Headland upon Amstel), and Ouderkerk aan de Amstel (Old Church upon Amstel) on the banks of the Amstel were derived from the river's name.

facts.text: Liberation Day concerts, rowing matches, and the Gay Pride parade occur here annually.
facts.sourceQuote: Annually, the river is the location of the Liberation Day concert, Head of the River Amstel rowing match, and the Amsterdam Gay Pride boat parade.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Annually, the river is the location of the Liberation Day concert, Head of the River Amstel rowing match, and the Amsterdam Gay Pride boat parade.

features.opening: The Amstel (Dutch: [ˈɑmstəl] ) is a river in the province of North Holland in the Netherlands.

features.name: Krom Boomssloot

facts.text: The Krom Boomssloot honors Cornelis Boom, a 16th-century landowner and shipbuilder.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal is named after the 16th-century landowner and shipbuilder Cornelis Boom.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is named after the 16th-century landowner and shipbuilder Cornelis Boom.

facts.text: Originally ditches commissioned by Cornelis Boom, these waterways were widened to connect his Lastage shipyard with the IJ.
facts.sourceQuote: Both the Kromboomssloot and Rechtboomssloot were originally ditches that were commissioned by Cornelis Boom to be widened into canals to connect his shipyard on the Lastage with the IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Both the Kromboomssloot and Rechtboomssloot were originally ditches that were commissioned by Cornelis Boom to be widened into canals to connect his shipyard on the Lastage with the IJ.

facts.text: Architect Emanuel Marcus Rood designed this structure in the early twentieth century.
facts.sourceQuote: The Branderij, the former coffee roasting factory of Alex Meijer & Co., was designed in the early 20th century by architect Emanuel Marcus Rood (1851-1929).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Branderij, the former coffee roasting factory of Alex Meijer & Co., was designed in the early 20th century by architect Emanuel Marcus Rood (1851-1929).

features.opening: The Kromboomssloot, or Krom Boomssloot, is a canal in the Lastage (Nieuwmarktbuurt) neighborhood in the center of Amsterdam.

features.name: Noordzeekanaal

facts.text: An English contractor built the canal because no Dutch company would take on the task.
facts.sourceQuote: Since no Dutch company was willing to take on this task, the project was awarded to an English contractor.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since no Dutch company was willing to take on this task, the project was awarded to an English contractor.

facts.text: Workers lived in twig huts where disease and fights were rampant during construction.
facts.sourceQuote: The workers lived in horrid conditions, being housed in huts built from twigs, driftwood, sod, and straw, where disease, fights, and alcohol abuse were rampant.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The workers lived in horrid conditions, being housed in huts built from twigs, driftwood, sod, and straw, where disease, fights, and alcohol abuse were rampant.

facts.text: King William III officially opened the Noordzeekanaal on November 1, 1876.
facts.sourceQuote: On 1 November 1876, the North Sea Canal was officially opened by King William III of the Netherlands.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On 1 November 1876, the North Sea Canal was officially opened by King William III of the Netherlands.

facts.text: Nine auxiliary canals were dug to accommodate drainage from tributaries like the Zaan.
facts.sourceQuote: To accommodate drainage of and shipping on the tributaries of the IJ, such as the Spaarne, the Zaan, and the Nauerna Canal, nine auxiliary canals needed to be dug as well (Side Canals "A" to "I").
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: To accommodate drainage of and shipping on the tributaries of the IJ, such as the Spaarne, the Zaan, and the Nauerna Canal, nine auxiliary canals needed to be dug as well (Side Canals "A" to "I").

facts.text: Construction of the Noordzeekanaal spanned from 1865 to 1876.
facts.sourceQuote: The North Sea Canal (Dutch: Noordzeekanaal) is a Dutch ship canal from Amsterdam to the North Sea at IJmuiden, constructed between 1865 and 1876 to enable seafaring vessels to reach the port of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The North Sea Canal (Dutch: Noordzeekanaal) is a Dutch ship canal from Amsterdam to the North Sea at IJmuiden, constructed between 1865 and 1876 to enable seafaring vessels to reach the port of Amsterdam.

features.opening: The North Sea Canal (Dutch: Noordzeekanaal) is a Dutch ship canal from Amsterdam to the North Sea at IJmuiden, constructed between 1865 and 1876 to enable…

features.name: Vlothaven

facts.text: Equipment once moved 1,200 tons of grain per hour through an uninterrupted transfer system.
facts.sourceQuote: De losapparatuur maakte een onafgebroken overslag van 1200 ton graan per uur mogelijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The loose equipment made an uninterrupted transfer of 1200 tons of grain per hour possible.

facts.text: In mid-2021, OBA Bulk Terminal Amsterdam acquired all assets including cranes and weighing towers.
facts.sourceQuote: Medio 2021 kreeg OBA Bulk Terminal Amsterdam (OBA) IGMA in handen. OBA koopt alle activa, met inbegrip van alle laad- en losapparatuur zoals kranen, weegtorens, grijpers en transportsystemen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In mid-2021, OBA Bulk Terminal Amsterdam (OBA) acquired IGMA. OBA purchases all assets, including all loading and unloading equipment such as cranes, weighing towers, grippers and transport systems.

features.opening: The Vlothaven is a port in the Amsterdam Western Port Area south of the Coenhaven, north of the Nieuwe Hemweg, east of the Einsteinweg and north of the…

features.name: Syphonsluis

facts.text: A siphon named Syphonsluis exists on the north side of the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal near the Zeeburg Pump Station.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de noordkant van het Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal, in Amsterdam, loopt overigens ook een onderleider onder het Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal: de Syphonsluis bij het Gemaal Zeeburg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: By the way, there is also an underleader under the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal on the north side of the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal, in Amsterdam: the Syphonsluis near the Zeeburg Pump Station.

facts.text: Each of the 70-ton concrete tunnel sections measures 8.89 meters wide and 2.85 meters high.
facts.sourceQuote: De tunnel bestaat uit geprefabriceerde betonnen elementen van 3 meter lang, 2,85 meter hoog en 8,89 meter breed. Met deze elementen, die elk 70 ton wegen, is een tunnel gemaakt van 138 meter lengte.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tunnel consists of prefabricated concrete elements 3 meters long, 2.85 meters high and 8.89 meters wide. With these elements, each weighing 70 tons, a tunnel 138 meters long has been made.

facts.text: Factory workers cast these massive elements at Kats Prefab Beton on Noord-Beveland before transport.
facts.sourceQuote: De tunnelsegmenten zijn gebouwd bij de betonfabriek Kats Prefab Beton in Kats op het eiland Noord-Beveland, waarna ze naar de bouwlocatie vervoerd zijn en geassembleerd in de tijdelijk drooggelegde sluiskolk van de Noordersluis bij Jutphaas.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The tunnel sections were built at the Kats Prefab Beton concrete factory in Kats on the island of Noord-Beveland, after which they were transported to the construction site and assembled in the temporarily dried-up sluice canal of the Noordersluis near Jutphaas.

features.opening: The Merwedekanaal siphon is a feeder tunnel, or water transport tunnel, that connects two branches of the Merwedekanaal on the south side of the city of…

features.name: Passeerdersgracht

facts.text: Six of the eleven Jordaan canals were filled in during the 19th century, leaving Passeerdersgracht intact.
facts.sourceQuote: In the 19th century. six of the eleven Jordaan canals were filled in. Only the Bloemgracht, Egelantiersgracht, Lauriergracht, Looiersgracht and Passeerdersgracht remained, connecting to the Prinsengracht, Keizersgracht, Herengracht, Singel, Lijnbaansgracht, Brouwersgracht, Leliegracht and Leidsegracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 19th century. six of the eleven Jordaan canals were filled in. Only the Bloemgracht, Egelantiersgracht, Lauriergracht, Looiersgracht and Passeerdersgracht remained, connecting to the Prinsengracht, Keizersgracht, Herengracht, Singel, Lijnbaansgracht, Brouwersgracht, Leliegracht and Leidsegracht.

facts.text: A narrow alley called Walengang once stood between numbers 15 and 17 on the Passeerdersgracht.
facts.sourceQuote: For example, in the "Walenhoek" on the Passeerdersgracht there was the "Walengang" between numbers 15 and 17.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For example, in the "Walenhoek" on the Passeerdersgracht there was the "Walengang" between numbers 15 and 17.

facts.text: Passeerdersgracht serves as a direct connector linking the Prinsengracht with the Lijnbaansgracht.
facts.sourceQuote: The Passeerdersgracht is a short canal in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, that connects the Prinsengracht with the Lijnbaansgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Passeerdersgracht is a short canal in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, that connects the Prinsengracht with the Lijnbaansgracht.

features.opening: The Passeerdersgracht is a short canal in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, that connects the Prinsengracht with the Lijnbaansgracht.

features.name: Coenhaven

facts.text: Ships and activities unwanted in the Eastern Port Area found new space here.
facts.sourceQuote: De haven is bood ruimte aan schepen en activiteiten die in het Oostelijk Havengebied niet meer gewenst waren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The port provided space for ships and activities that were no longer desired in the Eastern Port Area.

features.opening: The Coenhaven is a port in the Amsterdam Western Port Area north of the Vlothaven, south of the North Sea Canal near the Coentunnel named after the port, east…

features.name: Ransdorper Die

facts.text: The Uitdammer Die no longer connects directly to the Markermeer but empties at the Uitdammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuote: Tegenwoordig is het Uitdammer Die niet meer rechtstreeks verbonden met het huidige Markermeer maar loopt dood op de Uitdammerdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Today, the Uitdammer Die is no longer directly connected to the current Markermeer but runs out at the Uitdammerdijk.

features.opening: The Ransdorper Die is a creek, named, in Waterland in North Holland.

features.name: Van Noordtgracht

facts.text: The council officially named this waterway Van Noordtgracht on November 20, 1878.
facts.sourceQuote: De naam werd vastgesteld bij raadsbesluit van 20 november 1878.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name was determined by council decision of November 20, 1878.

facts.text: The dividing line between this canal and Le Mairegracht lies exactly halfway between their western connection points.
facts.sourceQuote: De scheidslijn tussen de Van Noordtgracht en de Le Mairegracht ligt precies halverwege de waterverbinding tussen die twee aan de westkant.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The line of scrimmage between the Van Noordtgracht and the Le Mairegracht is exactly halfway between the water connection between those two on the west side.

features.opening: The Van Noordtgracht is a canal in the West district of Amsterdam.

features.name: Le Mairegracht

facts.text: The Le Mairegracht was named after explorer Jacob le Maire, who discovered the southern sea route.
facts.sourceQuote: De gracht is vernoemd naar Jacob le Maire (1585-1616), een ontdekkingsreiziger, die de naar hem genoemde zeestraat aan de zuidpunt van Zuid-Amerika ontdekte.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is named after Jacob le Maire (1585-1616), a explorer, who discovered the sea route named after him at the southern tip of South America.

facts.text: Both banks of this canal are officially designated as Le Mairekade.
facts.sourceQuote: De beide kaden van de gracht heten Le Mairekade.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The two banks of the canal are called Le Mairekade.

facts.text: Bridge 349 was delivered in 1964 and kept the name Noordpoolbrug until 2016.
facts.sourceQuote: Er zijn twee oeververbindingen over de Le Mairegracht: brug 349, een basculebrug (opgeleverd in 1964 en tot 2016 bekend als Noordpoolbrug; in april 2020 officieel vernoemd naar Cor Thesing) in de Houtmankade; brug 1908, vaste brug tussen de Henk Curièrekade en de Noordkaapstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are two river crossings over the Le Mairegracht: bridge 349, a bascule bridge (delivered in 1964 and known as Noordpoolbrug until 2016; officially renamed after Cor Thesing in April 2020) in the Houtmankade; bridge 1908, fixed bridge between the Henk Curièrekade and the Noordkaapstraat.

facts.text: One crossing is a bascule bridge while the other is a fixed structure.
facts.sourceQuote: Er zijn twee oeververbindingen over de Le Mairegracht: brug 349, een basculebrug (opgeleverd in 1964 en tot 2016 bekend als Noordpoolbrug; in april 2020 officieel vernoemd naar Cor Thesing) in de Houtmankade; brug 1908, vaste brug tussen de Henk Curièrekade en de Noordkaapstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are two river crossings over the Le Mairegracht: bridge 349, a bascule bridge (delivered in 1964 and known as Noordpoolbrug until 2016; officially renamed after Cor Thesing in April 2020) in the Houtmankade; bridge 1908, fixed bridge between the Henk Curièrekade and the Noordkaapstraat.

features.opening: The Le Mairegracht is a canal in the West district of Amsterdam.

features.name: Zwanenburgwal

facts.text: Rembrandt lived here from 1631 to 1635 before buying the adjacent house now known as the Rembrandthuis museum.
facts.sourceQuote: From 1631 to 1635, Rembrandt lived and worked at the home of Hendrick van Uylenburgh at the corner of Zwanenburgwal and Jodenbreestraat. In 1639 he bought the adjacent house, now the Rembrandthuis museum.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1631 to 1635, Rembrandt lived and worked at the home of Hendrick van Uylenburgh at the corner of Zwanenburgwal and Jodenbreestraat. In 1639 he bought the adjacent house, now the Rembrandthuis museum.

facts.text: An exit ran underneath an adjacent corner house, allowing Rembrandt to move his giant Night Watch canvas out onto the street.
facts.sourceQuote: Rembrandt was able to leave his house via an exit onto the Zwanenburgwal, running underneath the adjacent corner house, which enabled him to move the giant canvas of the Night Watch out of his studio.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Rembrandt was able to leave his house via an exit onto the Zwanenburgwal, running underneath the adjacent corner house, which enabled him to move the giant canvas of the Night Watch out of his studio.

facts.text: A breach in the Sint Antoniesdike in 1602 created a sluice gate that separated the Zwanenburgwal from the Oude Schans.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1602 the Sint Antoniesdijk, a dike along the eastern edge of the city, was breached to construct a sluice gate, the Sint Antoniessluis. The inner section came to be known as the Zwanenburgwal and the outer section, beyond the sluice gate, became known as the Oude Schans.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1602 the Sint Antoniesdijk, a dike along the eastern edge of the city, was breached to construct a sluice gate, the Sint Antoniessluis. The inner section came to be known as the Zwanenburgwal and the outer section, beyond the sluice gate, became known as the Oude Schans.

features.opening: The Zwanenburgwal is a canal and street in the center of Amsterdam.

features.name: Herengracht

facts.text: Herengracht means Heren Regeerders van de stad Amsterdam, the Gentlemen Governors of the city.
facts.sourceQuote: When the ditch was widened into the present canal it was given the name Herengracht in 1612, after the Heren Regeerders van de stad Amsterdam (Gentlemen Governors of the city of Amsterdam).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When the ditch was widened into the present canal it was given the name Herengracht in 1612, after the Heren Regeerders van de stad Amsterdam (Gentlemen Governors of the city of Amsterdam).

facts.text: A kink at Driekoningenstraat remains where the outer moat once routed around a local stronghold.
facts.sourceQuote: The Herengracht therefore still has a kink at Driekoningenstraat, where the outer moat was routed around a stronghold at that height.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Herengracht therefore still has a kink at Driekoningenstraat, where the outer moat was routed around a stronghold at that height.

facts.text: Regents and traders who earned fortunes in South America or the Dutch East Indies inhabited the Gouden Bocht.
facts.sourceQuote: This part contains the Gouden Bocht (Golden Bend), the most prestigious part of the Herengracht. Many of the houses were inhabited here by regents, mayors and traders who earned their fortunes in trade with South America or the Dutch East Indies.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This part contains the Gouden Bocht (Golden Bend), the most prestigious part of the Herengracht. Many of the houses were inhabited here by regents, mayors and traders who earned their fortunes in trade with South America or the Dutch East Indies.

facts.text: The Gouden Bocht section features large, beautiful canal houses.
facts.sourceQuote: The Gouden Bocht (Golden Bend) in particular is known for its large and beautiful canal houses.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Gouden Bocht (Golden Bend) in particular is known for its large and beautiful canal houses.

features.name: Snoekjesgracht

facts.text: The name Snoekjesgracht honors Jan Pieters Snoeck, who displayed a pike on his 1595 house facade.
facts.sourceQuote: The Snoekjesgracht, originally called Snoeksgracht, was named after a 16th-century resident, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a house built on this canal in 1595 and depicted a pike (fish) on the facade.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Snoekjesgracht, originally called Snoeksgracht, was named after a 16th-century resident, Jan Pieters Snoeck, who had a house built on this canal in 1595 and depicted a pike (fish) on the facade.

facts.text: East side buildings were demolished after the war and replaced with new structures in the 1980s.
facts.sourceQuote: After the war, many of the buildings on the east side were demolished and replaced by new buildings in the 1980s .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: After the war, many of the buildings on the east side were demolished and replaced by new buildings in the 1980s .

facts.text: Bridge number 289 crosses this waterway exactly where Snoekjessteeg meets the canal.
facts.sourceQuote: 289) crosses the Snoekjesgracht at the Snoekjessteeg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 289) crosses the Snoekjesgracht at the Snoekjessteeg.

features.opening: The Snoekjesgracht (Pike Canal) is a small canal in Amsterdam, in the Lastage neighborhood.

features.name: IJmeer

facts.text: The IJmeer serves as a vital habitat for tufted ducks and scaup.
facts.sourceQuote: It is an important habitat for birds such as the tufted duck and scaup.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is an important habitat for birds such as the tufted duck and scaup.

facts.text: The IJmeer connects to the Gooimeer via the Hollandse Brug to its southeast.
facts.sourceQuote: The IJmeer is bordered, and separated from the IJ, by the Oranje Locks to the east, a straight line extending from Uitdam to the Almere-Pampus to the northeast, and the Hollandse Brug to the southeast, where it connects with the Gooimeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The IJmeer is bordered, and separated from the IJ, by the Oranje Locks to the east, a straight line extending from Uitdam to the Almere-Pampus to the northeast, and the Hollandse Brug to the southeast, where it connects with the Gooimeer.

facts.text: Oranje Locks separate the IJmeer from the IJ on its eastern side.
facts.sourceQuote: The IJmeer is bordered, and separated from the IJ, by the Oranje Locks to the east, a straight line extending from Uitdam to the Almere-Pampus to the northeast, and the Hollandse Brug to the southeast, where it connects with the Gooimeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The IJmeer is bordered, and separated from the IJ, by the Oranje Locks to the east, a straight line extending from Uitdam to the Almere-Pampus to the northeast, and the Hollandse Brug to the southeast, where it connects with the Gooimeer.

facts.text: A straight line from Uitdam to Almere-Pampus marks the northeastern boundary of the IJmeer.
facts.sourceQuote: The IJmeer is bordered, and separated from the IJ, by the Oranje Locks to the east, a straight line extending from Uitdam to the Almere-Pampus to the northeast, and the Hollandse Brug to the southeast, where it connects with the Gooimeer.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The IJmeer is bordered, and separated from the IJ, by the Oranje Locks to the east, a straight line extending from Uitdam to the Almere-Pampus to the northeast, and the Hollandse Brug to the southeast, where it connects with the Gooimeer.

features.opening: The IJmeer is a 'bordering lake' (Randmeer) in the Netherlands straddling the provinces of North Holland and Flevoland.

features.name: Sloterplas

facts.text: Debris was poured in to reach a final depth of 38 meters after the pond was deepened by dozens of meters.
facts.sourceQuote: Door het storten van puin werd de uiteindelijke diepte 38 meter.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: By pouring in debris, the final depth was 38 meters.

facts.text: The Maschsee bastions in Hanover, excavated in 1935, served as an almost direct inspiration for this project.
facts.sourceQuote: Voor inspiratie reisden Van Eesteren en zijn collega's langs Engelse en Duitse parken en de bastions van de Maschsee in Hannover, die in 1935 uitgraven werd, zijn vrijwel gekopieerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: For inspiration, Van Eesteren and his colleagues traveled through English and German parks and the bastions of the Maschsee in Hanover, which were excavated in 1935, were almost copied.

facts.text: A recreational beach on the northwest bank received its official name, Sloterstrand, in May 2017.
facts.sourceQuote: Ten noorden van het zwembad ligt aan de noordwestoever een recreatiestrand, dat in mei 2017 'Sloterstrand' werd gedoopt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: North of the swimming pool, on the northwest bank, is a recreational beach, which was named 'Sloterstrand' in May 2017.

facts.text: The northern bank became a protected landscape on October 18, 2017.
facts.sourceQuote: Het noordelijk deel bij de noordoever van de Sloterplas werd op 18 oktober 2017 aangewezen als gemeentelijk beschermd stadsgezicht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The northern part near the northern bank of the Sloterplas was designated as a municipal protected urban landscape on October 18, 2017.

facts.text: Amsterdam expanded protection to the entire lake and banks in March 2024.
facts.sourceQuote: Naar aanleiding van een aanvraag van Heemschut heeft de gemeenteraad van Amsterdam op 28 maart 2024 de gehele Sloterplas en oevers aangewezen als gemeentelijk beschermd stadsgezicht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Following a request from Heemschut, the municipal council of Amsterdam designated the entire Sloterplas and banks as a municipal protected urban landscape on March 28, 2024.

features.opening: The Sloterplas is located in the center of the Western Garden Cities in Amsterdam Nieuw-West.

features.name: Duivendrechtsevaart

facts.text: The Duivendrechtsevaart takes its name from the nearby village of Duivendrecht.
facts.sourceQuote: De vaart is vernoemd naar het nabij gelegen dorp Duivendrecht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is named after the nearby village of Duivendrecht.

facts.text: A dam once allowed traffic to cross east to west until Van der Madeweg opened in 1963.
facts.sourceQuote: Tot de openstelling van de Van der Madeweg in 1963 bleef er ter hoogte van de Paul van Vlissingenstraat een dam aanwezig om het verkeer de mogelijkheid te geven van oost naar west te rijden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Until the opening of the Van der Madeweg in 1963, there was a dam at the level of Paul van Vlissingenstraat to give traffic the opportunity to drive east to west.

facts.text: Five bridges span the waterway, including a metro bridge built in 1990.
facts.sourceQuote: Er zijn vijf bruggen over de vaart waarvan de eerste twee in Amsterdam liggen (van noord naar zuid): voetgangers/fietsersbrug brug 1962, die een verbinding geeft tussen de Omval en de Jan Vroegopsingel. verkeersbrug Amstelstroomlaan brug 2189 uit 2022 verkeersbrug De Heusweg brug 854 uit 1968. metrobrug brug 1641 met metrostation Overamstel uit 1990. een ongenummerde brug in Rijksweg 10.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: There are five bridges over the canal, two of which are located in Amsterdam (from north to south): pedestrian/cyclist bridge bridge 1962, which provides a connection between the Omval and the Jan Vroegopsingel. traffic bridge Amstelstroomlaan bridge 2189 from 2022 traffic bridge De Heusweg bridge 854 from 1968. metro bridge bridge 1641 with metro station Overamstel from 1990. an unnumbered bridge in Rijksweg 10.

features.opening: The Duivendrechtsevaart is a canal in Amsterdam and Duivendrecht (Ouder-Amstel municipality).

features.name: Uilenburgergracht

facts.text: Three newly created islands including Uilenburg formed the poorest section of the Jewish quarter in the nineteenth century.
facts.sourceQuote: In the nineteenth century, the newly created islands of Uilenburg, Valkenburg and Marken were the poorest neighborhoods of the Jewish quarter.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the nineteenth century, the newly created islands of Uilenburg, Valkenburg and Marken were the poorest neighborhoods of the Jewish quarter.

features.opening: The Uilenburgergracht is a secondary canal in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.

features.name: Onbekendegracht

facts.text: In 1948 residents asked to rename the canal because they found it too confusing.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1948, residents of the Onbekendegracht asked the municipality of Amsterdam to change the name of the canal because they found it too confusing.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1948, residents of the Onbekendegracht asked the municipality of Amsterdam to change the name of the canal because they found it too confusing.

facts.text: Buildings numbered one through five were erected in 1906 under architect AJ Tymensen.
facts.sourceQuote: The buildings at Onbekendegracht 1–5, built in 1906 and designed by AJ Tymensen, became a monument in 2006.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The buildings at Onbekendegracht 1–5, built in 1906 and designed by AJ Tymensen, became a monument in 2006.

facts.text: The canal sits directly behind the Royal Theater Carré within the Weesperbuurt district.
facts.sourceQuote: The Onbekendegracht, which connects the Nieuwe Prinsengracht and the Nieuwe Achtergracht, is located directly behind the Royal Theater Carré in the Weesperbuurt.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Onbekendegracht, which connects the Nieuwe Prinsengracht and the Nieuwe Achtergracht, is located directly behind the Royal Theater Carré in the Weesperbuurt.

features.opening: The Onbekendegracht (Unknown Canal) is a short canal in Amsterdam, in the eastern part of the Grachtengordel (canal belt).

features.name: Ringvaart

facts.text: The Watergraafsmeer polder surrounding the Ringvaart was reclaimed in 1629.
facts.sourceQuote: De Ringvaart in Amsterdam-Oost is de naam van het noordelijk en oostelijk deel van de ringvaart rond de in 1629 drooggelegde Watergraafsmeer-polder.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Ringvaart in Amsterdam-Oost is the name of the northern and eastern part of the ring canal around the Watergraafsmeer polder, which was reclaimed in 1629.

facts.text: Street names along the inner dike include Linnaeuskade and Ooster Ringdijk.
facts.sourceQuote: De ringdijk, de dijk langs het kanaal aan de binnenkant, heeft de straatnamen Ringdijk, Linnaeuskade en Ooster Ringdijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The ringdijk, the dike along the canal on the inside, has the street names Ringdijk, Linnaeuskade and Ooster Ringdijk.

facts.text: A section of the ring road vanished in the 1980s to accommodate the A10 extension.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de oostkant is een klein deel van de ringvaart verdwenen in de jaren 80 voor de verlenging van het oostelijk deel van de Amsterdamse Ringweg (A10) naar de Zeeburgerbrug en voor het Knooppunt Watergraafsmeer, die beide in 1990 zijn gereed gekomen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the east side, a small part of the ring road disappeared in the 1980s for the extension of the eastern part of the Amsterdam Ring Road (A10) to the Zeeburgerbrug and for the Watergraafsmeer Junction, which both came into operation in 1990.

features.opening: The Ringvaart in Amsterdam-Oost is the name of the northern and eastern part of the ring canal around the Watergraafsmeer polder, which was reclaimed in 1629.

features.name: Reguliersgracht

facts.text: During WWII, the illegal newspaper Het Parool operated its nerve center from house number 111.
facts.sourceQuote: During World War II the "nerve center" of the illegal paper Het Parool was housed there, in a house (number 111) occupied by Simon Carmiggelt, Max Nord, Wim van Norden and their families.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: During World War II the "nerve center" of the illegal paper Het Parool was housed there, in a house (number 111) occupied by Simon Carmiggelt, Max Nord, Wim van Norden and their families.

features.opening: Reguliersgracht is a canal in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

features.name: Spiegelgracht

facts.text: The Spiegelgracht translates to mirror canal.
facts.sourceQuote: The Spiegelgracht (Dutch: [ˈspi.ɣəlɣrɑxt], mirror canal) is a canal in the centre of Amsterdam, located near the Prinsengracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Spiegelgracht (Dutch: [ˈspi.ɣəlɣrɑxt], mirror canal) is a canal in the centre of Amsterdam, located near the Prinsengracht.

facts.text: Construction of this waterway dates back to the sixteenth century.
facts.sourceQuote: Built in the 16th century, it is a part of the Canals of Amsterdam which have been designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Built in the 16th century, it is a part of the Canals of Amsterdam which have been designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

features.opening: The Spiegelgracht (Dutch: [ˈspi.ɣəlɣrɑxt], mirror canal) is a canal in the centre of Amsterdam, located near the Prinsengracht.

features.name: Kattenburgervaart

facts.text: The canal runs parallel to the Wittenburgervaart, positioned to its east from Nieuwe Vaart to Dijksgracht.
facts.sourceQuote: The Kattenburgervaart runs parallel to the Wittenburgervaart (to the east) from the Nieuwe Vaart to the Dijksgracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Kattenburgervaart runs parallel to the Wittenburgervaart (to the east) from the Nieuwe Vaart to the Dijksgracht.

facts.text: Wittenburg, one of the islands separated by this waterway, was constructed during the seventeenth century.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal separates the island of Wittenburg, which was built in the 17th century, from the island of Kattenburg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal separates the island of Wittenburg, which was built in the 17th century, from the island of Kattenburg.

facts.text: The Kippebrug has served cyclists as a fixed bridge since 1923.
facts.sourceQuote: Four bridges cross the canal: the Paerlduiker (bridge number 91) at the Nieuwe Vaart, between the Wittenburgergracht and Kattenburgergracht streets, which form part of the so-called Eilandboulevard. the Kippebrug (bridge number 270), a fixed bridge for cyclists from 1923 in the Wittenburgerkade. the Witte Katbrug (bridge number 1914), an arched bridge for pedestrians and cyclists in the Jacob Burggraafstraat. the Zebrabrug (bridge number 389), in the Derde Wittenburgerdwarsstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Four bridges cross the canal: the Paerlduiker (bridge number 91) at the Nieuwe Vaart, between the Wittenburgergracht and Kattenburgergracht streets, which form part of the so-called Eilandboulevard. the Kippebrug (bridge number 270), a fixed bridge for cyclists from 1923 in the Wittenburgerkade. the Witte Katbrug (bridge number 1914), an arched bridge for pedestrians and cyclists in the Jacob Burggraafstraat. the Zebrabrug (bridge number 389), in the Derde Wittenburgerdwarsstraat.

facts.text: Bridge number 1914 features an arched design for pedestrians and cyclists.
facts.sourceQuote: Four bridges cross the canal: the Paerlduiker (bridge number 91) at the Nieuwe Vaart, between the Wittenburgergracht and Kattenburgergracht streets, which form part of the so-called Eilandboulevard. the Kippebrug (bridge number 270), a fixed bridge for cyclists from 1923 in the Wittenburgerkade. the Witte Katbrug (bridge number 1914), an arched bridge for pedestrians and cyclists in the Jacob Burggraafstraat. the Zebrabrug (bridge number 389), in the Derde Wittenburgerdwarsstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Four bridges cross the canal: the Paerlduiker (bridge number 91) at the Nieuwe Vaart, between the Wittenburgergracht and Kattenburgergracht streets, which form part of the so-called Eilandboulevard. the Kippebrug (bridge number 270), a fixed bridge for cyclists from 1923 in the Wittenburgerkade. the Witte Katbrug (bridge number 1914), an arched bridge for pedestrians and cyclists in the Jacob Burggraafstraat. the Zebrabrug (bridge number 389), in the Derde Wittenburgerdwarsstraat.

facts.text: Two missing bridges numbered 268 and 269 once crossed the former Binnenhaven.
facts.sourceQuote: On the extension of the Kattenburgervaart, there were two bridges over the former Binnenhaven. The missing bridges are numbers 268 and 269, the last of which was also known as the Worm bridge .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the extension of the Kattenburgervaart, there were two bridges over the former Binnenhaven. The missing bridges are numbers 268 and 269, the last of which was also known as the Worm bridge .

features.opening: The Kattenburgervaart is a short canal in Amsterdam that runs through the Oostelijke Eilanden (Eastern Islands).

features.name: Oosterdok

facts.text: Prince Willem laid the first stone for the lock on June 11, 1830 before becoming King William III.
facts.sourceQuote: Foundation work for the lock started before the first stone was laid by on 11 June 1830 by Prince Willem, the later King William III.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Foundation work for the lock started before the first stone was laid by on 11 June 1830 by Prince Willem, the later King William III.

facts.text: The western dyke end, once called Oosterdam, was removed in the late 2010s to improve views.
facts.sourceQuote: The western end of this dyke was until recently called Oosterdam. It was removed in the late 2010s in order to improve the visual quality of the area.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The western end of this dyke was until recently called Oosterdam. It was removed in the late 2010s in order to improve the visual quality of the area.

facts.text: Construction of the Oosterdoksdam and Oosterdoksluis occurred between 1831 and 1832.
facts.sourceQuote: It was created in 1831–1832 by constructing the Oosterdoksdam and the Oosterdoksluis, forming a reliable deep port closed off from the tidal IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was created in 1831–1832 by constructing the Oosterdoksdam and the Oosterdoksluis, forming a reliable deep port closed off from the tidal IJ.

facts.text: Engineers closed off the tidal IJ to create a reliable deep port for ships.
facts.sourceQuote: It was created in 1831–1832 by constructing the Oosterdoksdam and the Oosterdoksluis, forming a reliable deep port closed off from the tidal IJ.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was created in 1831–1832 by constructing the Oosterdoksdam and the Oosterdoksluis, forming a reliable deep port closed off from the tidal IJ.

features.opening: The Oosterdok ('Eastern Dock') is a former wet dock in Amsterdam.

features.name: Oudezijds Achterburgwal

facts.text: The name Oudezijds Achterburgwal reflects its origin as the rear rampart built behind an earlier defensive wall.
facts.sourceQuote: When new ramparts were constructed behind these ramparts around 1385, the existing rampart became the Voorburgwal and the new rampart became the Achterburgwal, both on the old and the new side.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: When new ramparts were constructed behind these ramparts around 1385, the existing rampart became the Voorburgwal and the new rampart became the Achterburgwal, both on the old and the new side.

facts.text: A book market has been held along this canal for centuries.
facts.sourceQuote: A book market has been held in this for centuries .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A book market has been held in this for centuries .

facts.text: The Walloon Church was consecrated in 1496 after replacing a chapel destroyed in the 1452 town fire.
facts.sourceQuote: The Walloon Church, originally the chapel of the Paulusbroedersklooster. This chapel, consecrated in 1496, replaced an earlier chapel that was probably destroyed in the town fire of 1452.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Walloon Church, originally the chapel of the Paulusbroedersklooster. This chapel, consecrated in 1496, replaced an earlier chapel that was probably destroyed in the town fire of 1452.

facts.text: The Oudemanhuispoort complex now serves as a main location for the University of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: The Oudemanhuispoort complex is one of the main locations of the University of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Oudemanhuispoort complex is one of the main locations of the University of Amsterdam.

features.opening: The Oudezijds Achterburgwal, often abbreviated to OZ Achterburgwal, is a street and canal in De Wallen, the red light district in the center of Amsterdam.

features.name: Geldersekade

facts.text: A fish market replaced the one on Dam Square after 1840 to make room for the Beurs van Zocher.
facts.sourceQuote: A fish market was built after 1840 in the water of the Geldersekade, on the north side of the Nieuwmarkt. It replaced the fish market on Dam Square, which had to make way for the Beurs van Zocher.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A fish market was built after 1840 in the water of the Geldersekade, on the north side of the Nieuwmarkt. It replaced the fish market on Dam Square, which had to make way for the Beurs van Zocher.

facts.text: Wooden sheds were replaced by a stone building called the Gemeentelijke Vishal in 1862.
facts.sourceQuote: The scaffolding and wooden sheds were replaced in 1862 by the stone Gemeentelijke Vishal, which was demolished in 1938.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The scaffolding and wooden sheds were replaced in 1862 by the stone Gemeentelijke Vishal, which was demolished in 1938.

features.opening: The Geldersekade is a canal and a street in Amsterdam that connects the Nieuwmarkt with the Prins Hendrikkade.

features.name: Oudeschans

facts.text: The Oudeschans was originally named Nieuwe Gracht when an arm of the Amstel was dug out between 1515 and 1518.
facts.sourceQuote: Between 1515 and 1518 an armof the Amstel was dug out, the Zwanenburgwal, leading to the Nieuwe Gracht, as the Oudeschans was then called.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1515 and 1518 an armof the Amstel was dug out, the Zwanenburgwal, leading to the Nieuwe Gracht, as the Oudeschans was then called.

facts.text: In 1602 a channel cut through the Sint Antoniesdijk allowed ships to sail to the Amstel via the Zwanenburgwal.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1602 a channel was cut through the Sint Antoniesdijk on the south side of the Oudeschans, and the Sint Antoniesluis (a lock) was built so that ships could sail to the Amstel via the Zwanenburgwal.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1602 a channel was cut through the Sint Antoniesdijk on the south side of the Oudeschans, and the Sint Antoniesluis (a lock) was built so that ships could sail to the Amstel via the Zwanenburgwal.

facts.text: Jan Hendrik Mulder Jr. designed a block of 72 homes built on the Oudeschans in 1927.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1927 the municipality built a block of 72 homes in the style of the late Amsterdam School in collaboration with the Bouwfonds Handwerkers Vriendenkring. The block was designed by Jan Hendrik Mulder Jr. (1888–1960) and built on the Oudeschans / Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1927 the municipality built a block of 72 homes in the style of the late Amsterdam School in collaboration with the Bouwfonds Handwerkers Vriendenkring. The block was designed by Jan Hendrik Mulder Jr. (1888–1960) and built on the Oudeschans / Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat.

facts.text: Jan Swammerdam lived at Oudeschans 18, where his father ran a pharmacy with a natural history collection.
facts.sourceQuote: Jan Swammerdam lived at Oudeschans 18, where his father, who was known for his natural history collection, had a pharmacy .
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Jan Swammerdam lived at Oudeschans 18, where his father, who was known for his natural history collection, had a pharmacy .

facts.text: Painter Willem Witsen rented the studio at Oudeschans 5 from 1887 to 1888 after George Hendrik Breitner used it.
facts.sourceQuote: Between 1887 and 1888, the painter Willem Witsen rented the studio in Oudeschans 5 formerly used by George Hendrik Breitner.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1887 and 1888, the painter Willem Witsen rented the studio in Oudeschans 5 formerly used by George Hendrik Breitner.

features.opening: The Oudeschans, or Oude Schans (Old Rampart), originally the Nieuwe Gracht, is a wide canal in the eastern part of the inner city of Amsterdam.

features.name: Rapenburgwal

facts.text: A 1737 map shows the canal once extended east to Markengracht before that section was filled in 1968.
facts.sourceQuote: A 1737 map shows that the canal once ran further east to the Markengracht, which was back-filled in 1968 during construction of the IJtunnel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A 1737 map shows that the canal once ran further east to the Markengracht, which was back-filled in 1968 during construction of the IJtunnel.

facts.text: Bridge 281, known as Peperbrug, crosses the center of this waterway connecting two distinct islands.
facts.sourceQuote: It is crossed in its center section by Bridge 281, Peperbrug, which connects Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat on Uilenburg island to Peperstraat on Marken (Valkenburg) island.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is crossed in its center section by Bridge 281, Peperbrug, which connects Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat on Uilenburg island to Peperstraat on Marken (Valkenburg) island.

facts.text: The eastern portion of Rapenburgwal disappeared in 1968 during the construction of the IJtunnel.
facts.sourceQuote: A 1737 map shows that the canal once ran further east to the Markengracht, which was back-filled in 1968 during construction of the IJtunnel.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A 1737 map shows that the canal once ran further east to the Markengracht, which was back-filled in 1968 during construction of the IJtunnel.

features.opening: The Rapenburgwal (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈraːpə(m)ˌbʏr(ə)xʋɑl]) is a canal in Amsterdam in the east of the Amsterdam-Centrum district, in the Lastage…

features.name: Nieuwe Meer

facts.text: A motorboat ferry named Helena connects the north and south banks every Sunday from April to October.
facts.sourceQuote: Op zondagen tussen april en oktober is er een veerverbinding met motorschip 'Helena' tussen de noord- en zuidoever.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On Sundays between April and October there is a ferry connection with motorboat 'Helena' between the north and south banks.

facts.text: The dredged sand was specifically used to elevate Amsterdam's Western Garden Cities.
facts.sourceQuote: Het gewonnen zand werd gebruikt voor de ophoging van de Westelijke Tuinsteden van Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The sand dredged was used for the elevation of the Western Garden Cities of Amsterdam.

facts.text: The village of Nieuwe Meer and traffic junction De Nieuwe Meer are named after this lake.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de overkant van de Ringvaart, tegenover de Nieuwe Meer, ligt de buurtschap Nieuwe Meer. Deze buurtschap en het verkeersknooppunt De Nieuwe Meer in de A4 en A10, zijn naar het meer genoemd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: On the other side of the Ringvaart, opposite the Nieuwe Meer, lies the village of Nieuwe Meer. This neighborhood and the traffic junction De Nieuwe Meer on the A4 and A10 are named after the lake.

features.opening: The Nieuwe Meer (or 'the' Nieuwe Meer) is a narrow lake southwest of Amsterdam.

features.name: Schinkel

facts.text: A dam blocked the Schinkel in 1434 to stop shipping, forcing vessels via Spaarndam.
facts.sourceQuote: Op last van de Graaf van Holland, werd echter in 1434 al een dam in de Schinkel gemaakt, zodat er geen scheepvaart plaats kon vinden. Schepen moesten, volgens de door graaf verleende rechten, de voorgeschreven route via Spaarndam volgen om bij het IJ te komen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: However, at the request of the Count of Holland, a dam was already built in the Schinkel in 1434, so that no shipping could take place. According to the rights granted by the count, ships had to follow the prescribed route via Spaarndam to reach the IJ.

facts.text: An overtoom drawbridge allowed only small ships to be pulled across the dam in 1515.
facts.sourceQuote: Over deze dam werd in 1515 een overhaal of overtoom gemaakt, waar alleen kleine schepen overheen getrokken mochten worden.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1515, a drawbridge or overtoom was built over this dam, where only small ships were allowed to be pulled over it.

facts.text: The river once hosted a wooden outdoor swimming pool called Schinkelbad.
facts.sourceQuote: In de eerste helft van de twintigste eeuw lag hier in de rivier het Schinkelbad, een houten buitenzwembad.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the first half of the twentieth century, the Schinkelbad, a wooden outdoor swimming pool, was located here in the river.

facts.text: The Overtoomse Lock was replaced by the Schinkelsluis on July 1, 1942.
facts.sourceQuote: De Overtoomse Sluis werd op 1 juli 1942 vervangen door de Schinkelsluis bij de Nieuwe Meer, waarna de Schinkel ten noorden van deze sluis tot het stadswater ging behoren.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Overtoomse Lock was replaced on July 1, 1942 by the Schinkelsluis near the Nieuwe Meer, after which the Schinkel became part of the city water north of this lock.

facts.text: Unlike city canals, the Schinkel still actively transports goods by water.
facts.sourceQuote: De Schinkel wordt nog steeds gebruikt voor goederenvervoer over het water, een functie die de stadsgrachten verloren hebben.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Schinkel is still used for goods transport over the water, a function that the city canals have lost.

facts.text: Since 1958, a statue of Jan Meefout has stood on the bank near the Ice Skating Path.
facts.sourceQuote: Op de oever ter hoogte van het IJsbaanpad staat sinds 1958 een beeld van Jan Meefout.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Since 1958, a statue of Jan Meefout has stood on the bank near the Ice Skating Path.

features.opening: The Schinkel is a small canalized river in Amsterdam, in the Dutch province of North Holland.

features.name: Minervahaven

facts.text: In May 1941, two English deserters and others fled to England using a seaplane moored here.
facts.sourceQuote: In mei 1941 vluchtten Jan Beelaerts van Blokland, Govert Steen en nog twee Engelandvaarders naar Engeland met een Fokker T.VIIIw watervliegtuig dat in de Minervahaven lag afgemeerd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In May 1941, Jan Beelaerts van Blokland, Govert Steen and two more English deserters fled to England with an Fokker T.VIII seaplane that was moored in the Minervahaven.

features.opening: The Minervahaven is a harbor basin in the port of Amsterdam.

features.name: Leidsegracht

facts.text: From 1615 until 1658, this waterway served as the southern boundary of Amsterdam.
facts.sourceQuote: Between 1615 and 1658, the Leidsegracht was the southern boundary of the city.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Between 1615 and 1658, the Leidsegracht was the southern boundary of the city.

facts.text: Hydraulic engineer Cornelis Lely was born at number 39 on this street.
facts.sourceQuote: Cornelis Lely (1854–1929), the hydraulic engineer, governor and minister who made the original plans for the reclamation of the Zuiderzee, was born on Leidsegracht no. 39.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Cornelis Lely (1854–1929), the hydraulic engineer, governor and minister who made the original plans for the reclamation of the Zuiderzee, was born on Leidsegracht no. 39.

facts.text: Pieter Goemans wrote his classic song Aan de Amsterdamse grachten while crossing a bridge here in 1949.
facts.sourceQuote: Pieter Goemans was inspired to write the classic song Aan de Amsterdamse grachten (On the Amsterdam canals) in 1949 while walking across the bridge where the Prinsengracht and the Leidsegracht intersect.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Pieter Goemans was inspired to write the classic song Aan de Amsterdamse grachten (On the Amsterdam canals) in 1949 while walking across the bridge where the Prinsengracht and the Leidsegracht intersect.

facts.text: Leidsegracht connects Herengracht, Keizersgracht, Prinsengracht and Lijnbaansgracht.
facts.sourceQuote: It is a cross-canal in Amsterdam-Center that connects Herengracht, Keizersgracht, Prinsengracht and Lijnbaansgracht and flows into the Singelgracht at Marnixstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is a cross-canal in Amsterdam-Center that connects Herengracht, Keizersgracht, Prinsengracht and Lijnbaansgracht and flows into the Singelgracht at Marnixstraat.

features.opening: The Leidsegracht (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈlɛitsəˌɣrɑxt]) is a canal in Amsterdam, Netherlands.

features.name: Zoutkeetsgracht

facts.text: Zoutkeetsgracht means salt-kiln canal, named for the salt factories that once lined its banks.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal is named after the salt factories that stood on both sides of the canal in the 17th and 18th centuries.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal is named after the salt factories that stood on both sides of the canal in the 17th and 18th centuries.

facts.text: A flour and bread factory called Holland operated here before new homes replaced it.
facts.sourceQuote: The flour and bread factory "Holland" was also there for some time, but after the demolition of the factory new homes were built on the site.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The flour and bread factory "Holland" was also there for some time, but after the demolition of the factory new homes were built on the site.

facts.text: Coarse salt was processed in sheds along this waterway to make it suitable for domestic use.
facts.sourceQuote: These were sheds along the canal where the coarse salt was processed and made suitable for domestic use.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: These were sheds along the canal where the coarse salt was processed and made suitable for domestic use.

facts.text: Smallepadsgracht flows into Zoutkeetsgracht from the south just before reaching Zoutkeetsbrug.
facts.sourceQuote: Smallepadsgracht enters Zoutkeetsgracht from the south just before Zoutkeetsbrug.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Smallepadsgracht enters Zoutkeetsgracht from the south just before Zoutkeetsbrug.

features.opening: The Zoutkeetsgracht (Salt sheds canal) is a canal to the west of the center of Amsterdam.
